title: Dashboard beads poll piles up a bd process every 15s under contention
description:
The admin TUI polls beads with `bd list --json -n 0 --no-pager` every 15 seconds. Each poll is spawned without a timeout and without regard for whether the previous one returned. When the embedded Dolt database is busy — beads defaults to embedded Dolt, which serves one writer at a time — every poll blocks instead of exiting, and they accumulate.

Observed 2026-09-01 04:47 UTC (12:47am ET) on this machine: 38 wedged `bd list --json -n 0 --no-pager` processes stacked up over 9.5 minutes, one every 15s, all parented to a single admin TUI (pid 12178, started 00:37:56 ET). Two dolt sql-server processes were up.

In that state every other bd caller hung too. Three `bd close`/`bd show` invocations from a separate session timed out at 120s and were killed without ever writing, and another session's `bd update admin-l6kb.1 --description ...` sat wedged for 6 minutes. Recovery required killing the TUI, every bd process, and both dolt servers.

The cost is not the idle processes — it is that one open dashboard makes the tracker unwritable for every other session on the machine, with no error, just hangs.

The condition the design permits is a fixed-interval poll with no timeout and no in-flight guard. Skipping a tick while one is outstanding, or putting a timeout on each poll, removes that condition; a longer interval only slows the pileup down.
acceptance_criteria: A slow or contended bd never accumulates more than one in-flight poll process. A poll exceeding its timeout is abandoned and shown as a stale indicator rather than hanging. Killing the dashboard is never required to make the tracker writable again.

title: Not every command writes a log file: Go made log creation opt-in per step
description:
## Category

bug

## Summary

Not every command writes a log file any more. In the Python implementation a log path was materialized on demand for any command; in Go a log only exists when a step body explicitly calls `set_log_context(name)`.

## Current behavior

The convention is `<repoRoot>/tmp/<stem>.<timestamp>.log` — `internal/luahost/host.go`'s `LogDir` default. `tmp/` is gitignored per repo.

`internal/tui/work.go:239-263` (`commandLogPath`) does not know a command's log path. It globs `<repoRoot>/tmp/<step>.*.log` for each of the command's step names and takes the newest match by mtime. Its own doc comment states the gap:

> a step whose body never calls set_log_context(name) under its own action name simply has nothing to find, and degrades to "none yet".

So the log path shown in the Work tab detail pane is a filesystem guess, and for any command whose steps never set a log context there is no file to guess at.

The Python entry point did not work this way. `admin_lib/core.py:214` `get_log_file()`:

> Asking for the path is a use, so it settles a pending name (see `_materialize_log_context`) — a caller that got a path and then found the log somewhere else would be worse than announcing slightly early.

Materialization was automatic and lazy: any caller asking for the path got one, and the file was created under the standard name. Go dropped that, so log-file creation became opt-in per step body rather than a property of running a command.

## Why it matters

The log file is the whole recovery path for a framed or hosted command — the pinned footer exists to show it, `admin logs` reads it back, and the Work tab detail pane points at it. A command with no log file has none of that, and nothing announces the absence: the detail pane just says "none yet", which is indistinguishable from "has not run yet".

## Desired behavior

Running any command produces a log file at the standard path, without the step body opting in. Asking for the path materializes it, as the Python did.

The Work tab reads the path it was given rather than globbing for it, so the displayed path is the file actually being written.

## Key interfaces

- `internal/luahost` — the log-context materializer that Go is missing the equivalent of.
- `internal/tui/work.go:246` `commandLogPath` — replaced by reading the real path rather than a glob over `tmp/`.
- The live-work entry, which is where a running command's real log path should be carried.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Running a command whose steps never call `set_log_context` still produces a log file at `<repoRoot>/tmp/<stem>.<timestamp>.log`.
- [ ] The path asked for and the path written to are the same file, asserted by running a command and stat-ing the announced path.
- [ ] The Work tab detail pane shows the path from the running command rather than a glob result, asserted with two commands whose step names collide on the glob.
- [ ] `tmp/` remains gitignored; no log file is ever created outside it without explicit `[logging] dir` config.
- [ ] A command that has genuinely never run still reads as "none yet" and is distinguishable from one that ran and wrote nothing.

## Out of scope

- Changing the log filename convention itself.
- Log retention or rotation.
- The `[logging]` config overrides, which are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Running a command whose steps never call set_log_context still produces a log file at <repoRoot>/tmp/<stem>.<timestamp>.log. The path asked for and the path written are the same file. The Work tab detail pane shows the running command's real path, not a glob result. tmp/ stays gitignored. A never-run command still reads as 'none yet' and is distinguishable from one that ran and wrote nothing.

title: Audit the Go port's 'not ported' notes for silently-ignored manifest keys
description:
## Category

bug

## Summary

Audit every "not ported" / "minus the X" note in the Go port and confirm each is either tracked or harmless — one of them was a silent, user-facing bug.

## Current behavior

The Python-to-Go port left a number of factories and helpers with doc comments saying a piece was deliberately left out. Some name a ticket. Several do not, and say so — "no ticket claims it yet", "tracked as a follow-up".

At least one of those was not a harmless gap. `kind="shell-passthrough"` dropped its `interactive` knob, and its own comment called that a follow-up nobody had filed. The consequence: `interactive = true` in a manifest parsed, resolved, passed `admin check`, and did nothing. Every such action ran through the captured path instead, and a captured child gets no controlling terminal — so a full-screen program received no window size, failed every isatty probe, and rendered a small monochrome fake of itself. Nothing errored. Nothing warned. `admin check` cannot see it, because the manifest is valid; the key is simply read by nobody.

That is the shape of the risk: a manifest key that validates and is then ignored is indistinguishable, from the outside, from a key that works.

## Desired behavior

Each of these notes has been examined once and resolved into one of three states:

- **Tracked** — a ticket exists and the note names it.
- **Harmless** — the omitted piece has no manifest-visible surface, so no project can ask for it. The note says why.
- **A bug** — a manifest key, or documented behaviour, is accepted and ignored. Filed, and the note names the new ticket.

The audit's real output is the third category. A key a manifest can set and the tool silently drops is the class this exists to find.

Known starting points, none of which name a ticket:

- `makeShell` — the watch-kind piece.
- The Docker factory's nil field.
- The Apple signing helper's unported expansion.
- The vite dev-loop's process sweep.
- The Apple device console/attached-stdout mode.

## Key interfaces

- The action-kind factories and the manifest keys each one reads.
- The schema validator, which is what decides whether an unread key is reported.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every "not ported" / "minus the X" / "no ticket claims it" note in the Go source is listed with its file and its resolution.
- [ ] Each is classified tracked / harmless / bug, with the reason recorded in the note itself.
- [ ] Every key a manifest can set that no factory reads is identified.
- [ ] Anything found in the bug class is filed with its own reproduction.
- [ ] A note left in place names its ticket, so the next reader does not have to repeat the audit.

## Out of scope

- Implementing the missing pieces. This audit finds and classifies them.
- The Python interpreter, which is being deleted wholesale.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Every not-ported note in the Go source is listed with file and resolution. Each is classified tracked/harmless/bug with the reason recorded in the note. Every manifest-settable key that no factory reads is identified. Anything in the bug class is filed with a reproduction. A note left in place names its ticket.

title: Dashboard runs commands on a hosted pty and stays up
description:
## Parent

admin-3rgp

## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Dispatch a dashboard-selected Command onto a pseudo-terminal the dashboard owns, so the dashboard keeps rendering while it runs.

## Current behavior

Activating a command row hands the entire terminal to the dispatched Command for the whole run. The dashboard's alt-screen is released before the run and restored after, because a dispatched runner writes to the real terminal — its output, and the pinned footer's scroll region, would corrupt the dashboard's own rendering if they ran concurrently with it.

The consequence is that picking any Command blanks the dashboard until that Command exits. For a transient Command such as a build, that is the entire build. The user loses the command list, the branch view and every other tab, and a Command that prompts drops them into a bare prompt on an otherwise empty screen.

## Desired behavior

Activating a command row allocates a pseudo-terminal, dispatches the Command through the hosted entry point onto it, registers a live-work entry addressing that pty, and returns immediately. The dashboard never releases the terminal and keeps rendering throughout.

The Command's output goes to its log file exactly as it does today — same path, same timestamping, same ANSI stripping. The pinned footer behaves exactly as it does today too: the frame writes its scroll region and footer into the pty, because from the child's point of view the pty is its terminal. No second footer implementation is introduced.

The pty is sized so the child's own cursor positioning is correct for the region it will eventually be rendered in.

Activating a command row that already has a live entry attaches to it rather than starting a second run on top of the one that owns its log file, matching the behavior already in place for pane-backed entries.

## Key interfaces

- The dashboard's command-activation path stops using the terminal-release mechanism and becomes an ordinary asynchronous command.
- It calls the hosted command-runner entry point rather than the existing one.
- It registers a live-work entry addressing the pty, keyed on the Action name, with kill and retry operations supplied.
- Log-file selection, the frame's activation rules, and the footer's URL resolution are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting a Command in the dashboard leaves the dashboard rendered; the command list stays on screen for the whole run.
- [ ] The Command's log file is written at the same path and in the same format as a plain-CLI run of the same Command.
- [ ] A Command declaring `urls` or `footer` still produces its pinned footer, written into the pty.
- [ ] A Command whose Step declares a long-running Kind does not open a Herdr pane when dispatched from the dashboard, even with Herdr available.
- [ ] A live-work entry exists while the Command runs and reports exited when it finishes.
- [ ] Activating a command row that already has a live entry attaches instead of starting a second run.
- [ ] Asserted through the dashboard's headless frame renderer: a frame taken during a run shows the dashboard, not a released terminal.

## Out of scope

- Rendering the pty's contents. Reading the output back is the terminal-view slice; this slice's demo is the surviving dashboard plus the log file.
- The richer per-row live-status line. Uses the existing live-row treatment.
- Kill, retry, and quit behavior. Separate slices.

## Blocked by

The hosted dispatch entry point, and the registry's pty address.

## Pty allocation — decided, do not re-derive

Use `github.com/creack/pty`, pinned at `v1.1.24`, added as a direct dependency in `go.mod`. Recorded in `docs/adr/0015-pty-allocation-uses-creack-pty.md`.

Two operations only:

- `pty.Start(cmd)` — run the child on a new pty.
- `pty.Setsize(f, ws)` — size that pty to the region the dashboard will render it in. Feed it from `internal/frame`'s existing winsize helper rather than computing a second one.

Rejected, so it is not reopened:

- Hand-rolling `posix_openpt`/`grantpt`/`unlockpt` on `golang.org/x/sys/unix`. It is already a direct dependency but exposes no `Openpt` symbol, so it would mean hand-written ioctls per platform (darwin `TIOCPTYGRANT`/`TIOCPTYUNLK`/`TIOCPTYGNAME`, linux `TIOCGPTN`/`TIOCSPTLCK`) plus our own `Setsize`.

Two things that are NOT blockers, both already settled:

- **ADR-0001 "stdlib only" does not apply.** It governs the Python generator and the generated `./admin` script. The Go binary already carries 13 direct dependencies including bubbletea, lipgloss, cobra and gopher-lua.
- **Windows is not a target.** ADR-0012 rules it out, so creack/pty's darwin+linux coverage is every platform in `internal/platform.Supported`. Do not write a Windows stub or a ConPTY path.

## What is already in place

- `internal/kinds/dispatch.go:342` — `RunCommandHosted` exists and never reaches pane dispatch.
- `internal/livework` — `PTYID`, `Attach`, `SetTerminalOpener`, landed by admin-3rgp.60.
- `internal/kinds` — `Factory` now takes an explicit `*Surface`, landed by admin-3rgp.69, so two hosted commands overlapping in one process no longer clobber each other's nested dispatch.

The remaining work is: thread a writer through `RunCommandHosted`'s step loop so `luahost.Host.Stdout` — and therefore the frame footer — lands on the pty instead of `os.Stdout`, size via the frame's winsize helper, and wire `Ops.Kill` / `Ops.Retry` on the registered entry.
design:
Diagnosed 2026-08-31. The Verify FAIL (child at 0% CPU forever, row stuck `running`) is two defects, one masking the other.

CAUSE A — nothing reads the pty master. StartHostedPTY allocates ptmx, sizes it, stores ptmx.Name() on the livework entry, and never reads it; grepping every PTYID consumer finds livework.go storing it and hostedpty.go writing it, and no reader anywhere. On macOS a pty's output queue only drains when the master reads, and the child's exit-time tty close waits for that drain — so the child completes every step and then blocks in the kernel at exit. Measured with `admin __run-command greet` (`echo hi`): no drain -> alive at 25s, ps state Ss+ (not a zombie); drain from start -> exits in 5.03s; drain starting at 8s -> all 66 bytes arrive at once and the child exits at 8.00s, within milliseconds of the first read. The bytes contain `say complete`, so the work was already done. Not the parent failing to close its fd (it must stay open) and not a full buffer (66 bytes).

CAUSE B — a 5s stall on every dispatch, hidden behind A. The child's first write is `\x1b]11;?\x1b\\\x1b[6n`: lipgloss/termenv probing the terminal's background colour, because the child's stdout is a real TTY for the first time. It waits 5s for a reply the dashboard never sends. TERM=dumb or CI=1 in the child's env drops a drained run from 5.26s to 0.23s; NO_COLOR=1 does not.

DECIDED APPROACH (1A/2A, picked 2026-08-31, not yet implemented):

1A. StartHostedPTY starts a reader goroutine copying ptmx into a bounded ring buffer owned by the livework entry, and the terminal view in .62/.63 renders that buffer. Chosen over an io.Discard drain because it makes draining and displaying the same mechanism, so a later view cannot be added and forget to read; .61's own acceptance needs the output addressable anyway. Cost: .61 defines the buffer shape that .62-.66 inherit.

2A. Fix Cause B inside .61 by setting the child's colour profile explicitly from the parent rather than letting it interrogate a terminal that cannot answer. Chosen over filing it separately because it is the same defect as A -- the child assuming a responder that does not exist -- and a 5s first-line delay reads as the same hang that failed Verify.

Regression seam: assert the livework entry reaches StateExited within a timeout after StartHostedPTY. The throwaway probe used for the diagnosis (internal/kinds/hptyprobe_test.go on branch hosted-pty-dispatch) is deleted; the real test replaces it.

Base: branch hosted-pty-dispatch, commit 2ce8bfe, unmerged.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a Command leaves the dashboard rendered for the whole run. The log file is written at the same path and format as a plain-CLI run. A Command declaring urls or footer still produces its pinned footer, written into the pty. A long-running Kind dispatched from the dashboard opens no Herdr pane even with Herdr available. A live-work entry exists during the run and reports exited when it finishes. Activating a row with a live entry attaches instead of starting a second run. Asserted through the headless frame renderer: a frame taken during a run shows the dashboard, not a released terminal.
close_reason: Landed as c84335e (merge of hosted-pty-drain, fix commit eb1bc7c). Drains the pty master into a bounded livework.Ring before c.Wait() (Cause A) and preseeds the child color profile via HostedColorProfileEnv/HostedDarkBackgroundEnv (Cause B). Verdict PASS with a discriminating mutation check; go build and full go test clean on the merged result; pytest exit 0.

comments.author: pierce
comments.text:
Halted at the /orchestrate dispatch gate on 2026-08-31, round 2. Not dispatched again until the pty allocation mechanism is chosen.

The worker's finding is real: this ticket is where OS-level pty allocation would first have to happen, and nothing in the repo provides it. go.mod has no pty library, and a repo-wide grep for openpty/ptmx/unlockpt/grantpt/TIOCPTYGNAME finds only prose in docs/spikes/admin-tui-desktop, no allocation code. Go's standard library has no pty support.

Two of the worker's three premises are wrong, and the decision is narrower than it reported:

- It cited CLAUDE.md "stdlib only" as forbidding a dependency. That principle is ADR-0001, which governs the Python generator and the generated ./admin script. It says nothing about Go, and the Go binary already carries 13 direct dependencies including bubbletea, lipgloss, cobra and gopher-lua.
- It cited a missing Windows/ConPTY story. ADR-0012 (accepted 2026-08-31) states supported platforms are darwin and linux, and Windows is not a target. winsize_windows.go is a build stub, not a commitment.

So the live choice is only: github.com/creack/pty v1.1.24 (tagged, the de-facto Go pty library) versus hand-rolling posix_openpt/grantpt/unlockpt via golang.org/x/sys/unix, which is already a direct dependency but exposes no Openpt symbol, so the ioctls would be hand-written per platform.

Everything downstream is already concrete and unblocked once the mechanism is picked: thread a writer through RunCommandHosted's step loop so luahost.Host.Stdout and the frame footer land on the pty rather than os.Stdout, size via frame.ApplyWinsize, wire Ops.Kill/Retry. internal/kinds/dispatch.go:342 RunCommandHosted already exists and never reaches pane dispatch; internal/livework already has PTYID/Attach/SetTerminalOpener from admin-3rgp.60.

comments.author: pierce
comments.text:
Resolved 2026-08-31. Pty allocation uses github.com/creack/pty pinned at v1.1.24, added as a direct dependency. Recorded in docs/adr/0015-pty-allocation-uses-creack-pty.md.

Two operations only: pty.Start to run the child on a new pty, pty.Setsize to size it to the region the dashboard renders it in.

Rejected: hand-rolling posix_openpt/grantpt/unlockpt on golang.org/x/sys/unix. It is already a direct dependency, but exposes no Openpt symbol, so it would mean hand-written ioctls per platform (darwin TIOCPTYGRANT/TIOCPTYUNLK/TIOCPTYGNAME, linux TIOCGPTN/TIOCSPTLCK) plus our own Setsize — two implementations to save one go.mod line.

The two premises that caused the earlier halt are both settled in the ADR: ADR-0001's stdlib-only governs the Python generator, not Go (which already has 13 direct deps), and ADR-0012 rules Windows out, so darwin+linux is complete coverage rather than a partial port.

Back to afk. Everything downstream was already concrete: thread a writer through RunCommandHosted's step loop so luahost.Host.Stdout and the frame footer land on the pty instead of os.Stdout, size via frame.ApplyWinsize, wire Ops.Kill/Retry.

comments.author: pierce
comments.text:
Round 3 (2026-08-31) FAILED at Verify. Not dispatched again until the hang is diagnosed.

The pty allocation decision (creack/pty, ADR-0015) was correct and unblocked the pass — the worker got as far as a hostedpty.go with pty.Start. It failed on behaviour, not design:

A command dispatched from the dashboard onto the hosted pty never finishes by itself. The child spawned via StartHostedPTY's pty.Start re-exec of __run-command hangs indefinitely at 0% CPU and the Work-tab row stays "running" forever, recoverable only by killing it manually. Reproduced with multiple trivial commands (echo hi; echo/sleep/echo) across independent tmux sessions, with sandbox both on and off.

0% CPU with no progress points at a blocked read or write rather than a busy loop — the usual candidates being the parent never closing its side of the pty, or nothing draining the pty while the child fills the buffer.

WIP is preserved on branch hosted-pty-dispatch, commit 2ce8bfe "wip(kinds): hosted-pty dispatch kind, halted at Verify (FAIL)". The worktree is retired; the branch is deliberately kept so the next attempt starts from the diagnosis rather than a blank sheet. FAIL verdict at /private/tmp/claude/Projects-admin-project-tool/verify/admin-3rgp.61.json.

Next step is a diagnose pass on the hang, not a re-dispatch of the same brief.

title: Live-work registry addresses a pty as well as a pane
description:
## Parent

admin-3rgp

## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Let a live-work entry address a hosted pseudo-terminal as well as a Herdr pane, and resolve attach by whichever it carries.

## Current behavior

A live-work entry addresses exactly one thing: a Herdr pane. Its attach operation means "focus that pane". Every producer that registers an entry — the long-running Kind dispatch and the workflow agent dispatch — opens a pane first and records its identifier.

There is no way to register something the dashboard is hosting itself, because there is no pane to point at.

## Desired behavior

An entry carries either a pane address or a pseudo-terminal address, never both and never neither. The producer decides which at registration.

Attach resolves by whichever address is present: a pane-addressed entry focuses its pane, a pty-addressed entry opens the dashboard's terminal view over that pty. Kill and retry keep their existing meanings for both — kill stops the underlying thing and marks the entry exited; retry re-dispatches under the same entry identity, replacing the entry in place rather than adding a second row beside a stale one.

Entry identity stays keyed on the Action name, unchanged. That is already the grain of the registry lookup and of the per-Action log file, and a retry that opens a different pane or a different pty must keep the same identity so the Work tab's cursor stays on the same row.

An entry registered with neither address, or with both, is a programming error the registry rejects rather than storing.

## Key interfaces

- The entry type gains a pseudo-terminal address beside its existing pane address.
- The registry's add path rejects an entry carrying zero or two addresses.
- The attach operation dispatches on which address is set.
- Kill and retry signatures are unchanged.
- The worker-info pointer, which distinguishes an agent worker from a process, is unrelated to this and unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An entry carrying a pane address resolves attach to pane focus.
- [ ] An entry carrying a pty address resolves attach to the terminal view.
- [ ] Registering an entry with both addresses set is rejected.
- [ ] Registering an entry with neither address set is rejected.
- [ ] A retry on a pty-addressed entry replaces it in place under the same identity, leaving exactly one row.
- [ ] A retry on a pane-addressed entry behaves exactly as it does today.
- [ ] Every assertion above is verifiable at the registry's own exported surface, with no dashboard involved.

## Out of scope

- Implementing the terminal view itself. This slice only routes attach to it; the view is a separate slice.
- Persisting entries across process restarts. The registry stays in-memory and process-scoped, as its current contract states.
- Any change to how agent-worker entries are registered.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
acceptance_criteria: A pane-addressed entry resolves attach to pane focus. A pty-addressed entry resolves attach to the terminal view. Registering an entry with both addresses is rejected. Registering with neither is rejected. Retry on a pty entry replaces it in place under the same identity, leaving one row. Retry on a pane entry is unchanged. Every assertion verifiable at the registry's exported surface with no dashboard involved.
close_reason: Entry addresses a pane or a pty, never both and never neither; attach resolves by whichever is set. Merged as a16b935 (commit 1543c2a), verdict PASS with a discriminating mutation check.

title: Hosted dispatch entry point that cannot open a pane
description:
## Parent

admin-3rgp

## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Add a second command-dispatch entry point that runs Steps inline and from which pane dispatch is structurally unreachable.

## Current behavior

There is one exported command runner. It runs a Command's Steps through the lifetime-aware Action router, which opens a Herdr pane for any Action whose Kind is marked long-running when Herdr is available, and otherwise falls through to the inline Action runner.

That is correct for the CLI. It is wrong for the dashboard, which must never open a pane for a manifest Command — a dashboard-dispatched Action is hosted by the dashboard itself.

## Desired behavior

Two entry points over one shared step-loop body:

- The existing one keeps its exact current behavior: Steps go through the lifetime-aware router, long-running Kinds open panes when Herdr is available.
- A new hosted entry point runs each Step through the inline Action runner directly. The lifetime-aware router is not on its call graph at all, so no pane can be opened from it regardless of Kind or Herdr availability.

The shared body owns everything neither entry point should duplicate: the always-on global preflight, the pure-routing check that rejects a Command carrying action-only keys, the empty-steps check, declared-order execution, stop-at-first-failure, and the error wrapping that names the Command. Only the per-Step dispatch call differs between them.

An Action's Lifetime consequently narrows to one meaning: whether a plain-CLI dispatch opens a pane. Nothing else reads it.

## Key interfaces

- A new exported command-runner entry point alongside the existing one, taking the same resolved manifest, registry, command name and args, plus whatever the caller needs to host the run.
- An unexported shared step-loop taking the per-Step dispatch function as a parameter; both entry points call it.
- The existing command runner's exported signature and behavior are unchanged.
- The lifetime-aware Action router is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With Herdr available and a Command whose Step declares a long-running Kind, the existing entry point opens a pane and the new hosted entry point does not.
- [ ] The hosted entry point runs a multi-step Command's Steps in declared order and stops at the first Step returning an error.
- [ ] The hosted entry point wraps a failing Step's error naming the Command, identically to the existing one.
- [ ] The hosted entry point rejects a Command carrying `kind`, `run` or `targets` with the ADR-0003 message, identically to the existing one.
- [ ] The hosted entry point runs the global preflight once per invocation, not once per Step.
- [ ] The existing lifetime tests pass unchanged as the regression baseline for the CLI path.
- [ ] Grepping the hosted entry point's call graph reaches no pane-dispatch function.

## Out of scope

- Allocating or wiring the pty. This slice only establishes the entry point; the dashboard's use of it is a separate slice.
- Any change to the Kind catalog or to which Kinds are marked long-running.
- Any change to how the dashboard currently dispatches. That swap is a separate slice.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
acceptance_criteria: With Herdr available and a long-running Kind, the existing entry point opens a pane and the hosted one does not. Hosted runs Steps in declared order, stops at first failure, wraps errors naming the Command identically. Hosted rejects a Command carrying kind/run/targets with the ADR-0003 message. Hosted runs the global preflight once per invocation, not per Step. Existing lifetime tests pass unchanged. The hosted entry point's call graph reaches no pane-dispatch function.
close_reason: Added RunCommandHosted over a shared runSteps loop; runActionInline plus currentSurface keep dispatchToPane off its call graph at every depth

title: Remove the bare-word branch fallback from admin dispatch
description: admin <word> with no matching tool verb or manifest command ran 'branch --yes <word>', creating and checking out a git branch. admin.toml is never committed, so step 2 of ADR-0011 section 2 is skipped in every fresh clone and every typed command name became a git checkout: 'admin dev' in a fresh clone of sideshow created branch 'dev'. Fallback removed (ADR-0014); branch/worktree are the only ref-creating verbs and stay reserved.
close_reason: Fallback removed in 37db393; ADR-0014 records it

title: Go binary ignored .env and passed ${VAR} unexpanded to the shell
description: admin (Go) never loaded the project's .env, and kind=shell/shell-passthrough/multi-target resolved run strings with ResolveComputed instead of ResolveEnv. /bin/sh expanded the surviving ${UNRAID_HOST} to the empty string and ran anyway: etv-station's deploy became 'ssh root@' -> 'ssh: Could not resolve hostname :'. admin-py deployed correctly from the same manifest and .env seconds later. Fix: internal/manifest/dotenv.go (LoadDotenv, port of core.py::_load_dotenv), called from cmd.resolveProjectManifest and tui.loadWorkManifest; luahost.RunCmd now ResolveEnv's every command string (matching core.py::run_cmd); shell/multi-target factories resolve fully. Unbraced $x still reaches the shell untouched.
close_reason: Fixed: LoadDotenv + ResolveEnv on every shell command string; verified etv-station deploy --dry-run now resolves the host and all four ETV_STATION_* vars.

title: Two dolt sql-servers for one beads workspace deadlock every bd call
description:
Observed 2026-08-31 11:45 EDT (15:45 UTC) in admin-project-tool.

Two dolt sql-server processes were live for the single .beads workspace at
/Users/pierce/Projects/admin-project-tool/.beads/embeddeddolt:

    59057  12:34  dolt sql-server -H 127.0.0.1 -P 63050 --loglevel=warning
    69717  12:01  dolt sql-server -H 127.0.0.1 -P 64563 --loglevel=warning

While both were up, every bd invocation blocked forever rather than erroring:
`bd where --json` at 9m44s and 2m59s, `bd count --status open` at 8m20s. A
`bd where --json` run from a fresh shell also blocked and was killed at 120s.

The repo had served 75 beads normally at 11:06. The second server appeared
around 11:33 and every bd call after that hung.

Killing all three bd processes and both sql-servers restored normal operation
immediately — the next `bd where --json` returned the workspace JSON at once,

Unknown and worth finding: what spawns the second server. Candidates are two
admin TUI instances running at once (one in this repo, one in reddit-poker,

title: internal/bd has no timeout: a hung bd leaves the Beads tab on 'loading…' forever
description:
internal/bd/bd.go:272 runs the subprocess on the caller's context:

    cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "bd", args...)

Every caller passes m.ctx, the app context, which carries no deadline. Nothing
in internal/bd sets WithTimeout or WithDeadline. commands.go:359 sets
beadsInterval = 15s and beadsTickCmd refires on it, so a bd that never returns
is never killed and each tick can stack another one behind it.

Observed 2026-08-31 in this repo: `bd where --json` blocked for 9m44s, a second
for 2m59s, and `bd count --status open` for 8m20s. The Beads tab rendered
"Beads 0" with `loading…` under Ready / In progress / Blocked and stayed there.
The same repo had rendered 75 beads 25 minutes earlier.

There is no error path for this. beadsErr (model.go:167) is only set when bd
RETURNS an error; a bd that never returns leaves beadsProbed false and the pane
on its placeholder indefinitely, so the failure is indistinguishable from a slow
first load.

The hang itself is admin-7nh3. This ticket is the dashboard having no defence
against it — a timeout here would have shown the problem in 5 seconds instead
of costing the user ten minutes of a spinner.
acceptance_criteria: every internal/bd call carries a context deadline; a bd that exceeds it is killed and the pane renders a timeout message instead of 'loading…'

title: Detectors are ported but unreachable: nothing imports internal/detect, and there is no bootstrap verb
description:
Every detector was ported to Go and none of them can run. Surfaced by the
2026-08-31 triage of the pre-rewrite backlog.

## What is there

internal/detect/detectors.go (424 lines) implements the full set — apple,
react-native, rust-tauri, firefox-extension, docker, hugo, docs, forge-engine,
raylib-game, and the `simple` fallback — with detect.go:32-43 preserving
DETECTOR_ORDER exactly and Match carrying structured `Archetypes []string`
plus partial manifest Tables.

## What is missing

Nothing imports the package. `grep -rn 'internal/detect' --include='*.go' .`
returns exactly one hit outside the package itself, and it is a doc spike
(docs/spikes/admin-tui-desktop/variants.go:373, a fixture string). There is
also no verb to call it from: "new" survives only as a reserved word in
cmd/manifest.go:23's reservedToolVerbs, which exists so a manifest cannot
claim the name — no bootstrap command is registered in cmd/root.go:202-207.

So a fresh project has no path to a generated starter admin.toml, and the
detector code is dead weight the compiler cannot warn about (an unused
package is legal Go).

## Who it hurts

Anyone starting a new project with the tool. Under the Python this was
`admin new` / init-admin --bootstrap; there is no successor.

## Makes unreachable

- admin-x6tn — forge-engine never fires. Cause is now located and is none of
  the three guesses on that bead: detect.go:37-43 states outright that
  forge-engine is deliberately absent from Order. raylib-game is in the same
  position (detectors.go:395). Both need adding to Order AND a verb to run
  from.
- admin-cx00 — rust-tauri depth capped at 2 levels (detectors.go:303-307).
- admin-52o9 — firefox-extension gates on browser_specific_settings alone
  (detectors.go:334).

## Carry forward

admin-fhhx's requirement stands for whatever bootstrap verb gets built: it
must not overwrite an existing admin.toml without confirmation.

title: Port the log reader: there is no admin logs verb in Go
description:
The Go binary writes log files but cannot read them back. Surfaced by the
2026-08-31 triage of the pre-rewrite backlog.

## What is there

- `[logs.*]` sections still parse in full: internal/manifest/logs.go (297
  lines) normalizes file/command/docker/pick kinds, and internal/archetype
  merges them.
- Actions still write log files: luahost.Host.logWrite appends ANSI-stripped
  text at internal/luahost/host.go:115-129, and the pinned footer prints the
  path via MaterializeLogFile (host.go:101).

## What is missing

Nothing consumes a LogSource. `grep -rln 'LogSource' --include='*.go'` returns
only manifest.go, logs.go and archetype/merge.go — the parser and the merger,
never a runtime. There is no log-tailing package in internal/ and no `logs`
verb registered: cmd/root.go:202-207 adds branch, worktree, prs, populate and
__run-action; check.go and archetypes.go add two more. `admin logs` is gone.

## Who it hurts

Every framed action still announces a log path it is writing to, and there is
now no command that reads it. The footer exists precisely so you can copy that
path and read the run back without cancelling the process still writing to it
(this repo's CLAUDE.md, "Pinned footer"), which is no longer possible.

## Blocks

- admin-d4ef — replayed lines must be stamped with their own time, not the
  time you opened the file. Half of it already exists on the writing side:
  logformat.Options.ReuseTimestamp (internal/logformat/logformat.go:242,
  honoured at :295) is wired for exactly one caller, the log-bridge sink
  (internal/keybindings/keybindings_unix.go:44). Build the reader with
  ReuseTimestamp: true.
- admin-ytun — four projects (muxarr, stash-reels, term, stash-organizer)
  hand-rolled log tailing and cannot migrate onto the [logs.*] kinds while
  those kinds have no runtime.
- admin-d2kq — the dev|live dispatch and the `--from DD:HH:MM:SS` relative
  offset are requirements for this port, not a help string to add today.

## Note

Worth deciding whether this should block admin-3rgp.30 (delete the Python).
Deleting admin_lib/logtail.py while the Go binary cannot tail a log loses the
capability outright rather than porting it.

title: A malformed admin.toml makes admin <command> silently create a git branch instead of erroring
description:
REPRODUCED by the orchestrator at 0d1ce9c in an isolated scratch repo:

  admin.toml (note: no project_name):
      archetypes = []
      [commands.run-args]
      desc = "x"
      steps = ["run-args"]
      [actions.run-args]
      kind = "shell"
      run = "echo hi"

  $ admin run-args
  Switched to a new branch 'run-args'
  created branch run-args

It created and checked out a branch. It did not run the command, and it did not report
that the manifest was invalid.

CAUSE, and it is a design flaw in ADR-0011's ordering, not a coding slip. The resolution
order for a bare first argument is (1) tool/cmd verb, (2) manifest command, (3) branch
shorthand. When the manifest fails to RESOLVE, step 2 cannot see any command names — so
every command in that project falls through to step 3 and is treated as a branch name.

The ADR justified putting manifest commands ahead of the shorthand on exactly this
reasoning: "a manifest command swallowed by the shorthand fails SILENTLY (`admin deploy`
quietly makes a branch called deploy); a branch name shadowed by a command fails LOUDLY.
Prefer the failure the user can see." That argument holds — but it assumed the manifest
always resolves. When it does not, the silent-branch failure it was designed to prevent is
exactly what happens, and it MUTATES GIT STATE while doing it.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR: an admin.toml that EXISTS but fails to parse or resolve must be a hard
error naming the manifest problem, never a fall-through to branch shorthand. Falling
through is only correct when there is NO manifest at all — which ADR-0011 already
specifies and which must keep working.

WHO THIS HURTS: anyone who typos their admin.toml and then runs any command. They get a
stray branch, a switched checkout, and no clue what went wrong. A swarm worker hit this
for real during admin-3rgp.37 and it attempted `git checkout -b run-args` against the
shared repo; it aborted only because the tree happened to be dirty.

ADR-0011 should be amended with this case once fixed.
close_reason: Landed on feat/one-tool-go-merge at 7669010. .52 (4876fbd): registerManifestCommand now distinguishes 'no admin.toml' (still falls through to branch shorthand) from 'admin.toml exists but fails to parse/resolve' (hard error, no git mutation); ADR-0011 amended to make step 2 three-way. Orchestrator re-ran its own repro against the fix in isolated repos: malformed manifest -> "admin.toml is invalid: ... 'project_name' is required", exit 1, NO branch created; a directory with no admin.toml -> branch shorthand still works exactly as before. .23 (f4de906): the on-enter dispatch logic already existed from .20 with zero tests, so this added five locking it in — note the stored acceptance criteria (per-project-configurable row actions naming workflows) describe a design the epic's amendment superseded. .26 (b686a2a): internal/kinds/workflowquery.go resolves over.query against beads, and internal/tui/workflowconfirm.go resolves-then-confirms before dispatching; selection-sourced workflows are explicitly refused bare ('X is selection-sourced — it cannot run bare'), which keeps .27's boundary intact.

title: Rewrite the 14 archetypes in Lua and Bash
description:
Follows docs/adr/0010-lua-and-bash-are-the-authoring-languages.md. Every archetype action body becomes Bash (kind = "shell") or Lua (in-process, host API). No Python payloads remain.

This supersedes the conversion done under admin-3rgp.4, which moved Python payloads to scripts/*.py byte for byte and pointed run at them. Those files and that shape go away. The epic's "their scripts stay as they are" no longer holds.

Per body, pick the tier: Bash when the action needs no host namespace, Lua when it calls host functions or reads archetype config. Roughly 130 host calls are spread across the 14 existing bodies, so most will be Lua.

The measured baseline, for sizing: 14 bodies, 567 lines, using err/info/ok/warn, set_log_context, pick_target, only_target, run_cmd and the platform verbs, plus sys.exit and a little dict/os/shlex/shutil work. json, plistlib, urllib and os.walk are used zero times.

One body performs process supervision with threading.Lock + subprocess.Popen + poll/wait. That does NOT become Lua — it moves into the host, per the repo rule that reload state lives only in admin_lib/reload.py and the output pump only in streams.OutputPump.

The Go/Python archetype equivalence harness (tools/archetype_parity.py, internal/archetypeparity/) compares the two loaders and loses its purpose when the Python side is deleted. Decide its fate here rather than leaving it asserting parity with something gone.
acceptance_criteria:
- All 14 archetypes have Bash or Lua bodies and no Python payload.
- Each rewritten action behaves as its Python predecessor did, demonstrated by running it, not by inspection.
- archetypes/*/scripts/*.py are deleted along with the archetype.toml run values that named them.
- The Go/Python archetype parity harness is deleted or repointed, with the choice stated.
notes:
THIRD PASS landed as fdf5941. Issue stays OPEN, but the ADR-0010 breakage is GONE.

MEASURED at fdf5941: `grep -rn 'kind = "python"' archetypes/` returns NOTHING. Every
archetype body is now Bash or Lua. The 8 stale actions that made docker and unraid-plugin
unrunnable are fixed, and a scratch project on archetypes = ["docker"] now passes
`admin check` (it previously passed check and then died at dispatch — see admin-3rgp.50).

PORTED AND RUN FOR REAL this pass: docker.build (against a live Docker daemon, plus the
on_host/ssh cross-build command construction), docker.run-args (the full [docker_run]
cfg -> argv renderer including _DOCKER_FIELD_TABLE), docker.logs (dev/live dispatch,
--from/--tail/--no-follow, real epoch-based RFC3339 filtering), and all three
unraid-plugin actions (rsync push, installplg, removeplg, on both the local and ssh
branches).

STILL STUBS — the last of this ticket:
- docker.deploy
- docker.diff
Both depend on remote_recreate_container's ~280 lines of drift-refusal / snapshot logic in
admin_lib, which is not ported. Named honestly rather than half-implemented.

NOT this ticket: the 14 legacy archetypes/*.py files still exist and belong to
admin-3rgp.30 (delete the Python).
close_reason: Landed on feat/one-tool-go-merge at e7d00f8. .22 (3ffbc97): visibleTabs now derives the PRs tab from the declared uses_pull_requests key and the tracker tab from the declared tracker key — the old usesPRs() (len(remote.PRs)>0) and hasBeads inference are gone, so the tab set no longer changes under the user; the bd probe now only decides what is INSIDE the Beads tab, never whether it exists. .51 (f086b0c): four regression tests for checkUnknownKinds including the false-positive guard and multi-error collection, mutation run against the SUITE this time, not a hand-built binary. .37 (e7d00f8): docker.deploy and docker.diff are real Lua bodies via a new internal/dockerrun package — admin-3rgp.37 is now COMPLETE, with no kind='python' and no stub left anywhere.

title: Embed a Lua VM and define the host API archetype bodies call
description:
Settled by docs/adr/0010-lua-and-bash-are-the-authoring-languages.md on 2026-08-28. An archetype action body is Bash (kind = "shell", no host namespace) or Lua (in-process, full host API). kind = "python" and kind = "python-script" are deleted; no Python is shipped, invoked or authored anywhere.

This ticket is the Lua half: embed the VM and expose the host surface.

Scope:
- Select and vendor a pure-Go Lua VM. gopher-lua (Lua 5.1) is the leading candidate; confirm no cgo and that cross-compilation still works before adopting. ADR-0001 is superseded, so a third-party Go dependency is fine.
- Register the host API into the Lua state. The measured surface from the 14 existing bodies, by call count: err 29, info 23, ok 8, set_log_context 7, pick_target 7, only_target 4, run_cmd 4, warn 4, plus the platform verbs (build_ios, dev_mac, deploy_tv and siblings) and config access that today reads globals().get("_APPLE_CONFIG").
- Replace the Python stdlib leaning the bodies do — sys.exit (32 calls), dict .get, os.getcwd, shlex.quote, shutil.rmtree — with host equivalents. Bind capability from Go (JSON, globbing, plist) rather than expecting it from Lua's stdlib.
- Config tables (_APPLE_CONFIG, _SERVER_CONFIG, _REACT_NATIVE_CONFIG and siblings) reach a body as real Lua tables, not as a globals() lookup.
- Document the registered surface. It is now a versioned interface an archetype author writes against, not whatever happened to be in the interpreter's globals.

Explicitly NOT in scope: rewriting the archetypes themselves (separate ticket), and process supervision. One current body uses threading.Lock + subprocess.Popen + poll/wait; that logic moves into the host per the repo rule that reload and output-pump logic lives in admin_lib/reload.py and streams.OutputPump and is never re-hand-rolled. It does not become Lua.

Background: this ticket replaces an earlier framing that treated the conflict between inline-source and script-path `run` values as a mis-typed kind to correct. That framing was disproven — archetypes/apple/scripts/*.py are function bodies (bare top-level return, globals() reads, bare helper calls, zero imports), and internal/archetypeparity/parity_test.go:283-295 wraps them in `def __py_action(args):` before compiling, so admin-3rgp.4 built a deliberate third shape. Choosing Lua deletes the question rather than answering it: there is no python kind left to disambiguate.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pure-Go Lua VM is embedded, with no cgo, and the binary still cross-compiles.
- A Lua body dispatched by the interpreter can call every host function in the documented surface and read its archetype config as a Lua table.
- pick_target prompts from the same process, with no subprocess and no wire protocol.
- The registered host surface is documented as an interface archetype authors write against.
- No Python interpreter is spawned on any code path.
close_reason: Landed on feat/one-tool-go-merge: .36 as 23819fa (internal/luahost + gopher-lua v1.1.2 + docs/architecture/lua-host-api.md), .29 as 4dccdb4 (internal/archetype.Deploy + cmd/archetypes.go). Re-verified on the integrated tree: go build, go vet, go test ./... all green.

title: Implement the transient kind factories
description:
Implement the transient kinds — those that run and exit rather than living until killed: `shell`, `shell-passthrough`, `python`, `python-script`, `go`, `npm`, `http`, `sync`, `multi-target`.

`internal/kinds` (landed as 2fb576c) declares all nine and registers STUB factories that return a not-yet-implemented error at dispatch. This ticket replaces those nine stubs with real implementations, registered the same way, without weakening the registry's two invariants.

The reference is `admin_lib/interp.py` — one closure factory per action kind — plus the modules `internal/kinds` names for each. Behaviour parity with the Python interpreter is the bar; this is a port, not a redesign.

Resolution runs through the packages already landed: `internal/manifest` parses, `internal/archetype` merges, and the resolved action set is what the factories execute. A command's `steps` run in order and stop at the first failure; a non-zero action exit is a non-zero result.

ADR-0003 is enforced here: a command carrying `kind` or `run` is rejected with an error naming the rule.

`multi-target` prompts for a target when given none. A non-TTY caller must get a clear error rather than block forever.

Split out of admin-3rgp.7, which halted at the AFK gate on 2026-08-28. The gate failure was entirely about the OTHER half of that ticket — how `admin <command>` reaches the CLI, given cmd/root.go's `rootCmd.Use = "repo"` and its bare-arg branch shorthand. That question stays on .7. Everything in this ticket is settled and portable.

Out of scope: any CLI wiring, argv shape, or root-command identity. Drive the factories through a Go-level entry point and tests; .7 decides how a human types it.
Also out of scope: long-running kinds, guards, the frame and footer, and platform kinds (.10 through .18).
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the nine kinds executes for real, replacing its stub, with the registry's two invariants intact.
- A manifest declaring each transient kind resolves and dispatches correctly.
- A command with several steps runs them in order and stops at the first failure.
- A non-zero exit from an action produces a non-zero result.
- multi-target dispatches a named target, and fails with a clear error rather than blocking when given none with no TTY.
- A command carrying kind or run is rejected with an error naming the rule.
notes:
RESCOPED 2026-08-28 by docs/adr/0010-lua-and-bash-are-the-authoring-languages.md.

The kind list is no longer the nine this ticket was written against. python and python-script are DELETED, and lua is added. The set is now eight: shell, shell-passthrough, lua, go, npm, http, sync, multi-target.

The ticket body's line saying kind = "python" and kind = "python-script" STAY is reversed by ADR-0010 and no longer applies. Ignore it.

The lua factory depends on admin-3rgp.36 (the embedded VM and the host API surface). The other seven have no such dependency and were assessed portable by the worker that gated this ticket on 2026-08-28.
close_reason: Landed as 46c06c5 on feat/one-tool-go-merge (worker commit ca26170). Eight transient kinds per ADR-0010 — shell, shell-passthrough, lua, go, npm, http, sync, multi-target — replacing the stubs, plus internal/kinds/dispatch.go as the Go-level entry point with ADR-0003 enforcement. Re-verified on the integrated tree: go build, go vet, go test ./... all green. Four behavioural mutations confirmed discriminating.

title: Delete the Python, drop compile, supersede ADR-0001, archive repo-dash

- `go install` is the only documented installation path.
- The compile verb is gone and nothing references it.
- An ADR records the Go decision and marks the stdlib-only ADR superseded.
- `grep -r "McBrideMusings/repo"` finds nothing outside historical documents.
- The repo-dash repository is archived.

~/.admin/admin, and demotes the Python interpreter to ~/.admin/admin-py
(symlink under --link, copy otherwise). uninstall.sh removes both.

title: Two deployment paths: go install for the binary, archetypes to ~/.admin/archetypes
description:
Establish the two deployment paths, which are deliberately separate.

The binary installs with `go install` and ships no archetypes. Archetypes install by their own
path, which copies this repository's archetype directories into `~/.admin/archetypes/`.

They are separate because they change at different rates and for different reasons: the binary is
the tool, the archetypes are content that the plugin architecture is meant to prove can live
outside it. Keeping them separate is what forces the plugin path to be the real path rather than
a fallback nobody exercises.

Some archetypes may later be promoted into the binary. The loader's embed slot exists for that
and ships empty.
acceptance_criteria:
- `go install` produces a working binary that ships no archetypes.
- The archetype deployment path copies this repo's archetypes into `~/.admin/archetypes/` and is
  runnable independently of building the binary.
- A binary installed with no archetypes deployed runs, opens the dashboard, and reports that no
  archetypes are available rather than failing.
- Deploying archetypes makes them available with no rebuild.
