title: "waiting before retry" prints, then admin gives up without retrying
description:
### What happens

Start `admin dev` in a project whose backend dies immediately — say the backend port is already taken. The terminal prints:

```
Starting dev...
error: Address already in use (os error 48)
Process exited in 0.4s (code 1) — waiting before retry...
```

Then `admin dev` exits. Nothing is retried. The Vite server that was started a moment earlier is torn down with it, so the dev URL stops answering.

### What it says vs. what it does

| The message says | What the code does |
|---|---|
| "waiting before retry" — sleep, then start the backend again | sleeps 1 second, then returns and quits |

### Why that's wrong

The message promises a second attempt. There is no second attempt. Someone watching the terminal waits for a restart that is never coming, and the only clue that it gave up is the shell prompt reappearing.

### The line

`admin_lib/reload.py:319-324`:

```python
elapsed = time.monotonic() - launch_time
rc = proc.returncode
if elapsed < 2.0:
    warn(f"Process exited in {elapsed:.1f}s (code {rc}) — waiting before retry...")
    time.sleep(1)
return rc
```

`return rc` is outside the `if`, so both the fast-exit branch and the normal-exit branch leave the `while True:` loop at line 238. The sleep is the whole of the "retry".

### Who it hurts and when

Anyone running `admin dev` on any project using `kind = "vite-dev"`, every time the backend fails to come up within 2 seconds — a taken port, a compile error on a cold start, a missing env var. One wasted second, then a dead session and a misleading last line.

### One thing to decide before fixing

Vite is started once at `admin_lib/web_dev.py:182`, outside `run_with_reload`, and torn down by the cleanup registered at `web_dev.py:202` when `run_with_reload` returns. So a real retry loop restarts the backend only and leaves Vite alone, which is the right shape — but it needs an attempt cap, or a backend that can never start will spin forever.

### Fix

Either make the fast-exit branch `continue` into a bounded retry loop, or change the message to say it is giving up.

---

Filed from web-file-manager#253, whose description of the symptom ("Vite gets killed but is not relaunched, leaving only the backend running") does not match this code path — there the backend is what is gone. The misleading-message defect above is what reading the code actually shows.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #439] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-10T17:45:46Z:

Decision, so this is unambiguous for whoever picks it up: implement the bounded retry, not the reworded message.

- The fast-exit branch `continue`s the `while True:` loop at `admin_lib/reload.py:238` instead of falling through to `return rc`.
- Cap: 3 consecutive fast exits. On the 3rd, stop retrying and return the child's last exit code.
- Only the backend restarts. Vite is started once at `admin_lib/web_dev.py:182` and torn down by the cleanup at `web_dev.py:202`; the retry loop must not touch either.
- A normal (non-fast) exit still returns immediately, as today.

Acceptance: with the backend port already taken, `admin dev` attempts the backend 3 times, says so each time, then exits non-zero. Vite stays up across the retries and is torn down once at the end.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #439] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-10T17:57:45Z:

Landed in `514b38f` on `main`.

The fast-exit branch in `admin_lib/reload.py` now continues the loop instead of returning, so a backend that dies inside 2 seconds is actually relaunched. Capped at 3 consecutive fast exits, then it gives up and returns the child's own exit code. The counter resets on a manual reload (`r` / SIGUSR1), so three fast exits spread across separate reloads in one long session no longer add up to a cap. Vite is untouched — it is started and torn down outside `run_with_reload` and keeps its own lifecycle.

Driven out of process against two synthetic children:

- child exiting immediately: `retrying (1/3)...`, `retrying (2/3)...`, `giving up after 3 attempts.`, rc=1 after 3 launches (~2.1s).
- child exiting after 2.2s (past the fast-exit threshold): no retry message, one launch, rc=0 — the normal path is unchanged.

Full suite: 787 passed, 2 skipped. Regression tests for this deliberately went to #454.

title: hide_urls is silently ignored, and the URL it was meant to hide prints anyway
description:
## What happens

Every `admin` invocation in a project with `hide_urls` in its manifest opens with:

```
warning: /Users/…/etv-station/admin.toml: unknown keys are ignored: hide_urls
```

and then prints the thing it was asked to hide:

```
prod-playlist  http://100.64.0.10:8419/channels.m3u
prod-guide     http://100.64.0.10:8419/xmltv.xml
prod           http://100.64.0.10:8419
```

The manifest says:

```toml
hide_urls = ["prod"]
```

## Why that's wrong

Whoever wrote that line believed the URL was hidden. It is not, and the only signal is a warning that scrolls past on every single command. A prod URL with a raw tailnet IP then appears in the header of every terminal, screenshot, and pasted transcript from that project.

Either `hide_urls` should work, or it should be a hard manifest error — but "warn once per invocation and do the opposite of what was asked" is the worst of the three.

## Fix

Support the key: entries in `hide_urls` are matched against `[urls]` names and those rows are omitted from the header (or shown with the host masked). If the key is not going to be supported, make `admin check` reject it by name so it fails at authoring time rather than every run afterwards.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #438] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-10T18:50:02Z:

Landed on `main` (merge of `fix-hide-urls`, `21099e0`).

`hide_urls` is now a real key: `admin_lib/manifest.py` accepts it (so the "unknown keys are ignored" warning is gone) and validates its shape, and `admin_lib/archetypes.py` deletes each named entry from the merged `[urls]` dict right after the final merge. That one choke point is why nothing else needed changing — the header, the health check, the TUI URL table and `docker.py`'s `open` command all read the already-filtered dict.

A name in `hide_urls` matching no `[urls]` entry now hard-fails `admin check` (`hide_urls references unknown url ...`, exit 1) instead of silently doing nothing — which was the same failure mode as the original bug.

Driven against a scratch project matching your etv-station setup: with `hide_urls = ["prod"]` and `prod` / `prod-playlist` / `dev` in `[urls]`, the `prod` row and its literal URL are absent from the header entirely, while `prod-playlist` — same host, different label — stays visible. Matching is exact-name, not prefix. Suite on the merged result: 839 passed.

**Separately, and worth your attention:** the real tailnet IP this issue is about is committed in three files, unrelated to this fix — `tests/test_docker.py` (7 times), a docstring in `admin_lib/docker.py`, and `tampermonkey/log-bridge.user.js` (in `@connect` and in `PROBE_HOSTS`). Filed as #464.

title: Run-config drift diff renders ${VAR:-default} literally, so every redeploy is a false conflict
description:
## What happens

`admin deploy image` on a project whose `[docker_run]` uses default-form vars refuses to deploy, claiming the live container has settings the manifest doesn't:

```
live has, target missing:
    --user  99:100
    -e      ETV_STATION_TZ=America/Chicago
    -p      8419:8409/tcp

Refusing to deploy. Either back-port the live values to admin.toml,
or rerun with --force (live state will be discarded).
```

Every one of those IS in the manifest:

```toml
user = "${ETV_STATION_UID:-99}:${ETV_STATION_GID:-100}"
[[docker_run.ports]]
host = "${ETV_PORT_HOST:-8409}"
[[docker_run.env]]
value = "${ETV_STATION_TZ:-America/Chicago}"
```

and `admin env` resolves them all correctly:

```
ETV_PORT_HOST    set  = 8419
ETV_STATION_UID  set  = 99
ETV_STATION_TZ   default  = America/Chicago
```

## Why that's wrong

The drift check exists to catch a container someone edited in the Unraid GUI. Here it fires on a container the tool itself created moments earlier from the same manifest — so the one safety rail that means anything gets trained away. `--force` becomes the normal way to deploy, and a real drift will sail through unnoticed.

## Where it comes from

The comparison renders the manifest side without expanding `${VAR:-default}`. Plain `${VAR}` is expanded in the very same output — `PLEX_URL` and `PLEX_TOKEN` come out fully resolved on the `docker run` line — so it is the default-bearing form specifically. `resolve_env` in `admin_lib/core.py:441` handles both correctly; the diff path isn't going through it.

`--dry-run`'s printed `docker run` has the same gap, which makes the preview misleading in a second way: it shows a command that would fail if you ran it by hand.

## Fix

Put both the drift comparison and the dry-run preview through `resolve_env` before rendering, the same way the executed command already is.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #437] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-10T18:38:00Z:

Already fixed — closing without a change.

`d3d49c8` ("Expand `${VAR:-default}` in `[docker_run]`, not just `${VAR}`", 2026-08-08) unified `admin_lib/docker.py`'s placeholder regex with `core._ENV_VAR_RE`, which already understood the default form. Because `_build_run_args_from_cfg`'s output is the single `args` list feeding the drift comparison, the real `docker run`, and the `--dry-run` preview, fixing that one regex fixed all three paths this issue named at once. There was no separate "route the drift path through `resolve_env`" step left.

Reproduced your exact scenario to confirm rather than taking the commit message's word for it: `user`, `ports` and `env` all in `${VAR:-default}` form, against a simulated `docker inspect` of a container built from that same config, with `ETV_PORT_HOST=8419` set and `ETV_STATION_UID`/`GID` unset so they fall to `99:100`. `_compute_drift` returns `([], [])` — no false conflict. `tests/test_docker_run_args.py::test_render_run_args_expands_the_default_form_everywhere` already covers it, and the masking tests #436 added to the same rendering path still pass.

Also grepped for a second copy of the narrow regex anywhere in `admin_lib/` or `archetypes/` — there is none, so this cannot drift back out of sync at another call site.

title: deploy --dry-run prints PLEX_TOKEN and every other secret in full plaintext
description:
## What happens

Running `admin deploy all --dry-run` in a project whose `[[docker_run.env]]` carries an API token prints the token, in full, to the terminal:

```
Dry run — docker run command that would be executed on root@<host>:
  docker run -d --name etv-station … -e PLEX_URL=http://<ip>:32400 -e PLEX_TOKEN=<the actual token> …
```

The same line is written to `tmp/deploy.<timestamp>.log`, which persists.

`admin env` does it too, in its resolved-values table.

## Why that's wrong

The whole reason the value lives in a gitignored `.env` and reaches the manifest as `${PLEX_TOKEN}` is to keep it out of anything that gets read, copied, pasted, or shared. A dry run is the command you run *to show someone what will happen* — screen-shared, pasted into a chat, handed to an agent. It is the single worst place for the secret to appear.

## Who it hurts

Any project with a credential in `[[docker_run.env]]`. Deploy previews are exactly when people copy terminal output around.

## Fix

Render secret-looking env values as a mask in the preview and in `admin env` — `-e PLEX_TOKEN=••••` — while still passing the real value to the actual `docker run`. Detect on the name (`*_TOKEN`, `*_KEY`, `*_SECRET`, `*_PASSWORD`) or let the manifest mark a var `secret = true`.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #436] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-08T15:32:01Z:

Third print site, found while deploying a new Tautulli key to etv-station: the run-config drift diff on a **real** `admin deploy image`, not a dry run. The new variable landed in the "target has, live missing" block and printed in full:

```
  target has, live missing:
    -e      TAUTULLI_API_KEY=<the actual key>
```

This matters more than the dry-run case. A dry run is something you choose to run and choose to share. The drift diff fires unprompted in the middle of an ordinary deploy, so the value goes into terminal scrollback, screen shares, and anything reading the session — without anyone deciding to show it.

It also explains why this went unnoticed for so long. The diff only renders arguments that *differ*, so a secret stays invisible until the one deploy that first introduces it. `PLEX_TOKEN` was already on the live container, matched exactly, and never entered the diff. Every project hits this exactly once, on the deploy that adds the credential — and that is the deploy you are most likely to be watching closely or walking someone else through.

Two things this sharpens about the fix:

1. **Mask in the diff renderer, not just the preview.** If masking only covers `deploy --dry-run` and `admin env`, the leak simply relocates to the path nobody thinks to preview.
2. **`secret = true` on the manifest entry beats name matching alone here.** The diff still has to report that the variable differs while hiding what it differs by — "live is missing TAUTULLI_API_KEY" is the useful half, and the value contributes nothing to it. A masked diff line is strictly more readable than the real one.

Name-based detection (`*_TOKEN`, `*_KEY`, `*_SECRET`, `*_PASSWORD`) is still worth having as the default, since it protects manifests nobody has annotated. The explicit flag is what makes it dependable for a variable the pattern misses — `PLEX_URL` carries a host, `ETV_STATION_APPDATA` carries a path, and neither matches a secret-looking name.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #436] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-10T18:27:43Z:

Landed on `main` (merge of `fix-mask-secret-env`, `728b7a4`).

Values whose variable name ends in `_TOKEN`, `_KEY`, `_SECRET` or `_PASSWORD` (case-insensitive) now render as `••••` in three places: the `deploy --dry-run` docker-run preview, the `[docker_run]` drift-on-deploy report, and `admin env`'s resolved-values table. The mask is applied to a separate display copy of the argv, so the real `docker run` still receives the real value.

Driven against a fixture project with a real local Docker container:

- `deploy --dry-run` prints `-e 'PLEX_TOKEN=••••'` and leaves `PLEX_URL` in the clear. The real token appears in neither stdout nor `tmp/deploy.<ts>.log`.
- with a genuinely drifted container, the refusal-path drift report masks the token on both the live and target sides, in the terminal and the log.
- `admin env` shows `PLEX_TOKEN ... = ••••` alongside the real `PLEX_URL`.

**Also found and fixed:** the `--force` drift path used a bare `print()`, so its report never reached `tmp/deploy.<ts>.log` at all — only the header did. Both paths now write the masked report to the log.

title: apple archetype: notarize the macOS build so 'deploy mac' produces something distributable
description:
## Summary

The `apple` archetype's `deploy mac` builds a signed Release app and installs it to `/Applications`, but nothing notarizes it. Any project using the archetype therefore produces a build that Gatekeeper rejects on any machine other than the one that built it — "deploy" means "install locally", not "distributable".

Notarization is generic Apple-platform work, not project-specific, so it belongs here rather than being re-implemented as a custom `[commands.notarize]` in each project's `admin.toml`.

## Where it goes

- `admin_lib/apple.py:2401` — `deploy_mac(cfg, *, clean=False)`. Builds via `xcodebuild_filtered(...)` with `_compose_sign_settings(cfg)`, then installs. The notarize step slots in after the build succeeds and before the install.
- `archetypes/apple.py:295,304` — the `deploy` command and action definitions, if the surface changes.

## What it needs to do

After a successful Release build: zip the `.app`, `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`, then `xcrun stapler staple`. Verify with `spctl -a -vv` reporting `accepted / source=Notarized Developer ID`.

Credentials come from the project's `.env` by **reference only** — the archetype reads env var names, never literal values, and no credential ever lands in `admin.toml` or any tracked file. Two credential shapes exist and both should work: an app-specific password (Apple ID + team id + password) or an App Store Connect API key (issuer id + key id + `.p8` path).

Signing also has to change: `_compose_sign_settings(cfg)` currently produces whatever the project configures, and notarization requires a Developer ID Application identity specifically. A build signed `Apple Development` will submit and be rejected, so that should fail fast with a clear message rather than after a round trip to Apple.

When the credential env vars are absent, `deploy mac` should keep working exactly as it does today — build, install locally, and say plainly that it skipped notarization and why. Notarization being unavailable must not break the existing local-install path that every project currently depends on.

## Open decision — needs an iron-out pass before this is worked

Whether notarization is a **flag on the existing command** (`admin deploy mac --notarize`, opt-in), **automatic whenever the credential keys are present** (zero new surface, but a slow network round trip silently joins a command that is currently local and fast), or **a separate `admin notarize` command** composed after `deploy`. That choice determines the config keys and the archetype's command table, so it should be settled before implementation rather than during.

## Context

Surfaced while working `McBrideMusings/iptv-mac#27`, which needs a distributable macOS build. That issue keeps only the project-local half — Developer ID signing config and the credential key names — and depends on this.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — never implemented, in either language. A repo-wide grep for notarize/notarytool/stapler across *.go, *.lua and *.sh finds nothing outside docs/. The apple archetype's deploy mac still builds signed and installs locally, so it still produces something Gatekeeper rejects off the build machine. The Go home for it is internal/kinds/apple_darwin.go's deploy verb, after the build succeeds and before the install; the signing primitives it needs are already bound (apple.sign / apple.resolve_signing_identity, docs/architecture/lua-host-api.md:192-193).

title: docker archetype name over-promises — still hardwires the unraid module + UNRAID_HOST
description:
The `docker-unraid` archetype was renamed to `docker` (commit 133c692) because the `[docker_run]` parsing it wraps is plain Docker — Unraid is only the deploy *target*. But the archetype still hardwires Unraid specifics:

- `modules` includes `"unraid"` (`archetypes/docker.py:18`)
- `deploy`/`diff` actions read `UNRAID_HOST` / `UNRAID_USER` and build the SSH host from them
- `net.unraid.docker.managed=dockerman` label conventions, "create in the Unraid GUI first" workflow in the docstring

So the generic name `docker` now implies portability the archetype doesn't have: a plain non-Unraid Docker deploy target can't use it as-is.

**HITL — this is a design decision, not a mechanical fix.** Options to weigh:
- Split a generic `docker` (build + `run-args` + generic remote recreate) from an `unraid` archetype that layers on the Unraid module/env/labels — composed via `archetypes = ["docker", "unraid"]`.
- Parameterize the deploy target (host/user/label env keys) so one archetype serves any SSH Docker host.
- Accept the name as aspirational and document that today it targets Unraid.

Surfaced during wrap-up of #429.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — inherited verbatim into the Lua archetype. archetypes/docker/archetype.toml still hardwires Unraid: :130-131 and :374-375 both build the SSH host as `(env("UNRAID_USER") or "root") .. "@" .. env("UNRAID_HOST")`, and :305 emits a config snippet naming ${UNRAID_USER:-root}@${UNRAID_HOST}. The rename to the generic name `docker` still over-promises the same portability. One thing the port DID change: `modules` no longer exists, so the 'modules includes unraid' half of the bead is moot — the remaining coupling is the env vars and the label/workflow conventions. Still HITL: split generic docker from an unraid archetype composed on top, or rename back.

title: Plugin architecture — define custom kinds/archetypes without recompiling admin
description:
raylib-forge's iOS dev loop reuses `admin_lib.apple` via a `~/.admin` sys.path bridge (see #432) because there's no supported way for a repo to register its own kind/archetype. That bridge hardcodes the install path and breaks under `admin compile`.

A plugin mechanism (project-local `admin_ext/` or similar, discovered at runtime) would let framework repos like raylib-forge own their tooling cleanly — define custom kinds/archetypes without touching admin's core or coupling to its install layout.

Deferred from the raylib-forge iOS refactor. Keeps admin releasable as a generic tool rather than hardcoded to private game frameworks.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). NARROWED — half of this landed, half did not. ARCHETYPES are now user-extensible without recompiling: internal/archetype/search.go:36-44 searches <repoDir>/.admin/archetypes/ (project-local) and <homeDir>/.admin/archetypes/ (installed) as well as the built-ins, and archetypes are data — Lua and Bash per ADR-0010 — not Go code. So a framework repo like raylib-forge can ship its own archetype today, and the ~/.admin sys.path bridge this bead complains about is gone with the Python. KINDS are still closed: internal/kinds/catalog.go is a compiled-in catalog and factories.go panics at init on an undeclared kind, so a project cannot register a new kind without rebuilding the binary. Re-scope to that — and note ADR-0009/0010 may already answer it (a project needing new behaviour writes a Lua archetype, not a new kind), in which case this closes as won't-do rather than being built.

title: Migrate iptv-mac onto the apple archetype
description:
Split from #420 (deliverable 2).

## Problem

title: remote-build.sh reimplements [docker_run] parsing and drifts from admin_lib
description:
`tools/remote-build.sh` (in consuming projects) parses `admin.toml`'s `[docker_run]` table with its own inline awk parser + a `case "$key"` allowlist, instead of reusing `admin_lib`'s deploy run-args renderer. The two implementations drift:

- The awk/case path only honored `container_name`, `gpu`, `restart` — it **silently ignored** `memory` and `cap_add`. A container that needs a RAM cap or a capability (e.g. `PERFMON` for intel_gpu_top) would come up **without them** on a native build, even though `./admin deploy` applies them. Found while adding a `--memory` cap: had to patch the awk parser separately to honor `memory`; `cap_add` is still dropped.

Fix direction: have `remote-build.sh` call the same admin_lib renderer (or emit the run-args via a small admin subcommand) so the native-build recreate path can never diverge from `./admin deploy`. Until then, every new `[docker_run]` key has to be hand-mirrored into the shell parser.

Context: added the `memory` key to admin_lib's deploy builder in commit adding `--memory` support; the shell parser was patched in the consuming repo.

title: Convert the remaining dev/logs dispatchers to multi-target (stash-reels dev, term)
description:
Split out of #418, which landed per-target `env` and converted the four mechanical dispatchers. What's left is the set I would not convert without being able to run it.

## Why these are separate

The converted ones (stash-reels build/deploy/test/clean) were pure dispatch — pick a target, set the log context, hand off. These are not:

- **stash-reels `dev-dispatch`** (59 lines) — per target it does docker up-checks, one-shot build+sync into a container plugin dir, a curl to `reloadPlugins`, and parks `dev-plugin-test-watch` with a localhost-scoped log bridge. The dispatch part is now expressible (per-target `env` from #418 covers the bridge scoping); the orchestration is real work that has to land as child actions.
- **term `build` / `dev` / `deploy` / `e2e`** (36–106 lines each) — `dev` alone boots a simulator via `ensure_booted_simulator`, backgrounds Metro, and `os.execvp`s into `tools/dev-supervisor.mjs`.

Both drive things I cannot exercise here: a Stash container, an iOS simulator, a Metro bundler. Converting a project's primary dev loop with no way to run it afterwards is how you find out three days later that `admin dev ios` is broken. They want a session where the loop can actually be driven.

## Sequencing note

**term's dispatchers should be done together with #423** (generic dev loop). term's `dev` execvp's into `dev-supervisor.mjs`, which #423 replaces outright — converting the dispatcher first would mean rewriting the same targets twice. #423 also owns `build-mac.mjs`'s dev-watch loop, and McBrideMusings/term#146 owns its install path; between them those three empty most of that sidecar.

## Groundwork already in place

- per-target `env` (#418) — covers the bridge-host scoping both dispatchers hand-roll
- `@`-ref targets forward remaining args; plain shell targets do not — so any target taking args (`test plugin --headed`) becomes an @-ref to a `shell-passthrough` action
- stash-reels' `logs-dispatch` is #421's, not this one's

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels (dev-dispatch), /Users/pierce/Projects/term (build, dev, deploy, e2e)

## Done when

- [ ] stash-reels `dev-dispatch` → multi-target + child actions; `admin dev plugin` and `admin dev plugin-test` verified against a real test Stash
- [ ] term `build`/`deploy`/`e2e` → multi-target
- [ ] term `dev` → multi-target, alongside #423
- [ ] `admin check` passes and each converted dev loop actually runs
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, RE-POINTED. The conversions this bead deferred are still undone, and the port changed what they convert INTO: kind="python" no longer exists, so the orchestration in stash-reels' dev-dispatch and term's build/dev/deploy/e2e cannot be moved as Python at all — it becomes Lua or Bash archetype bodies (ADR-0010) plus multi-target child actions. Several of the specific pieces now have first-class kinds to land on: dev-precheck for the docker up-checks, http for the reloadPlugins curl, and luahost.RunGroup for the parallel supervision term's dev does by hand.

title: Fold muxarr's live-vs-orphan dev precheck into ports_nuke
description:
Split out of #416, which closed the pattern/pidfile/port gaps but not this one — it is a distinct feature rather than more of the same sweep.

## Problem

muxarr's `dev-precheck` is an ~86-line bash heredoc that refuses to start `dev` when another Muxarr dev process already owns the ports. What makes it more than a kill is that it **classifies** what it finds:

- `has_tty_ancestor()` — walks `/proc/<pid>/stat` up to PID 1 looking for a real TTY. Found one → the process belongs to a live interactive session, so **abort** and tell the user to Ctrl-C it. Chain ends at init without one → an **orphan**, safe to reap silently.
- `argv_in_project()` — requires an argv token to be a path inside the project root, so `bun /root/projects/muxarr/worker.js` is matched but `node /root/.npm/_npx/.../comfyui-mcp` (same `comm`, cwd happens to be under the project) is not.
- Also aborts if the `muxarr-dev` container is up.

That live-vs-orphan distinction is generic and valuable: every project with a foreground dev server wants "reap the corpse of the last run, but never kill the session I'm sitting in". `nuke_dev_processes` today has no notion of it — it kills whatever matches.

## Proposed abstraction

A precheck entry point in `admin_lib/ports_nuke.py` that reuses the existing `list_processes` / `_pid_cwd` / `_cwd_in_root` scoping and adds:

- a portable TTY-ancestor test (muxarr's is `/proc`-only; macOS needs the `ps` path, as `child_pids` already had to do — `ps -Ao pid=,ppid=,tty=`)
- the orphan-reap / live-abort split, surfaced as config on `[dev_kill]` (e.g. `precheck = true`)
- the `argv_in_project` narrowing, which `_is_project_dev_proc` partly does already

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr (dev-precheck)

## Done when

- [ ] Portable TTY-ancestor / orphan classification in ports_nuke, tested on both platforms
- [ ] Exposed via [dev_kill] config
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr; delete the dev-precheck heredoc
- [ ] `admin check` passes and `admin dev` still refuses a second session
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). DONE — the classification landed as a first-class kind. `kind = "dev-precheck"` (internal/kinds/devprecheck.go, backed by ports.DevPrecheck) reads a [dev_precheck] table and does what muxarr's 86-line heredoc did: a live interactive session or a running declared container aborts; orphans are reaped and reported, never treated as a failure. muxarr's heredoc can be deleted in favour of the table — that migration, if you want it tracked, is a downstream ticket, not this one.

title: Add a lan_ip() helper and ${LAN_IP} substitution for device-testing against local dev servers
description:
## Problem

`ipconfig getifaddr en0 || ipconfig getifaddr en1` appears twice in reddit-poker with no shared source:

- inline in the `dev-cf` action, to print the LAN URL wrangler serves on
- again in `apps/mobile/tools/build.ts`, to bake the API origin into the iOS build

Same fragile en0/en1 guess, two implementations that can disagree — and when they do, the mobile build points at the wrong host. The en0/en1 fallback is itself wrong on machines where neither is the active interface.

The underlying capability is generic: "what LAN IP will another device on this network reach me at?" Nothing in admin_lib provides it, and any project doing device-testing against a local dev server needs it — stash-reels' ios-test targets pass localhost launch args, term's React Native targets have the same shape, and it applies to any future phone-against-laptop-server setup.

## Proposed abstraction

- `lan_ip()` helper in admin_lib: enumerate interfaces properly and return the address a peer on the LAN would reach, instead of guessing en0/en1.
- Expose it as a `${LAN_IP}` substitution usable in `run` strings (touches the `${VAR}` scanner in `admin_lib/kinds.py`), so `dev-cf` becomes config rather than inline shell, and sidecars/python actions call the helper directly.

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Work/reddit-poker (dev-cf action + apps/mobile/tools/build.ts). Candidates for adoption once it exists: /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels (ios-test launch args), /Users/pierce/Projects/term (RN device targets).

## Done when

- [ ] `lan_ip()` in admin_lib with real interface enumeration, tested
- [ ] `${LAN_IP}` substitution recognized by the manifest var scanner
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Work/reddit-poker: dev-cf uses ${LAN_IP}; apps/mobile/tools/build.ts calls the helper (single source of truth)
- [ ] `admin check` passes in reddit-poker

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #426] @McBrideMusings at 2026-07-16T22:26:11Z:

Landed in 2be1cbd. reddit-poker's `dev-cf`/`dev-cf-https` migrated; its build.ts half carries Forevr-Games/social-poker#1324 (tracked file, repo has work in flight).

Two things worth recording:

**The en0/en1 guess wasn't just duplicated, it was wrong.** `ipconfig getifaddr en0 || ipconfig getifaddr en1` is macOS-only and picks nothing useful whenever the live interface is neither — a second Ethernet, a dock, a VM bridge, Wi-Fi with Ethernet also up. `lan_ip()` asks the routing table which source address it would use to reach an off-link host, which is the actual question being asked. No traffic is sent: UDP has no handshake, so `connect()` only performs the route lookup, and the target is unroutable TEST-NET-1.

**`${LAN_IP}` had to be a *computed* var, not an environment one.** The manifest scanner registers every `${VAR}` as required, so a plain substitution would make `admin env` demand a value for LAN_IP and abort a command that runs perfectly. There's now a `COMPUTED_VARS` table that `resolve_env` consults and the scanner skips. An explicit `LAN_IP` in the environment still wins, so pinning it stays possible.

That scanner behavior is worth knowing about generally — muxarr's `kill-dev` has a comment warning that the scanner reads `${...}` refs *inside comments* and registers them as required, which was making `./admin kill` abort. Same root cause; probably worth its own issue.

9 new tests in `tests/test_lan_ip.py`; suite 569 passing.

title: Expose a signing helper in admin_lib.apple (stable identifier + ad-hoc fallback); migrate nts-desktop onto the apple archetype
description:
## Problem

`[apple]` config + `admin_lib/apple.py`'s `resolve_signing_identity` already own code signing (macterm and poker-native consume them). Three projects hand-roll it:

- **nts-desktop** — `mac/codesign-local.sh` (39-line bash): auto-resolves an Apple Development identity from the keychain with ad-hoc fallback, and signs with a **stable identifier so macOS Keychain/TCC grants survive rebuilds**. Same job as `resolve_signing_identity`, reimplemented in bash. The whole project routes through `mac/Makefile` (53 lines, build-then-copy .app assembly) that the apple archetype would largely replace.
- **apple-coding-tool** — `build_pushd` (~26-line inline): Go cross-compile for 4 targets, then `codesign --force --sign -` ad-hoc on the darwin binaries so AMFI accepts them. Ad-hoc-only so it sidesteps identity resolution, but "codesign a built binary" is generic.
- **iptv-mac** — hand-written `-allowProvisioningUpdates` / `${IOS_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM}` xcodebuild lines (also covered by the apple-archetype migration in #420).

Worth noting: nts-desktop's stable-identifier trick is a capability admin_lib does **not** have today. Harvest it upward rather than delete it — rebuilds currently re-prompt for permissions in projects that lack it.

## Proposed abstraction

Expose `sign(path, identity=None, identifier=None)` in `admin_lib/apple.py`: resolve identity via the existing `resolve_signing_identity`, fall back to ad-hoc, and support a stable `--identifier` so TCC/keychain grants persist across rebuilds. Then:

- migrate nts-desktop onto the `apple` archetype (Makefile targets become archetype actions; delete codesign-local.sh)
- apple-coding-tool's `build_pushd` calls the helper instead of inline `codesign --force --sign -`

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/nts-desktop, /Users/pierce/Projects/apple-coding-tool, /Users/pierce/Projects/iptv-mac

## Done when

- [ ] `sign(...)` helper in admin_lib/apple.py with stable-identifier + ad-hoc fallback, tested
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/nts-desktop to the apple archetype (delete mac/codesign-local.sh; shrink or delete mac/Makefile)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/apple-coding-tool (build_pushd uses the helper)
- [ ] /Users/pierce/Projects/iptv-mac signing lines land via the apple archetype (see #420)
- [ ] `admin check` passes in all three

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #425] @McBrideMusings at 2026-07-16T22:35:08Z:

Upstream landed in e4ab4b7. Both migrations carry issues in their own repos (both are tracked files in dirty, off-default repos): McBrideMusings/apple-coding-tool#379, and McBrideMusings/nts-desktop#13 (comment added).

`sign()` is genuinely harvested from nts-desktop's script, as the issue predicted — admin_lib had `resolve_signing_identity` but nothing that bound a signature to a fixed identifier, which is the part that matters.

**The finding worth recording: an identifier alone is not enough.** I wrote the test to prove "same identifier → same designated requirement", and it failed — under **ad-hoc** signing the requirement stays `cdhash H"..."` no matter what identifier you pass, because there's no signing authority to anchor to. The identifier only stabilizes the requirement under a *real* identity. nts-desktop's script is already right about this (it auto-picks Apple Development and only falls back to ad-hoc for CI and the public dmg) but the issue text above implied the identifier alone did the work. It doesn't. The tests now pin both halves: identifier + real identity → identifier-anchored requirement, stable across two different binaries; ad-hoc + identifier → still cdhash-bound.

Identity resolution matches the script it replaces: explicit argument → `$CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY` → keychain → ad-hoc, so a machine with no certificate still produces a loadable binary instead of failing. It uses `resolve_signing_identity`'s proper `security find-identity` parse rather than nts-desktop's `awk '{print $2}'`, which breaks if the description shifts.

Corroborating detail from #417: an unsigned copy of a system binary is killed by AMFI on exec (`<defunct>`), which is exactly why apple-coding-tool ad-hoc signs its cross-compiled Go binaries. That guard is doing real work.

iptv-mac's signing lines are part of its apple-archetype migration, which is re-scoped and still open on #420.

title: Support build-on-host in docker-unraid deploy so muxarr stops re-parsing admin.toml with awk
description:
## Problem

muxarr's `tools/remote-build.sh` (184-line bash) rsyncs the working tree to the Unraid host, runs `docker build` there, then recreates the container — a build-remotely variant of what the `docker-unraid` archetype's deploy already does (build locally, ship the image, `remote_recreate_container`).

Its reason to exist is real: the CUDA/nvcc ffmpeg image must be built natively on amd64, which a Mac cannot produce locally.

The unacceptable part is how it gets there. To render the `docker run` argv it **re-parses `admin.toml`'s `[docker_run]` table with a hand-written awk parser**, and re-implements `${VAR}` expansion via `python3 os.path.expandvars`. That is a second, drift-prone parser for data the tool already parses canonically — any `[docker_run]` schema change silently breaks it. It also mirrors `.dockerignore` excludes by hand.

## Proposed abstraction

Add a build-on-host option to the docker-unraid deploy path (e.g. `[docker_run] build_remote = true`, or a dedicated deploy target): rsync the tree to the host honoring `.dockerignore`, `docker build` over ssh, then reuse the existing `remote_recreate_container`. The manifest stays the single source of the `docker run` argv — no second parser.

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr

## Done when

- [ ] docker-unraid deploy supports building on the remote host
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr to it; delete tools/remote-build.sh (awk [docker_run] parser and hand-rolled ${VAR} expansion die with it)
- [ ] `admin check` passes in muxarr; a real remote build/deploy verified once
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, AND THE UNACCEPTABLE PART GOT WORSE. muxarr's tools/remote-build.sh re-parses [docker_run] with a hand-written awk parser precisely because the tool would not build on the host — and the canonical parser it is drifting from has now moved and changed shape entirely (internal/dockerrun/, with a declarative field table at fieldtable.go). An awk mirror of a Python dict is now an awk mirror of a Go struct table, which nothing keeps in step. The build-on-host opt-in this proposes is still the fix; internal/remotehost and internal/kinds/installtemplate.go show the remote-exec machinery already in the tool.

title: Generalize the restart-hotkey dev loop beyond the apple archetype
description:
## Problem

The `apple` archetype's `dev_mac` loop (build, launch, stream logs, `r` reload) is the only shared dev-supervisor; macterm consumes it. Three non-Apple projects hand-rolled the same skeleton — spawn supervised process(es), keyboard restart, clean teardown:

- **term** — `tools/dev-supervisor.mjs` (100-line Node): spawn detached in own process group, `R`=restart / `q`=quit raw-mode hotkeys, TERM-then-KILL signal-tree escalation; `apps/desktop/tools/build-mac.mjs` dev mode adds a watchFile-restart variant
- **nts-desktop** — `mac/dev.sh` (67-line bash): build+sign, launch background pid, `R`=rebuild+relaunch, `Q`=quit
- **muxarr** — `dev-local` (~100-line inline heredoc): spawn bun+vite, respawn loop, `r`/`R`/`v` per-process restart keys, /proc cleanup-trap sweep

admin_lib already has the raw pieces (`watch.py`, `reload.py`, `keybindings.py`, the apple loop) but no generic entry point.

## Proposed abstraction

A generic dev-loop capability: config table declaring one or more supervised processes (`build` step, `run` command, optional watch paths), standard hotkeys (restart one / restart all / quit), and the existing teardown semantics (process-group TERM then KILL). Either a new kind (e.g. `dev-loop`) or an admin_lib helper the `python` kind can call — whichever composes better with the apple archetype so dev_mac becomes a consumer of the same core.

Projects then keep only their process definitions; the supervision code is deleted (term dev-supervisor.mjs, nts-desktop dev.sh loop, muxarr dev-local heredoc).

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/term, /Users/pierce/Projects/nts-desktop, /Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr

## Done when

- [ ] Generic dev-loop exists in admin_lib; apple dev_mac shares the same core
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/term (delete tools/dev-supervisor.mjs; fold build-mac.mjs dev-watch into it)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/nts-desktop (dev.sh)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr (dev-local)
- [ ] `admin check` passes in all three
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, AND MOST OF THE SUBSTRATE NOW EXISTS. The apple dev loop is still the only shared restart-hotkey supervisor (internal/kinds/appledevloop_darwin.go), and term, nts-desktop and muxarr still hand-roll their own. But the generic pieces the bead says are missing an entry point are now cleanly separated Go packages with a caller-owned shape: internal/reload (SetupReload/PollForReload/IsRebuildRequested/ClearRebuildRequest, documented at docs/architecture/lua-host-api.md:232-234), internal/keybindings (Run with r/R/q bindings and signal targets), internal/streams.OutputPump, and luahost.RunGroup for supervising N children with signal-tree teardown (rungroup.go:36-46). What is still missing is exactly what this bead names: a generic long-running dev-supervisor KIND that composes them for a non-Apple project.

title: Add a bridge-listen kind to replace tail -f /dev/null log-bridge parking actions
description:
## Problem

Two projects define interactive-shell actions whose entire body is `tail -f /dev/null`, existing only to park a session so the log bridge attaches and browser console output streams in:

- **reddit-poker** — `logs-prod-client`, `logs-local-client`, `logs-branch-client` (three copies differing only in bridge host scope)
- **stash-reels** — `logs-bridge` (host scope injected by the dispatcher that invokes it)

The idiom is opaque — nothing about `tail -f /dev/null` says "log bridge listener" — and each copy re-derives it.

## Proposed abstraction

A configless kind `bridge-listen` that parks the session (reusing the interactive-shell machinery, which already spins up the bridge) and takes host scope from config/env:

```toml
[actions.logs-live-client]
kind  = "bridge-listen"
hosts = "${LOG_BRIDGE_LIVE_HOSTS}"
```

One `_kind(...)` entry in `admin_lib/kinds.KINDS` + one `register_factory` in `admin_lib/interp.py`, per the standard recipe.

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Work/reddit-poker, /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels

## Done when

- [ ] `bridge-listen` kind exists (KINDS entry + factory)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Work/reddit-poker (three client-log actions)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels (logs-bridge)
- [ ] `admin check` passes in both

comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #422] @McBrideMusings at 2026-07-16T22:29:37Z:

Landed in 26ae26b. All four actions migrated (reddit-poker's three client listeners, stash-reels' logs-bridge); `admin check` passes in both.

The kind needs no `run` at all, and `hosts` is optional — it narrows what a listener advertises so several can run side by side. None of these four needed it: they all want the project-level `[log_bridge].hosts`, and stash-reels' has its scope injected by the caller (now via per-target `env` from #418).

**One thing found that's worth its own fix: stash-reels' `kill-local` reaps the listener with `pkill -f 'tail -f /dev/null'`.** That is a dependency on the park command — an implementation detail that, as of this change, lives in the tool rather than in their manifest. title: Migrate hand-rolled log tailing onto the [logs.*] kinds; extend them where real gaps pushed projects off
description:
## Problem

The tool owns log streaming: `[logs.*]` kinds `file`, `command` (host/user), `docker` (container + remote host), `pick` (glob), plus `logtail`/`log_format`. stash-organizer's `[logs.plugin]`/`[logs.docker]`/`[logs.pick]` tables show correct usage. Four re-implementations exist anyway:

- **muxarr** — `logs-dev-stream`/`logs-live-stream`: inline `ssh ${UNRAID_USER}@${UNRAID_HOST} 'docker logs -f --tail 200 <container>'` (exactly `[logs.docker]` with `host`), plus a 6-line python `logs-dispatch` that picks dev/live and scopes `ADMIN_LOG_BRIDGE_HOSTS`
- **stash-reels** — `logs-dispatch` python: same ssh docker logs, plus a grep-highlight "both" mode
- **term** — `logs` python action: `tail -F tmp/admin/*.log` per target (`[logs.file]`/`[logs.pick]` territory)
- **stash-organizer** — `scripts/logs.mjs` (158-line Node sidecar): remote-or-local JSONL follow with `--since/--level/--grep` and colors; the JSONL format is project-specific but the follow/filter/color mechanics duplicate `logtail`/`log_format`

## Proposed abstraction

Migrate muxarr, stash-reels, and term onto `[logs.*]` tables. Before migrating, name the real gaps that pushed each off the shared path and extend the kinds for the genuine ones:

- per-target log-bridge host scoping during a logs command (muxarr/stash-reels dispatch)
- match-highlight option (stash-reels "both" mode)
- structured (JSONL) level/field filtering (stash-organizer logs.mjs)

Whatever proves genuinely project-specific in logs.mjs (its noise filters) can stay, but the transport/follow/format layer should be shared.

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr, /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels, /Users/pierce/Projects/term, /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-organizer

## Done when

- [ ] Gap analysis done; [logs.*] kinds extended for the genuine gaps
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr (both stream actions + dispatch)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/term (logs action)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels (logs path of the dispatcher)
- [ ] Shrink or delete /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-organizer scripts/logs.mjs
- [ ] `admin check` passes in all four
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL AND NOW BLOCKING — the migration target does not exist any more. [logs.*] sections still parse and merge (internal/manifest/logs.go, 297 lines) but nothing consumes a LogSource: there is no log tailer in internal/ and no `admin logs` verb. So the four hand-rolled re-implementations this bead lists (muxarr, stash-reels, term, stash-organizer) cannot be migrated onto the [logs.*] kinds today, because the kinds have no runtime. This bead is now blocked on porting the log reader — the same gap admin-d4ef records. Keep the extension list (--since/--level/--grep, the dev/live dispatch, bridge-host scoping) as the requirements for that port rather than as follow-on work.

title: Delete the stash-plugin archetype; migrate Stash plugin repos to the generic sync kind
description:
## Problem

The `stash-plugin` archetype (`archetypes/stash-plugin.py`) is too specific to earn archetype status — it describes a single project shape (rollup + rsync to a plugin dir), not a platform or development environment. Fittingly, none of the three actual Stash plugin repos use it; each rebuilt deploy from scratch:

- **stash-subtitles** — `scripts/deploy.mjs` (63 lines): dotenv, build, rsync to remote `STASH_DEPLOY_TARGET` or cpSync to local dir
- **stash-organizer** — same-shaped `scripts/deploy.mjs` (reached via `npm run deploy`)
- **stash-reels** — deploy inline in its python dispatcher: build, rsync, `curl` GraphQL `reloadPlugins`; test fixtures re-implement copy-into-plugin-dir + reload

The underlying operations are generic: build, then copy build artifacts to a specified folder (local or remote), then optionally hit an HTTP endpoint. The tool already owns both halves — the `sync` kind (`admin_lib/interp.py` `_make_sync`) and the `http` kind.

## Proposed change

1. **Delete `archetypes/stash-plugin.py`** (and its detector entry if one exists). Not an archetype-shaped concern.
2. Verify/extend the `sync` kind so it covers what the deploy scripts actually do: local dir dest and remote `user@host:path` dest (rsync), delete-extraneous semantics. If remote isn't supported yet, add it — that is the generic capability worth owning.
3. Migrate all three repos: `deploy` = build step + `sync` action; Stash-specific `reloadPlugins` becomes a small `http` (or one-line shell curl) action per repo. Delete both `deploy.mjs` files.

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/stash-subtitles, /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-organizer, /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels

## Done when

- [ ] `archetypes/stash-plugin.py` removed (plus detector references)
- [ ] `sync` kind handles local + remote dests with delete semantics (verified against the deploy.mjs behavior)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-subtitles (delete scripts/deploy.mjs)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-organizer (delete scripts/deploy.mjs)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels (deploy path of the dispatcher; fixtures reload can reuse the http action)
- [ ] `admin check` passes in all three

comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #419] @McBrideMusings at 2026-07-16T22:23:15Z:

Landed in 839429a. Archetype and detector deleted, `sync` made a real replacement, stash-subtitles migrated. **stash-organizer deliberately not migrated** — see below.

`sync` already did more than the issue assumed: the remote/local split was there (rsync when the dest looks like `user@host:/path`, copytree otherwise). Two things were missing:

- **Delete parity.** The remote half has always run `rsync --delete`; the local half was a plain copytree. So the two halves of one function meant different things — a renamed or removed source file lingered in a local dest forever and the plugin kept loading the stale copy. Local now prunes too. Nothing declares `kind = "sync"` today, so this changes no current behavior — which is precisely why it was the moment to fix it, before adoption.
- **`excludes`.** Pruning makes this load-bearing, not a nicety (next point).

**The find that changed the plan: stash-organizer's deploy guards live databases.** Its `deploy.mjs` has a `PROTECTED_RUNTIME_FILES` set — `py/library.db`, `py/organize_state.db`, `py/duplicate_state.db`, `py/sort_state.db`, their `-wal`/`-shm` siblings, `py/remux_state.json`. Those are live SQLite DBs sitting *inside the deployed plugin directory*, and the deploy deliberately does not delete them. A plain `sync --delete` would have destroyed that media library index and organize/dedupe state.

So `excludes` exists for that case (excluded paths are neither copied nor deleted), but I would not run that migration blind against a real plugin dir. It carries McBrideMusings/stash-organizer#143 with the exact config, the warning, and a verify-first checklist. It also has a dev/production mode switch that wants a multi-target with per-target env (#418) rather than a script arg.

**stash-subtitles migrated** — `deploy` is now `build` + a `sync` action, and McBrideMusings/stash-subtitles@f8184dc deletes its 63-line `deploy.mjs` and the package.json script. The `STASH_PLUGIN_DEST` it injected turned out to be the absolute path of `dist/`, which both `rollup.config.common.mjs` and `generateYaml.mjs` already default to — nothing depended on it. (Its `admin.toml` change is uncommitted on purpose: `admin.toml` is tracked in that repo, which is its own problem.)

stash-reels' deploy already became an `http` action for reloadPlugins in #418; its rsync can move to `sync` when #428 converts `dev-dispatch`.

Also updated `docs/architecture/design.md`, which listed stash-plugin as a live archetype and detector, with a note on why it's gone. The historical survey that first named it stays as written — it was true then.

9 new tests in `tests/test_sync.py`; suite 560 passing.

title: Convert python dispatcher actions to multi-target; extend the kind where targets need setup it can't express
description:
## Problem

The `multi-target` kind already provides one-action/N-targets dispatch with a picker (rpg-toolkit uses it cleanly: build/dev/deploy dispatch to `@`-ref'd child actions). Two projects hand-roll the same dispatch as `kind = "python"` blobs — the largest inline-code blocks found in the audit:

- **stash-reels** — six `*-dispatch` actions (build/dev/deploy/test/clean/logs), all multiline python; `dev-dispatch` is 59 lines mixing target-picking with per-target logic (docker up-checks, curl reloadPlugins, rsync, `ADMIN_LOG_BRIDGE_HOSTS` scoping)
- **term** — `build`/`dev`/`deploy`/`e2e`/`logs` are python dispatchers holding dicts of triple-quoted shell strings, 36-106 lines each, calling `pick_target` manually

The python wrapper mostly re-implements what multi-target + child actions express declaratively. Converting is structural, not cosmetic: each target becomes a named, individually-runnable action, and the bespoke dispatch layer disappears.

## Proposed abstraction

1. Mechanically convert each dispatcher to a `multi-target` parent with per-target child actions.
2. Where a target genuinely cannot express its setup declaratively today (e.g. per-target env vars like stash-reels' log-bridge host scoping, or pre-steps like "boot test Stash first"), extend the multi-target/child schema to cover it (per-target `env` table, `steps` composition) instead of keeping python.
3. Residual real logic (term's execvp into dev-supervisor) stays as small python child actions — the dispatch itself must not.

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels, /Users/pierce/Projects/term

## Done when

- [ ] multi-target children support whatever setup the converted targets actually need (per-target env at minimum, verified against both projects)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/stash-reels (six dispatchers)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/term (build/dev/deploy/e2e/logs)
- [ ] `admin check` passes in both

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #418] @McBrideMusings at 2026-07-16T22:16:46Z:

Landed in cfefee2. Upstream capability done; four of six stash-reels dispatchers converted. The rest split to #428 — reasoning below.

**Per-target `env`** was exactly the gap the issue guessed at. An inline target could already carry `desc`/`run`/`action`/`pty`/`watch`/`requires` but not `env`, and that single missing thing is why both stash-reels and muxarr wrapped a declarative multi-target in a python dispatcher — both only needed to scope `ADMIN_LOG_BRIDGE_HOSTS` to dev vs live. Env applies after the target is picked but before its guards run, so a guard sees what the target will.

**One thing worth knowing for future conversions:** `@`-ref targets forward the remaining args (`run_command(shell[1:], rest_args)`); plain shell targets do not. So any target that takes arguments — `test plugin --headed` — has to be an `@`-ref to a `shell-passthrough` action. That's how stash-reels' `test` kept its arg forwarding.

Converted in stash-reels: **build**, **deploy**, **test**, **clean**. Its inline curl to Stash's `reloadPlugins` became an `http` action. `admin check` passes; all four resolve as multi-target with their targets intact.

**Not converted, moved to #428: stash-reels `dev-dispatch` and all of term's.** These aren't dispatch — stash-reels' `dev` does docker up-checks, build+sync into a container plugin dir, and a reloadPlugins curl; term's `dev` boots a simulator, backgrounds Metro, and `execvp`s into `dev-supervisor.mjs`. They drive a Stash container, an iOS simulator, and a Metro bundler, none of which I can exercise here, and converting a primary dev loop with no way to run it afterwards is how it silently breaks. They want a session where the loop can be driven.

**term's should be done with #423 specifically** — its `dev` execvp's into `dev-supervisor.mjs`, which #423 deletes outright, so converting first means writing the same targets twice.

7 new tests in `tests/test_target_env.py`; suite 551 passing.

title: Add an install_app helper (kill, atomic replace in /Applications, relaunch) to admin_lib
description:
## Problem

Six projects hand-roll the same "install .app into /Applications" ritual — kill running instance, remove old bundle, copy new one, sometimes lsregister/relaunch — with wildly varying quality:

- **charcoal** `install-app`: `pkill -f` + `rm -rf` + `cp -r` + explicit `lsregister -f`
- **rpg-toolkit** `deploy-mac` (5-line inline): electron:make, `rm -rf`, `cp -R`
- **iptv-mac** `deploy-mac`: Release xcodebuild, `rm -rf` + `ditto`
- **nts-desktop**: Makefile `install` target, build + `ditto`
- **macterm** `install` (~22-line inline python+heredoc): resolve signing identity, graceful TERM loop (50x0.1s) then KILL by exact exec path, `mise run install-app`, conditional relaunch
- **term** `apps/desktop/tools/build-mac.mjs` release path: atomic ditto+temp+rename install with relaunch, inside a 207-line sidecar

macterm/term have the good version (graceful kill, atomic replace, relaunch); the rest clobber. Everyone should get the good version.

## Proposed abstraction

`admin_lib` helper `install_app(bundle_path, app_name=None, process_name=None, relaunch=True)`: graceful TERM-then-KILL of the running instance, atomic replace (ditto to temp dir + rename over /Applications/X.app), `lsregister -f`, optional relaunch-if-was-running. Expose to `kind = "python"` actions and wire the `apple` archetype's deploy/install path through it; Electron/Tauri/Swift projects call the same helper.

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/charcoal, /Users/pierce/Projects/rpg-toolkit, /Users/pierce/Projects/iptv-mac, /Users/pierce/Projects/nts-desktop, /Users/pierce/Projects/macterm, /Users/pierce/Projects/term

## Done when

- [ ] `install_app` exists in admin_lib with tests; apple archetype install/deploy uses it
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/charcoal
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/rpg-toolkit
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/iptv-mac
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/nts-desktop
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/macterm
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/term (build-mac.mjs install step)
- [ ] `admin check` passes in all six

title: Extend nuke-dev/dev_kill with pattern-based kills so projects stop hand-rolling kill actions
description:
## Problem

`kill-port` and `nuke-dev` kinds (backed by `admin_lib/ports.py` + `admin_lib/ports_nuke.py`) already own process/port teardown — web-file-manager consumes `nuke-dev` via `[dev_kill]` config correctly. Seven projects hand-roll it instead:

- **muxarr** — ~59-line `kill-dev` heredoc (lsof ports 3300/3350, process-group TERM→KILL, pid-file reap) plus an ~86-line `dev-precheck` orphan reaper walking /proc
- **term** — `down` action, ~67 lines of inline python: pid-file stops, port frees (8790/5173/8081), pkill
- **rpg-toolkit** — 5-line inline `kill`: docker compose down + `lsof -ti tcp:3300 | xargs kill -9` + pkill electron-forge/vite
- **wedding** — 7-line pkill loop over hugo/wrangler/workerd patterns
- **etv-next** — `kill` pkill by binary-path regex, duplicated inside `dev`
- **portfolio** — `kill-dev` pkill of hugo server
- **reddit-poker** — `kill-supabase` 9-line docker-socket probe + supabase stop

Two mechanisms in the wild: port/pidfile-based (muxarr, term, rpg-toolkit) and pkill-by-pattern (wedding, portfolio, etv-next).

## Proposed abstraction

Extend the `[dev_kill]` config consumed by `nuke-dev` to accept `patterns = [...]` (pkill -f sweeps) alongside the existing ports/pidfiles, so every project expresses teardown as config instead of inline code. Fold muxarr's dev-precheck ("refuse to start when a live session owns the ports; reap orphans") into `ports_nuke` as a reusable precheck — it is generic, not muxarr-specific. reddit-poker's supabase docker-socket probe likely stays project-specific, but its kill-* chain can compose the shared kind.

## Affected projects

/Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr, /Users/pierce/Projects/term, /Users/pierce/Projects/rpg-toolkit, /Users/pierce/Projects/wedding, /Users/pierce/Projects/etv-next, /Users/pierce/Projects/portfolio, /Users/pierce/Work/reddit-poker

## Done when

- [ ] `[dev_kill]` supports `patterns`; nuke-dev handles pattern + port + pidfile teardown
- [ ] Orphan/live-session precheck available upstream (ports_nuke), replacing muxarr dev-precheck
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/muxarr (kill-dev + dev-precheck)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/term (down procs layer; tmux/tests layers stay project-specific)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/rpg-toolkit
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/wedding
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/etv-next (kill + the pkill embedded in dev)
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Projects/portfolio
- [ ] Migrate /Users/pierce/Work/reddit-poker where composable
- [ ] `admin check` passes in all

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #416] @McBrideMusings at 2026-07-16T22:02:12Z:

Landed in 1899473. Six of seven projects migrated; `admin check` passes in each, and `admin down procs` (term) and `admin kill` (muxarr) verified against live processes.

Three gaps kept these projects off nuke-dev, not one. The issue named the first; the other two only showed up while migrating:

- **patterns** (as specified) — cwd-scoped by default. Worth stating plainly: the `pkill -f 'hugo server'` this replaces is machine-wide and will kill the same dev server running from an unrelated checkout. There's a test for exactly that.
- **child reaping** — a pidfile names a *supervisor*, and SIGTERM to it does not take its children; they reparent and keep the port. term was doing `pkill -P "$p"; kill "$p"` by hand for this reason, so migrating it as-is would have silently left strays. The pidfile pass now kills the tree deepest-first. (`ps --ppid` is GNU-only and `ps -P` on macOS is *not* a ppid filter — descendants come from one portable `ps -Ao pid=,ppid=` pass.)
- **env-resolved ports** — pidfile paths already resolved `${VAR}`; ports did not. muxarr's port is `${PORT:-3300}`, so it would have had to hardcode 3300 and drift from whatever its server actually binds.

Per-project outcomes:

- wedding, portfolio, etv-next — pkill loops → `patterns` (etv-next's is a regex)
- rpg-toolkit — its docker-compose teardown stays its own action; the port free + stray reaping are now the shared sweep
- term — `down` is now a multi-target picker. Only its `procs` layer is generic; the two tmux layers are genuinely its own and stay hand-written (the test-socket sweep is prefix-scoped so it can't touch the `term` dev socket — its comment records 265 leaked sockets). Also needed `ports_nuke` added to its explicit `modules`, since a `kind = "python"` action doesn't pull the module in the way a `kind = "nuke-dev"` one does.
- muxarr — `kill-dev`, 59 lines of bash heredoc, is now ports + pidfiles.
- **reddit-poker: no change, deliberately.** The issue said "migrate where composable" — nothing is. Its `kill-local`/`kill-cf`/`kill-mainframe` delegate to `bun run dev:kill:*` scripts, and `kill-supabase` probes the docker socket. None of that is nuke-dev's job.

**muxarr's `dev-precheck` split out to #427.** It isn't more of the same sweep — it *classifies* processes (TTY-ancestor walk → live session, abort; no TTY → orphan, reap). That live-vs-orphan idea is generic and worth having, but it's a feature of its own and muxarr's version is `/proc`-only.

15 new tests in `tests/test_ports_nuke_patterns.py`; suite 534 passing.

title: Add a raylib-game archetype covering the duplicated cmake-build/dev/smoke/clean actions
description:
## Problem

Seven raylib/CMake game projects hand-declare near-identical actions:

- `cmake-build`: `cmake -S . -B build [-DRF_HOTRELOAD=ON] && cmake --build build [-j8]`
- `dev`/`run`: build then launch `./build/<name>`
- `smoke`: `RF_SMOKE=1 ./build/<name>` (auto-exiting smoke run — uniform raylib-forge convention)

title: Teach go-cli archetype a binary-output config so Go projects stop shadowing its actions
description:

The `go-cli` archetype provides `build`/`test`/`vet`/`fmt`/`deploy`/`clean` actions (`archetypes/go-cli.py`), but three projects that declare `archetypes = ["go-cli"]` shadow most of them inline:

title: register_factory should raise on double-registration of a kind
description:
Noted by code-review during #403 wrap-up (not a current bug — out of scope for #403).

`admin_lib/kinds.py` `register_factory(name, fn)` sets `KINDS[name].factory = fn` unconditionally. If two `register_factory` calls in `interp.py` ever target the same kind (a copy-paste slip), the second silently overwrites the first with no error.

It's not reachable today (each kind is registered exactly once), but a guard would catch the mistake at import:

```python
if spec.factory is not None:
    raise FragmentError(f"register_factory: kind {name!r} already has a factory")
```

Small hardening that complements #403's other two invariants (unknown-kind rejection + missing-factory check).

## Acceptance criteria

title: Architecture: no structural boundary between manifest frontend and runtime in admin_lib/
description:
Surfaced by the architecture-fit check during #406 wrap-up.

Folding `gen/` into `admin_lib/` (#406) was the right call — it removed an inverted dependency (the runtime interpreter was importing helpers out of the "generator" package). But the consequence: `admin_lib/` now holds **both** the manifest frontend (`manifest.py`, `archetypes.py`, `kinds.py`, `detectors.py`, `compile.py`) and the runtime (`interp.py`, `core.py`, `logtail.py`, `guards.py`, ...). There is no longer a directory boundary enforcing "frontend vs runtime."

The only thing preventing a *new* inverted import (e.g. `manifest.py` importing `interp`) is discipline, not structure. `admin_lib/manifest.py` already duplicates `GUARDS_BUILTIN` rather than importing it "so the manifest layer stays independent" — a good instinct that's now a convention, not a wall.

**Options (not yet decided):**
- A lightweight import-direction test/lint asserting the frontend modules never import the runtime ones (cheap, AFK).
- A sub-package split inside `admin_lib/` (e.g. `admin_lib/frontend/`) to make the seam structural again — but that partly re-introduces the two-package shape #406 deliberately removed; weigh carefully.

Low priority — no current violation. File so a future reader (or `improve-codebase-architecture`) can pick it up.

_Source: #406 wrap-up architecture-fit finding._
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). FIXED BY THE PORT — the boundary is now structural, not a convention. Frontend and runtime are separate Go packages: internal/manifest, internal/archetype and internal/validate parse and resolve; internal/kinds and internal/luahost execute. An inverted import (manifest importing kinds) is a compile error, not a discipline failure, so neither the import-direction test nor the sub-package split this bead weighed is needed.

comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #409] @McBrideMusings at 2026-06-23T18:56:20Z:

Deferred from an autonomous follow-up pass — the cheap import-direction test needs one design decision first, so I'm surfacing it rather than guessing (same handling as #408).

**Import graph today** (admin_lib-internal edges only):
- `kinds` → (none) — leaf
- `validate` → `kinds`
- `guards` → `core`
- `manifest` → `kinds`, `guards`, `validate`
- `archetypes` → `kinds`, `manifest`, `guards`, `validate`

Good news: **no frontend module imports `interp` or any per-kind runtime helper** (logtail/apple/ports/docker/watch/web_dev/…). The core invariant from #406 (frontend usable without the interpreter) already holds.

**Why a flat \"forbid the runtime modules incl. core\" test isn't writable as-is — two muddy spots:**
1. **`core` is a shared leaf.** It holds logging/registry primitives used by *both* layers; `guards` imports `from .core import err`. Forbidding the frontend from importing `core` would fail on that legitimate edge. So `core` must be classified \"shared, allowed,\" not \"runtime.\"
2. **`guards` is a *mixed* module.** It exposes frontend hooks (`parse_guard_tables`, `validate_requires`) AND runtime behavior (`register_shell_guard`, `run_requires`, the git built-ins) and imports `core`. The frontend imports `guards` for the hooks but thereby pulls its runtime half. So \"frontend imports no runtime\" is already fuzzy at `guards`.

**The decision (pick one):**
- **(a) Narrow test — forbid `interp` (+ `compile`) only.** Unambiguous, true today, and is the exact #406 regression guard (\"frontend never pulls the interpreter engine\"). Cheapest; under-delivers vs the broad wording but encodes the property that actually matters.
- **(b) Allowlist test — frontend modules may import only {kinds, validate, manifest, archetypes, guards, core}; everything else forbidden.** Robust (enumerate the small allowed set, not the runtime set). Bakes in \"core + guards are allowed frontend/shared infra\" as the contract — fine if you accept guards-as-frontend.
- **(c) Split `guards` first** into guards-frontend (parse/validate) vs guards-runtime (register/run), then the boundary is clean and either test above is exact. This is the structural option (akin to #409's sub-package split) and needs its own design pass.

My recommendation: **(a)** now (it's the real invariant and zero-ambiguity), optionally **(b)** if you want the broader wall, and treat **(c)** as a separate structural ticket. A 30-second call turns this back into AFK.

title: Extract a named action/command schema validator (admin_lib/validate.py)
description:
## Problem

The true action-schema enforcer is `_to_command()` in `gen/archetypes.py:408` — 208 lines, nameless, doing kind validation, key validation, `requires` parsing, target handling, and descriptor collation all at once. Meanwhile the "commands are pure routing" rule (ADR-0003) is checked in **two** places with **two** exception types:

- `gen/manifest.py:157` — manifest `[commands]`, raises `ManifestError`
- `gen/archetypes.py:416` — archetype commands inside `_to_command()`, raises `ArchetypeError`

A reader can't find "where is an action validated" by name, and the central invariant of ADR-0003 is enforced piecemeal.

## Decision (resolved)

**New module `admin_lib/validate.py`** — the single home for "is this manifest entity well-formed":

```
admin_lib/validate.py
  validate_command(c)   -> routing-only rule (ADR-0003): desc + steps only
  validate_action(a)    -> kind in catalog, allowed keys, requires shape
  (one error type)
```

Both ingestion paths call it:

- `manifest.py` parse -> `validate.validate_command(...)`
- `archetypes.py` resolve -> `validate.validate_action(...)` (and `validate_command` for archetype-declared commands)

`_to_command()` shrinks to wiring/merge; the schema rules move out. The pure-routing rule is checked **once** (in `validate_command`), called from both paths.

### Error type

Unify on **one** validation error type raised by `validate.py` (e.g. `ValidationError`), rather than today's split `ManifestError` (parse) vs `ArchetypeError` (resolve). Callers (`admin-run` dispatch) catch the one type. Keep messages phase-aware (they can say "in admin.toml [commands]" vs "in archetype X") but the exception class is one.

## Scope of work

- Create `admin_lib/validate.py` with `validate_command` + `validate_action`.
- Move kind / key / requires-shape checks out of `_to_command()` into `validate_action`.
- Move both pure-routing checks into the single `validate_command`; delete the duplicate.
- Pick the unified error type; update catch sites in `admin-run`.
- `_to_command()` becomes thin (merge + wire only).

> Note: the kind-membership check should read the unified kind registry from #403 (`admin_lib/kinds.py`), not a second copy. The `requires`-shape check overlaps with the guard module in #407 — `validate_action` checks the **shape** of `requires` (a list of strings); `guards.validate()` checks the **names** resolve. Keep that division.

## Wins

- Locality: every action/command schema rule in one place
- Pure-routing rule (ADR-0003) checked once
- Navigability: a discoverable, named validator
- One validation error type for callers

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `admin_lib/validate.py` owns `validate_command` + `validate_action`.
- [ ] The pure-routing check exists in exactly one place.
- [ ] One validation error type; `admin-run` catches it; messages stay phase-aware.
- [ ] `_to_command()` no longer contains schema rules (merge/wiring only).
- [ ] `tests/test_manifest.py` + `tests/test_archetypes.py` updated/green; `./admin test` green.

## Sequencing

After #406 (everything in `admin_lib/`). Reads the kind registry from #403; coordinates the `requires`-shape vs name-resolution split with #407. Reinforces ADR-0003.

## Classification

**AFK** — design resolved (new `admin_lib/validate.py`, one error type).

_Source: local architecture review (deepening candidate 05)._

Scope finding from an autonomous iterate pass — deferring #408 for an interactive design decision rather than guessing.

The issue body assumed two validation sites (`_to_command` + the manifest routing check). There are actually **three** passes of command/action schema validation:

1. `admin_lib/archetypes.py::load_archetype` (~lines 141-161) — per-archetype-file unknown-key check.

- **Error-type collapse vs phase precision.** Collapsing to one `ValidationError` means re-pointing ~37 message/type test assertions. Want the literal single class, or the subclass-umbrella?

Also confirm how far to push: should `validate_action` fully replace the schema rules in `_to_command` (leaving it build-only, ~double-iterating inline targets), and should `load_archetype`'s early check delegate to the same validator?

title: Make guards a deep module: parse/validate/register/run hooks in admin_lib/guards.py
description:
## Problem

Guard logic is spread across six sites in three modules. Adding a guard feature (defaults, composition, a new built-in) touches up to four files. Poor locality for one concept.

Current sites:

- `gen/manifest.py:301` — parse `[guards.<name>]` tables (validate run/fail, reject built-in collisions)
- `gen/archetypes.py:514` — parse `requires` on actions
- `gen/archetypes.py:548` — parse per-target `requires` (`target_requires`)
- `gen/archetypes.py:354` — audit: every `requires` name maps to a known guard
- `admin_lib/interp.py:601` — register shell guards
- `admin_lib/interp.py:554` — wrap actions with the guard check
- `admin_lib/guards.py:38,61` — `register_shell_guard()` + `run_requires()` (execute)

The parse/register/run phases are genuinely different points in the pipeline (parse at TOML-parse, register/run at runtime), so the call sites can't fully collapse — but the guard-specific **knowledge** can concentrate in one module.

## Decision (resolved)

**Full guard module with named hooks.** `admin_lib/guards.py` becomes the single home for all guard knowledge:

```
admin_lib/guards.py
  parse(toml_tables)   -> GuardDef[]          # [guards.*] + requires shapes
  validate(resolved)   -> raise on unknown name
  register(defs)       -> into runtime registry
  run(names)           -> fail-fast check (existing run_requires)
```

Each pipeline phase delegates exactly one call and holds **no** guard-specific logic:

- manifest parse  -> `guards.parse(...)`
- resolve/audit   -> `guards.validate(resolved)`
- interp register -> `guards.register(defs)`
- interp dispatch -> `guards.run(names)` (already the case via `run_requires`)

> After #406 everything is in `admin_lib/`, so this is intra-package — `guards.py` already lives there; manifest.py/archetypes.py/interp.py become siblings calling into it.

## Scope of work

- Move `[guards]` table parsing out of `manifest.py` into `guards.parse()`.
- Move `requires` / `target_requires` parsing + the unknown-name audit out of `archetypes.py` into `guards.parse()` / `guards.validate()`.
- Keep `run()` (rename of / wrapping `run_requires`) and `register_shell_guard` in place.
- Pipeline phases call the four hooks; built-in guard names (`git-clean`, `git-pushed`) stay defined in `guards.py` (today they're in `GUARDS_BUILTIN` in manifest.py — move the source of truth into `guards.py`).

## Wins

- Locality: all guard logic in one module
- A guard feature change touches one file
- Interface: four named hooks the pipeline calls

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `admin_lib/guards.py` exposes `parse / validate / register / run`.
- [ ] No guard-specific logic remains inline in `manifest.py` / `archetypes.py` / `interp.py` — each delegates one call.
- [ ] `GUARDS_BUILTIN` source of truth lives in `guards.py`.
- [ ] Existing guard behaviour unchanged (dynamic diagnostics for built-ins; captured output + static `fail` for shell guards).
- [ ] `tests/test_guards_manifest.py` + `tests/test_guards_runtime.py` updated/green; `./admin test` green.

## Sequencing

Best after #406 (frontend folded into `admin_lib/`), since it relocates guard parsing out of the frontend modules. See ADR-0005 for the existing guard design.

## Classification

**AFK** — design resolved (full guard module).

_Source: local architecture review (deepening candidate 03)._
