title: Fold the manifest frontend into admin_lib/ (retire the gen/ package)
description:
## Problem

After ADR-0006 (interpreter mode) the `gen/` package no longer generates anything except `compile` (the zipapp). The rest of `gen/` is the **manifest frontend** — parse, resolve, kind-metadata, `${VAR}` scan — yet the runtime engine `admin_lib/interp.py` reaches back **into** `gen/` for four helpers:

- `gen.archetypes._order_modules` (`interp.py:87`)
- `gen.manifest.SPACER` (`interp.py:579`)
- `gen.fragments._safe_ident` (`interp.py:637`)
- `gen.fragments.scan_env_vars` (`interp.py:652`)

The package name lies (a navigability problem: "gen" implies code generation that's gone), and a runtime module importing out of a package called "generator" reads as an inverted dependency.

## Decision (resolved)

**Fold the frontend into `admin_lib/` — one package, no `gen/`.**

```
admin_lib/
  manifest.py    (was gen/manifest.py     — parse)
  archetypes.py  (was gen/archetypes.py   — resolve / merge)
  kinds.py       (was gen/fragments.py    — kind metadata + scan_env_vars)
  detectors.py   (was gen/detectors.py)
  compile.py     (was gen/compile.py      — the one real generator)
  interp.py      (runtime; now imports siblings, no cross-package hop)
  ... existing admin_lib modules ...
```

The cross-package import that motivated this dissolves: `interp.py` imports siblings within `admin_lib`. The frontend-vs-runtime distinction stops being "two packages" and becomes module-level within one package.

> Naming note: `gen/fragments.py` is renamed `kinds.py` because what survives in it is the kind catalog/metadata, not "fragments" (rendering is gone). This is also the home for the unified kind registry in #403 — coordinate the two (see Sequencing).

## Scope of work

- Move `gen/manifest.py`, `gen/archetypes.py`, `gen/fragments.py` (→ `kinds.py`), `gen/detectors.py`, `gen/compile.py` into `admin_lib/`.
- Update all imports (`admin-run`, `interp.py`, tests, archetypes/detectors).
- Delete the `gen/` package + `gen/__init__.py`.

Note: the data dirs `archetypes/` and `detectors/` (the partial-manifest and heuristic files) are NOT part of `gen/` and do not move — only the `gen/` code package folds in.

### Migration: pickle path in compiled artifacts

`compile.py` pickles a `ResolvedManifest` that references `gen.manifest.Command` / `gen.archetypes.ResolvedManifest` (see `gen/compile.py:23-26`). Moving these modules **changes the pickle import path**, so `.pyz` artifacts compiled before this change will fail to unpickle. Acceptable (recompile fixes it), but: note it in the release/CHANGELOG and verify a fresh `admin compile` round-trips after the move.

### Docs drift to fix in the same change

The codegen-era docs are now wrong and should land with this move or they deepen the drift:

- `docs/architecture/design.md` — narrates the generator/render/bundle model.
- `docs/CONTEXT.md` — the **Bundler** and **Fragment** glossary terms describe rendering that no longer exists; the "Example dialogue" still tells contributors to "add a renderer in `gen/fragments.py`". Revise or remove.
- `CLAUDE.md` — repo-structure section names `gen/`.

## Wins

- Locality: the package name matches its job
- One package; no runtime→"generator" import
- Navigability: no "gen" misnomer for new readers (incl. AI)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gen/` removed; frontend modules live under `admin_lib/`.
- [ ] All imports updated; `admin-run`, `admin check`, `admin compile` all work.
- [ ] Fresh `admin compile` produces a working `.pyz` (pickle path verified).
- [ ] `design.md`, `CONTEXT.md` (Bundler/Fragment + example dialogue), `CLAUDE.md` updated.
- [ ] `./admin test` green.

## Sequencing

Keystone for #403, #407, #408 (all reference `admin_lib/` paths). Land this **first**, or do those directly in the new locations to avoid double-moving files. Overlaps with #403 specifically on `kinds.py`. #404 and #405 are independent of this move.

## Classification

**AFK** — design resolved (fold into `admin_lib/`).

_Source: local architecture review (deepening candidate 02)._

title: Enforce the archetype/detector pairing with a test
description:
## Problem

Archetypes (`archetypes/*.py`) and detectors (`detectors/*.py`) are paired **by filename only**. Nothing enforces that both halves exist. A detector that outlives its archetype will suggest an archetype name during `admin new`, then fail only later at resolve time with `ArchetypeError: unknown archetype` (`gen/archetypes.py:131`) — far from the edit that caused it.

## Current state

- 12 filename pairs, e.g. `archetypes/apple.py` <-> `detectors/apple.py`.
- Detectors run via `gen/detectors.py`; a detector returns a partial manifest naming an archetype.
- No code checks that a detected archetype name has a matching `archetypes/<name>.py` until `load_archetype()` tries to import it at resolve time.

```
detectors/apple.py ──▶ resolve() ──▶ missing archetypes/apple.py
  suggests "apple"     load_archetype   raises LATE (resolve time)
```

## Solution (AFK, cheap)

Add a test asserting the pairing holds in both directions:

- every `detectors/<name>.py` has a matching `archetypes/<name>.py`
- (and, if we want the contract symmetric) every `archetypes/<name>.py` that a detector can suggest exists

This fails at `./admin test` time — at the edit — instead of at a user's `admin new`.

## Noted alternative (out of scope here)

A deeper fix pairs archetype + detector behind one "stack" interface so the contract cannot half-exist structurally. That is a larger refactor; the test is the right first step and stands on its own regardless.

## Wins

- Fail at edit time, not at a user's resolve time
- Locality: the pairing contract is enforced in one place

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New test in `tests/` asserts the archetype/detector filename pairing.
- [ ] Test fails if either half is deleted; passes on current tree.
- [ ] `./admin test` green.

## Classification

**AFK** — test-only first step, no open design decision.

_Source: local architecture review (deepening candidate 06)._

title: Collapse log_columns_apple.py into log_columns.py (shallow file split)
description:
## Problem

`admin_lib/log_columns_apple.py` (87 lines) is a shallow split off `admin_lib/log_columns.py` (171 lines). It is one layout constant + two method overrides + import-time registration — not a real seam. Only one Apple adapter exists, so the file split buys nothing and adds an import + registration ceremony.

## Current state

- `admin_lib/log_columns.py` — `Column`, `ColumnFormatter`, `make_column_formatter()`; the generic `_reformat_generic_line()`.
- `admin_lib/log_columns_apple.py` — `APPLE_OS_LOG_NATIVE` constant, `AppleColumnFormatter` (overrides `format_line()`, adds `_reformat_apple_line()`), and a registration call at import time.

The Apple class is a **total override** — it does not reuse the base's `_reformat_generic_line()`. The only variation is (a) header detection waiting for the native `Timestamp...` header, and (b) fixed-width parsing via `APPLE_OS_LOG_NATIVE`. That is platform-specific *constant data* + two methods, not a behaviour that varies across a seam.

"One adapter = hypothetical seam. Two adapters = real seam." There is one Apple adapter — the file split is premature.

## Solution

Move `APPLE_OS_LOG_NATIVE` + `AppleColumnFormatter` + the registration into `log_columns.py`. Keep the **class** (it is a legitimate formatter variant); drop the **file** and the extra import.

Result: `log_columns.py` ~258 lines, one import, the Apple layout constant sitting beside its class.

## Watch out (verify during the change)

Apple formatter registration happens at import time and is wired through `KIND_MODULES` (`gen/fragments.py:52`) which auto-injects the apple log module for apple kinds. Confirm the formatter still registers when `log_columns` is imported — i.e. that collapsing does not change *when* registration fires for non-apple projects. If registration must stay conditional, gate it rather than re-splitting the file.

## Wins

- Delete one file + one import
- Locality: the Apple layout constant lives beside the class that uses it
- Removes a premature split

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AppleColumnFormatter` + `APPLE_OS_LOG_NATIVE` live in `log_columns.py`.
- [ ] `log_columns_apple.py` deleted; all imports updated (check `admin_lib/interp.py` and `gen/fragments.py` KIND_MODULES).
- [ ] Apple log formatting still works (registration fires).
- [ ] `tests/test_log_columns.py` updated/green; `./admin test` green.

## Classification

**AFK** — clear deletion test, no open design decision.

_Source: local architecture review (deepening candidate 04)._

title: Unify the action-kind catalog into one registry (kill the KNOWN_KINDS/_FACTORIES split)
description:
## Problem

A single action *kind* is declared in four separate places. A test plus a CLAUDE.md "hard rule" exist **only** to stop the four from drifting — classic shallow split. Adding a kind means editing two files in lockstep and trusting a sync test to catch a miss.

## Current state

A kind's definition is smeared across:

- `gen/fragments.py:30` — `KNOWN_KINDS` (frozenset of kind names)
- `gen/fragments.py:43` — `CONFIGLESS_KINDS` (subset that needs no `run`)
- `gen/fragments.py:52` — `KIND_MODULES` (kind → admin_lib modules to auto-inject)
- `admin_lib/interp.py:485` — `_FACTORIES` (the actual per-kind behaviour closures)

Kept from drifting by:

- `tests/test_interp.py::test_factories_cover_known_kinds` — asserts `set(_FACTORIES) == set(KNOWN_KINDS)`
- CLAUDE.md "Hard rules": *"A new action kind needs both a `KNOWN_KINDS` entry and an `interp._FACTORIES` factory."*

Consumers of the metadata vs the behaviour:

- `gen/archetypes.py:25` imports `KNOWN_KINDS`, `CONFIGLESS_KINDS`, `KIND_MODULES` for **resolve-time validation** (`gen/archetypes.py:483` raises `ArchetypeError` on unknown kind).
- `admin_lib/interp.py` uses `_FACTORIES` for **runtime dispatch**.

## Proposed shape

One `Kind` record per kind, in one registry:

```
Kind(name, configless: bool, modules: tuple[str, ...], factory)
```

- The resolver (`gen/archetypes.py`) reads names + flags + modules — metadata only.
- The interpreter reads the factory — behaviour only.

Two views of one source. Adding a kind = one entry.

### Before / After

```
BEFORE                                AFTER
one kind, four declarations           one Kind record
  KNOWN_KINDS      ┐                    Kind(name,
  CONFIGLESS       ├ gen/fragments.py     configless,
  KIND_MODULES     ┘                      modules,
  _FACTORIES        — interp.py           factory)
  + sync test + "hard rule"           drift structurally impossible
```

## Layering constraint (must hold)

The resolver must **not** import the runtime closures (that would make manifest validation depend on the interpreter). Keep the registry holding name + flags + modules **eagerly**, with the factory referenced **lazily** (or registered from `interp.py` into the same registry object) so the validation path never pulls in runtime code.

## Wins

- Adding a kind = one entry (leverage)
- Locality: one definition of a kind
- Delete `test_factories_cover_known_kinds`
- Retire the CLAUDE.md "hard rule" (drift becomes impossible, not policed)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A single source defines every kind's name, configless flag, and modules.
- [ ] `gen/archetypes.py` validates kinds against that source without importing `admin_lib/interp`.
- [ ] `admin_lib/interp.py` dispatches from that source.
- [ ] The sync test is removed (no longer expressible — there is nothing to drift).
- [ ] CLAUDE.md "Hard rules" updated to drop the two-places requirement.
- [ ] `./admin test` green.

## Classification

**AFK** — well-scoped, no open design decision.

_Source: local architecture review (deepening candidate 01)._

title: Spike: let admin pin tool/runtime versions (like mise/asdf)
description:
## Motivation

Right now `admin` is purely a task-runner front-end: it defines verbs (`dev`, `build`, `install`, …) and shells out to whatever per-project tool does the real work. Version management of the dev toolchain (zig, swiftformat, swiftlint, gh, xcodegen, …) is delegated entirely to a separate tool — in the macterm project that's `mise`'s `[tools]` table.

That leaves a gap: a project that wants `admin`'s uniform verbs **also** has to adopt a second tool (mise/asdf/etc.) just to pin tool versions. It'd be worth exploring whether `admin` can own that axis too, so a project can pin its toolchain in `admin.toml` and not need a second version manager.

## What to spike

Investigate adding tool/runtime version pinning to `admin`. Open questions to answer in the spike:

- **Surface.** A `[tools]` table in `admin.toml` (e.g. `zig = "0.15.2"`, `swiftformat = "latest"`)? Per-archetype defaults?
- **Backend.** Native install/resolve, or shell out to an existing resolver (mise/asdf) under the hood? Reusing mise as a library/CLI avoids reimplementing a plugin ecosystem.
- **Coexistence.** How does this interact with a project that already uses mise/asdf? Detect-and-defer vs. take-over vs. opt-in.
- **Activation.** How do pinned versions get onto `PATH` for the commands admin runs (and for an interactive shell)?
- **Scope creep.** Is this in `admin`'s remit (personal, cross-project task front-end), or does owning version management blur the line with mise? Document the tradeoff either way.

## Out of scope

Library/package dependency management (SPM, npm, cargo deps) — this is strictly about pinning the **dev tool/runtime** versions, the slice mise's `[tools]` covers.

## Reference

macterm pins its toolchain in `mise.toml` `[tools]` (gh/swiftformat/swiftlint/xcodegen/xcbeautify) + zig via the ghostty submodule. That's the concrete shape admin would be replacing/absorbing.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — unaffected by the rewrite, and one input changed in its favour. The spike question is unchanged: should admin own toolchain version pinning (a [tools] table) rather than sending every project to mise/asdf. What changed is that admin is now a single static Go binary installed with `go install`, so shipping a version-manager shim no longer has to answer 'how does this survive being bundled into a generated script'. Still a spike: investigate and recommend, do not implement.

title: Document the [apple] signing/prereq keys (sign_identity, mac_dev_rename, prebuild_cmd)
description:
The `[apple]` archetype has keys documented only in code docstrings:

- `sign_identity` — dynamic keychain identity selector: a case-insensitive substring matched against `security find-identity -v -p codesigning`; auto-picks a lone identity, ad-hoc on none/ambiguous. Lets dev builds sign with a stable identity (TCC grants persist) without a hardcoded hash.
- `mac_dev_rename` — set `false` to skip the `<name>Dev.app` rename/display-patch for projects that already differentiate their debug build at the Xcode level (distinct bundle id + CFBundleDisplayName).
- `prebuild_cmd` — shell command run before each build (e.g. project regeneration / dependency setup).

Add an `[apple]` schema reference so these are discoverable without reading admin_lib/apple.py.

Saw this because: migrating macterm to the apple archetype used all three keys, and there was no docs/archetypes/ doc listing the [apple] schema to update.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — the keys survived and are still undocumented for manifest authors. docs/architecture/lua-host-api.md documents the Lua BINDINGS (apple.sign, apple.resolve_signing_identity, apple.dev_macos_postprocess at :192-194), not the [apple] TABLE KEYS a project writes. sign_identity is still consumed as a keychain substring selector (internal/luahost/apple_darwin.go's ResolveSigningIdentity, bound per lua-host-api.md:192), and the sign-settings composition is internal/kinds/applesign_darwin.go. What is needed is unchanged: an [apple] schema reference listing every key with its meaning and default. Check mac_dev_rename's status while writing it — the mac dev-rename postprocessing it toggles is one of the documented unported gaps (internal/kinds/apple_darwin.go:14-21), so the key may currently do nothing.

title: poll_for_reload crashes on a non-tty stdin (termios.error)
description:
`poll_for_reload` (admin_lib/apple.py) calls `termios.tcgetattr(fd)` / `tty.setcbreak` on stdin to watch for the `r` reload keypress. When stdin isn't a tty — `admin dev` run piped, redirected, backgrounded, or under CI/log capture — `tcgetattr` raises `termios.error: (19, 'Operation not supported by device')`, which propagates and kills the dev command *after* a successful build + launch.

Fix: guard the termios setup; if stdin isn't a tty, fall back to watching only the SIGUSR1 reload signal + process exit (skip the keypress path) so `admin dev` still runs to completion non-interactively.

Saw this because: during a live `admin dev mac` verification (migrating macterm to the apple archetype), the build succeeded and the app launched, then the command crashed at admin_lib/apple.py:121 (`old_settings = termios.tcgetattr(fd)`) because the harness stdin was not a tty.

comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #400] @McBrideMusings at 2026-07-16T18:26:10Z:

Fixed: poll_for_reload now skips the termios/cbreak setup when stdin isn't a tty and watches only SIGUSR1 + process exit, so a piped/backgrounded/CI `admin dev` runs to completion instead of dying after a successful build and launch.

The function moved from admin_lib/apple.py to admin_lib/reload.py in the same pass — the reload flag, SIGUSR1 handler and pid-file plumbing were duplicated between docker.py and apple.py and now live in one module. It also picked up two new call sites (dev_loop_device, dev_loop_android), which widened the crash surface this was reported against.

title: Add a command to reconstruct admin.toml from a legacy generated ./admin
description:
Repos created under the old generator may have an empty, missing, or old-schema `admin.toml` with the real config living only inside a committed generated `./admin` (the old "bundles config inline" scheme), or commands using the pre-ADR-0003 inline-`run` shape. Under interpreter mode these can't run until `admin.toml` is reconstructed/migrated, and there is no tooling for it today (`docs/architecture/design.md` mentions a planned `--from-existing`).

Proposal: an `admin migrate` / `admin from-existing` verb that reads a legacy generated `./admin` (or an old-schema `admin.toml`) and emits a current commands/actions-split `admin.toml`.

Saw this because: the interpreter-mode cross-repo migration found ~8 repos that couldn't run the interpreter because their `admin.toml` was missing/empty/old-schema, requiring manual restoration of the committed `./admin` as a stopgap.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — this describes the generator/bundler architecture (admin-gen, gen/, the bundled ./admin, generator_commit, templates/), which was already replaced by interpreter mode (ADR-0006) and is now replaced again by the Go binary. None of the named code has a successor: `admin compile` is dropped by admin-3rgp.30, and there is no code-generation step left to audit, bundle or re-bundle. Same reconstruction problem, same moot cause.

title: admin_lib/cache.py NameError on bare _project_root under package import
description:
`_cache_dir()` in `admin_lib/cache.py` references a bare `_project_root`, but `cache.py` only imports `ok` from core — so that name resolved only in the old flat bundle's single namespace. Under interpreter mode (real package import) any code path through `cache.py` raises `NameError: name '_project_root' is not defined`.

Latent today (no shipped archetype imports `cache`), but it is the same reassignable/flat-namespace global class as the `LOG_DIR`/`LOG_FILE`/`_urls` accessor conversion done on the interpreter-mode branch.

Fix: add a `core.get_project_root()` accessor (mirroring `get_log_dir()`/`get_log_file()`/`get_urls()`) and use it in `cache.py`.

Saw this because: code-review of the interpreter-mode branch flagged `admin_lib/cache.py` (bare `_project_root`, ~line 32) as the same class of bug.

title: [inline] escape-file bodies don't re-sync reassignable core globals (stale LOG_FILE)
description:
Under interpreter mode (ADR-0006), `kind="python"` action bodies refresh the reassignable core globals (`LOG_DIR`/`LOG_FILE`/`LOG_CONFIG`/`_project_root`/`_urls`) per call via `_sync_core_globals` in `admin_lib/interp.py::_make_python`.

The `[inline]` escape file is different: it is `exec()`'d once into the build-time namespace in `register_all`, and the commands it registers close over that snapshot. They never refresh, so a bare `LOG_FILE` read in an `[inline]` body sees the pre-boot empty value. Same stale-reassignable-global class as #394, just via the inline `exec` path instead of a module value-import.

Fix options: route inline-registered commands through the same per-call `_sync_core_globals`, or document that `[inline]` bodies must use the `get_log_file()`/`get_log_dir()`/`get_urls()` accessors rather than bare globals.

Saw this because: during the interpreter-mode wrap-up review, `_sync_core_globals` was wired only into `_make_python._fn`, not the `exec(inline_body, ns)` path in `admin_lib/interp.py::register_all`.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — this is pytest-suite hygiene for tests/ and admin_lib/, both deleted by admin-3rgp.30. The Go suite (117 *_test.go files) is a fresh suite with none of the machinery named here. The [inline] block and kind="python" are both gone (internal/kinds/catalog.go:14-20), so there is no exec'd namespace holding a stale snapshot of reassignable globals.

title: [docker_run] --user drift is asymmetric: declaring user == image USER causes spurious target-only drift
description:
`_build_run_args_from_cfg` now renders `--user` whenever `cfg.user` is set. But the live-side drift normalizer `_live_argv_for_drift` strips `--user` from the live argv when it equals the image's baked user (`val == image_user`, ~docker.py:1166).

These two are asymmetric: if someone declares `user = "<image-user>"` in `[docker_run]` to be explicit, the cfg side emits `--user <image-user>` while the live side strips it, so a deploy reports a spurious `target has --user X / live missing` drift and refuses to deploy (or `--force` recreates pointlessly).

Harmless for the real Unraid case (99:100 ≠ the image's `appuser`), and gated behind a deliberately redundant declaration, but it's a latent footgun.

Options:
- Symmetric skip: have the cfg renderer omit `--user` when it equals the image user (requires fetching image user at render time, which the cfg path doesn't currently do — may not be worth it).
- Or just document the caveat on the `user` block.

Related to but narrower than #388 (full cfg/inspect schema parity).

Provenance: code review of the `--user` addition this session — `admin_lib/docker.py` `user` block in `_build_run_args_from_cfg` vs the `--user` strip in `_live_argv_for_drift`.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). FIXED BY THE PORT, and by exactly the symmetric skip this bead proposed. internal/dockerrun/drift.go:150 gates the whole live-side strip block on `!truthy(cfg[row.Key])`, so the `val == imageUser` strip at :157 only runs when [docker_run] does NOT declare `user`. Declaring user == the image's own USER now keeps --user on both sides, so no spurious target-only drift and no pointless --force recreate.

title: Add logs subcommand help documenting dev/live and --from format
description:
## Problem

The docker-unraid `logs` command is now a `dev`|`live` dispatcher with a `--from DD:HH:MM:SS` relative-offset flag (right-aligned, so partials like `02:00:00` work). None of this is discoverable from the CLI — there is no `subcommand_help` entry, so `./admin logs --help` shows nothing about targets or the `--from` format.

## Fix

Register a `subcommand_help` function for `logs` (or a generic mechanism for dispatcher commands) that documents:
- `./admin logs` — dev|live picker
- `./admin logs dev` — trail the newest local dev log
- `./admin logs live` — stream the deployed container's docker logs
- `--from DD:HH:MM:SS` — relative offset (days:hours:mins:secs ago), shows from that point then trails

Saw this because: pinning down the `--from` semantics took several rounds of back-and-forth this session precisely because the format is undocumented at the CLI.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — there is no `logs` command to document. No log tailer exists in Go and no logs verb is registered (cmd/root.go:202-207); [logs.*] sections parse (internal/manifest/logs.go) but nothing consumes them. The dev|live dispatch and the --from DD:HH:MM:SS relative-offset format are requirements for whoever ports the log reader — recorded on admin-d4ef and admin-ytun, which track that port — not a help string to add today.

title: tail_dev_log/_newest_log read import-time LOG_DIR instead of get_log_dir()
description:
## Problem

The new `tail_dev_log` and `_newest_log` helpers in `admin_lib/docker.py` read the module-level `LOG_DIR` name imported `from .core`, which is bound at import time (before `core._init()` sets it). In the flattened `./admin` bundle this is one shared global so it resolves fine; only the live-package import path is stale.

## Fix

Use `get_log_dir()` (added to core.py specifically for late-binding in package-import contexts) instead of the imported `LOG_DIR` in those two helpers.

## Notes

Consistency cleanup, not a regression — existing call sites (e.g. docker.py lines ~132/161/290) use bare `LOG_DIR` the same way.

Saw this because: code-review flagged it (severity ~15) while reviewing the logs dev/live dispatch changes.

title: Regenerate ignores the recorded generator_commit, bundling unrelated generator drift into downstream config edits
description:
## Problem

A generated `admin` records the generator it was built from (`set_generator_commit(...)` and the `@bundled ... generator_commit=<sha>` header), but `admin-gen --regenerate` regenerates from the *current* admin-project-tool working tree, not that recorded commit. So a downstream project that only wants to pick up its own small `admin.toml` edit cannot run a clean regen without also adopting whatever unrelated — and possibly uncommitted — changes exist in the generator since.

## Repro

In web-file-manager, `admin-gen --audit` reported drift where the committed `admin` (generator_commit `b9f6d0de`) would be regenerated by a newer `+dirty` tree (`700a7acf...+dirty`), pulling in an in-progress Docker-deploy refactor (`remote_recreate_container` rework, a new `_parse_env_file`, `[docker_run]` rendering) entirely unrelated to the project's config change. The SessionStart drift hook also reported "drift detected but auto-regeneration failed — run admin-gen manually." Net effect: the three config-derived spots in the generated `admin` (two command descriptions + the baked fixtures config) had to be hand-patched rather than regenerated, to avoid bundling the unrelated Docker work.

## Proposed direction

Either (a) honor the recorded `generator_commit` on regen — regenerate from that tree unless explicitly overridden — or (b) add a guard that refuses or loudly warns when the generator tree is dirty or ahead of the recorded commit, so a downstream regen can't silently absorb unrelated generator changes.

Saw this because: `admin-gen --audit` on web-file-manager showed a config-only intent vs a large unrelated Docker diff sourced from a `+dirty` generator; the bundled header records `generator_commit` but regen used a different tree.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #393] @McBrideMusings at 2026-06-22T12:39:35Z:

Obsolete under interpreter mode (ADR-0006), now merged to main. The regenerate path and generator_commit recording were removed — the tool interprets admin.toml at runtime and emits no vendored artifact, so there is no generator drift to bundle. compile is the only thing that emits a file, and it has no generator_commit.

title: setup_dev_mounts never prunes stale data/ symlinks when DEV_MOUNTS changes
description:
## Problem

`setup_dev_mounts` (`admin_lib/web_dev.py:59`) only adds or updates symlinks for the names currently in `DEV_MOUNTS`; it never removes symlinks under `data/` for names that are no longer present. When a project's `DEV_MOUNTS` changes — e.g. dropping `media`, `pierce`, `programs`, `storage` and keeping only one mount — the old symlinks persist in `data/`. Because the backend serves all of `data/`, those orphans keep appearing as top-level roots in the app.

## Repro

A web-file-manager project switched `DEV_MOUNTS` from four real-share mounts to a single fixtures mount. The four stale symlinks remained under `data/` across subsequent `./admin dev` runs and kept showing as roots, with no cleanup path other than manual `rm`.

## Proposed fix

On dev start, after creating the configured symlinks, remove any symlink directly under `data/` whose name isn't in the current `DEV_MOUNTS`. Prune only symlinks, never real files/dirs — reuse the existing "refuse to clobber non-symlinks" guard so a real directory is never deleted.

Saw this because: `admin_lib/web_dev.py:59` `setup_dev_mounts` adds/updates but never prunes; observed stale `data/` symlinks persisting as roots after `DEV_MOUNTS` was narrowed.

title: Stash-plugin detector only matches exact rollup.config.{js,mjs,ts} filenames
description:
`detectors/stash-plugin.py` looks for a rollup config under three exact filenames:

\`\`\`python
has_rollup = any(
    (project_dir / name).exists()
    for name in ("rollup.config.js", "rollup.config.mjs", "rollup.config.ts")
)
\`\`\`

This misses projects that split rollup config across named variants — e.g. `rollup.config.common.mjs`, `rollup.config.dev.mjs`, `rollup.config.prod.mjs`, `rollup.config.app.mjs` — which is the convention the Valkyr-JS Stash plugin template (and stash-reels itself, forked from it) ships with.

Suggested fix: glob `rollup.config*.{js,mjs,ts}` instead of the literal three names. Also worth thinking about whether the `"stash" in package.json` substring check is robust — a repo whose dependencies mention something stash-related but isn't a Stash plugin would false-positive — but that's a separate concern.

Saw this because: stash-reels (a Stash plugin project) didn't match this detector during bootstrap, only the fallback fired. The project has `rollup.config.common.mjs`, `rollup.config.dev.mjs`, `rollup.config.prod.mjs`, `rollup.config.app.mjs` — none of which match the three literal filenames the detector checks.

_parse_env_file strips surrounding quotes; docker --env-file keeps them
description:
## Problem

`_parse_env_file` in `admin_lib/docker.py` strips surrounding double or single quotes from values:

\`\`\`
FOO=\"bar baz\"   → parser yields FOO=bar baz
\`\`\`

Docker's `--env-file` does NOT do this — it injects the entire post-\`=\` string verbatim, so the live container would have \`FOO=\"bar baz\"\` (with literal quote chars in the value).

## Consequence

Currently latent: muxarr's \`[docker_run]\` no longer uses \`env_file\` (replaced with per-key \`[[docker_run.env]]\` entries). But the code path is wired and the function is called from `remote_recreate_container` when `target_cfg.env_file` is set. If any future project re-introduces \`env_file\` with target_cfg, two things break:

1. The rendered target argv has the wrong value.
2. Strict drift comparison will fire forever because target says \`FOO=bar baz\` and live says \`FOO=\"bar baz\"\`.

## Fix sketch

Match docker semantics — don't strip quotes. Or stop using \`_parse_env_file\` for drift comparison entirely and pass \`--env-file\` through to docker, then read the resulting Config.Env from inspect as the source of truth.

## Provenance

Saw this because: code-review of the drift detection module in \`admin_lib/docker.py\`.

title: Two functions must agree on the docker field list by hand, and they don't
description:
`admin diff` and the deploy drift check answer one question: does the container running on the server match what `admin.toml` says it should be. To answer it, admin turns each side into a `docker run` command line — the declared side with `_build_run_args_from_cfg` (`admin_lib/docker.py:752`), the live side with `_build_run_args_from_inspect` (`:1336`). Each function carries its own hand-written list of fields. Anything on the live list but not the declared list can never be declared, so it reports as a difference forever.

## What happens, with real values

Add `CAP_SYS_NICE` to a container through the Unraid web UI, then run `admin diff`:

| What admin reports | What is true |
|---|---|
| drift: `--cap-add CAP_SYS_NICE` present live, absent in `[docker_run]` | the container is configured exactly as intended |

Before `cap_add` was added to the declared side, there was no line you could write in `admin.toml` to make that go away. The drift report is permanently wrong, and a report that is always wrong stops being read.

## Why that is wrong

The drift check exists to answer "has someone changed this container behind my back". A field the declared side cannot express turns that answer into "yes, always" — the check reports a difference that no action can resolve.

## The state of the list today

Six fields the original filing listed as missing have since been added to `_build_run_args_from_cfg`: `cap_add`/`cap_drop` (`:943-946`), `privileged` (`:947`), `security_opt` (`:949`), `sysctls` (`:951`), `memory` (`:877`), `user` (`:896`). `anonymous_volumes` is emitted at `:808`.

Still missing from the declared side: `--add-host` (ExtraHosts), `tmpfs`, `group_add`, `ulimits`, `tty`/`open_stdin` (Tty/OpenStdin), `hostname`, `workdir` (WorkingDir), `mac_address`.

## The real problem is the arrangement, not the eight fields

Two functions have to agree about a list, and they are kept in agreement by a person remembering to edit both. They have already fallen out of agreement once. Adding eight more fields by hand is the same arrangement with a longer list, and the next field added to one side and not the other reproduces this issue exactly.

This is the third issue in this file from one rule being written more than once — #387 fixed the flag-pairing rule in `_argv_to_pair_set`, #468 found the same rule in `_live_argv_for_drift` and again in `remote_container_diff`. Here the duplicated thing is the field list itself.

## The fix: one table, both renderers read it

Decided 2026-08-11.

Introduce a single declarative table of docker fields — one entry per field, holding:

- the `[docker_run]` TOML key
- the `docker run` flag it emits
- how to read it out of `docker inspect` JSON (the path under `HostConfig`/`Config`)
- its shape: repeated flag (`--cap-add`), single value (`--memory`), boolean (`--privileged`), or key-value pair (`--sysctl`)

`_build_run_args_from_cfg` and `_build_run_args_from_inspect` both render from that table instead of each carrying its own branches. A new field becomes one row, and the two sides cannot disagree because there is only one list.

Put it next to `_BOOLEAN_FLAGS` (`admin_lib/docker.py:1117`) and `_argv_pair_at` (`:1120`) — the boolean-flag set is already a small version of exactly this table, and should be derived from it rather than sitting beside it as a second source of truth.

The eight missing fields are then eight rows, not eight pairs of hand-written branches.

**Alternatives rejected.** Adding the eight fields by hand and splitting them between schema fields and a tolerate-on-live allowlist was rejected: it restores parity today and loses it again at the next field, which is the thing this issue is actually about. An allowlist alone — teaching the drift check to ignore all eight — was rejected because it makes eight real container settings undeclarable, which is the same failure as the `cap_add` case above, just chosen deliberately.

## Scope note

Fields the image supplies rather than the operator choosing them — `workdir` and `mac_address` in particular — still need a row, but their row can mark them "compare only if declared", which is what `_live_argv_for_drift` already does for `WorkingDir` when it matches the image's own (`:1227`). That behaviour moves into the table rather than staying as a special case in the live renderer.

## Acceptance check

- The table exists and both renderers read from it; neither function contains a hand-written per-field branch for anything in the table.
- All eight missing fields are declarable in `[docker_run]` and round-trip: declaring a value renders the flag, and the same value read back from `docker inspect` renders the identical flag, so the drift comparison reports nothing.
- Existing tests in `tests/test_docker_run_args.py` and `tests/test_docker.py` pass unchanged — this is a refactor of how the argv is produced, not a change to what it contains for fields that already worked.
- Full suite green (`.venv/bin/pytest`, 861 at time of writing).

Type: AFK

title: _argv_to_pair_set mis-parses argv values that start with -
description:
## Problem

`_argv_to_pair_set` in `admin_lib/docker.py` detects flag-vs-value by checking whether the next argv element `startswith("-")`. Any flag value that legitimately starts with `-` is mis-classified as the next flag, silently dropping the original flag from the drift comparison.

Concrete cases:
- `--ulimit nofile=-1` — value is `nofile=-1`, starts with safe char, but a value of just `-1` (some ulimit forms) would.
- A future port spec, label, or env value whose value starts with `-`.

The drift check happily compares a missing pair against the actual live state and reports no drift — so the regression is invisible.

## Fix sketch

Either:
- Maintain a known-flag set with arity (e.g. `--privileged` takes no value, `--gpus` takes one) and pair according to that.
- Or use a pair-iterator that consumes argv with explicit knowledge of docker's flag schema.

## Provenance

Saw this because: code-review of the new TOML-canonical deploy path flagged it. Not currently biting because muxarr's `[docker_run]` produces no \`-\`-prefixed values, but the next consumer (or a future schema addition) will silently misbehave.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #387] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-10T23:03:03Z:

Fixed in ee28d05 (merged to main). _argv_to_pair_set no longer guesses flag-vs-value by checking whether the next token starts with a dash; it pairs every flag with the token after it except a closed set of zero-value flags (--privileged, -t, -i), which is all the two argv renderers in this file ever emit. The worker proved the bug before fixing it: reimplemented the old heuristic and ran both against the same argv — old code turned ['--ulimit', '-1'] into two bogus valueless entries, new code produces the single correct pair. Verified against a real local Docker container and its real docker inspect output driven through the production drift pipeline, not a synthetic fixture. Two regression tests in tests/test_docker.py; suite green at 860 after merge.

title: Validate archetype 'order' references at archetype load time
description:
Archetype `order` arrays can list command names that the archetype doesn't actually declare, and the regression isn't caught until a project resolves against the archetype. `archetypes/docker-unraid.py` had `"dev"` in its order with no `dev` command defined for an unknown duration; any project using docker-unraid alone hit the resolver's `order references unknown command 'dev'` guard.

**Fix shipped this session:** removed `"dev"` from docker-unraid's order (commit `b8f7c25`-adjacent). That restores `test_manifest_override_propagates_group_and_priority` to green.

**Underlying issue:** `load_archetype` (`gen/archetypes.py:130-170`) doesn't validate that every entry in `arch.order` is a key in `arch.commands`. The check only runs at project-resolve time (`gen/archetypes.py:285-300`), so a broken archetype ships and only breaks consumers.

**Proposed:** add a load-time check inside `load_archetype`:

```python
for entry in raw_order:
    if entry in ("", "---"):
        continue
    if entry not in data.get("commands", {}):
        raise ArchetypeError(
            f"{path}: order references unknown command '{entry}' "
            f"(known: {sorted(data.get('commands', {}))})"
        )
```

This makes the archetype's own boundary catch the regression, and the project-resolve check becomes a redundant defense-in-depth instead of the only line of defense. Sweep the other archetypes (`apple`, `hugo`, `rust-tauri`, etc.) once the check is in place to find similar latent drift.

Provenance: docker-unraid.py had this drift undetected; only the manifest-override test caught it, and only because that test happens to use docker-unraid as its archetype.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #386] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-10T22:58:54Z:

Fixed in 52c2c84 (merged as 07beb57). load_archetype in admin_lib/archetypes.py now raises ArchetypeError when a non-spacer entry in an archetype's order list is not a key in that archetype's own commands dict, so a broken archetype fails at its own boundary instead of only when a project resolves against it. Verified through the real CLI: a temp archetype with a stray order entry fails admin check with 'order references unknown command' and exit 1, while an archetype using the '---' spacer still passes. Swept all 14 archetypes for the same drift — zero hits. New regression test in tests/test_archetypes.py; suite green at 856 after merge. Note the issue body cites gen/archetypes.py, which no longer exists; the live file is admin_lib/archetypes.py.

title: gen/manifest.py dump() silently drops guards and requires fields
description:
`gen/manifest.py:dump()` was last touched before the guards/requires feature landed and has no emitter branch for `[guards.<name>]` tables or `requires` lists on actions/targets. The `Manifest.guards` field and per-action `meta["requires"]` / `meta["target_requires"]` are silently dropped on serialization.

**Current blast radius:** zero. The only callers today are tests and the bootstrap path in `admin-gen` (which writes empty starter manifests). No project is currently affected.

**Latent risk:** any future "rewrite admin.toml in place" feature, schema migration tool, or test that round-trips a guards-using manifest will silently lose data.

**Two options:**

1. Add emitter branches to `dump()` that handle `[guards.<name>]` tables and `requires` lists (parent-level + per-target overrides, including `requires = []` opt-out).
2. Rename `dump()` to `dump_starter()` or document explicitly that it only handles the starter-manifest shape and is not a general serializer. Add an `assert not manifest.guards` etc. so a misuse fails loudly instead of silently.

Either resolution is fine — the bug is the gap between what `dump()` looks like it does and what it actually preserves.

Provenance: noticed while implementing guards in commit `b8f7c25`. Confirmed `manifest.guards` and the action `requires` meta keys never reach the emitted TOML.

title: git-gate assumes the upstream is origin/<branch>
description:
## Problem

`git_gate` (`admin_lib/core.py`) hard-codes `origin/<current-branch>` as the upstream when checking "pushed". A branch that tracks a differently-named upstream (e.g. `upstream/main`, or `origin/<other-name>`) gets a false "not on origin" failure even when fully pushed.

## Provenance

`admin_lib/core.py` `git_gate()` — both `rev-parse --verify origin/<branch>` and `rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD` assume the remote ref is `origin/` + the current branch name. Surfaced during the code review of the git-gate feature.

## Options

- Resolve the branch's configured upstream from git config / `git for-each-ref --format='%(upstream:short)' refs/heads/<branch>` rather than hard-coding `origin/<branch>`.
- Keep the `origin/<branch>` convention and document it — this matches the convention that a branch's upstream should match its own name, so this may be WONTFIX. Filing for visibility.
close_reason: Fixed by admin-3rgp.10's Go guards port (4a5b95c) rather than ported forward. internal/guards/git.go resolves the branch's real @{upstream} instead of assuming origin/<branch>, and fetches that upstream immediately before comparing instead of trusting a stale remote-tracking ref. Regression tests: TestGitPushedGuardUsesConfiguredUpstreamNotOriginBranch and TestGitPushedGuardDetectsRemoteRewoundSinceLastFetch in internal/guards/git_test.go. NOTE: the Python admin_lib/guards.py still carries both bugs until admin-3rgp.30 deletes it.

title: git-gate 'pushed' check compares against a stale remote-tracking ref (no fetch)
description:
## Problem

`git_gate` (`admin_lib/core.py`) verifies a branch is pushed by running `git rev-list --count origin/<branch>..HEAD` against the **local** remote-tracking ref. It never fetches, so the comparison can be stale: if `origin/<branch>` advanced or was rewound elsewhere since the last fetch, the gate can report "pushed" against an out-of-date ref and let a deploy through that isn't actually current with the real remote.

## Provenance

`admin_lib/core.py` `git_gate()` — the `require_pushed` block runs `rev-parse --verify origin/<branch>` then `rev-list --count origin/<branch>..HEAD` with no preceding `git fetch`. Surfaced during the code review of the git-gate feature.

## Options

- `git fetch --quiet origin <branch>` before the rev-list — accurate, but adds network latency + a failure mode to every gated command (needs timeout/error handling).
- `git ls-remote origin <branch>` to compare the remote tip SHA without fetching objects — lighter, still a network call.
- Document the limitation (gate trusts the local tracking ref) and leave fetching to the user.

Trade-off: fetching makes every deploy/preview/staging command depend on the network; `ls-remote` is cheaper but still online. The "document only" option keeps the gate offline-fast at the cost of the stale-ref edge case.
close_reason: Fixed by admin-3rgp.10's Go guards port (4a5b95c) rather than ported forward. internal/guards/git.go resolves the branch's real @{upstream} instead of assuming origin/<branch>, and fetches that upstream immediately before comparing instead of trusting a stale remote-tracking ref. Regression tests: TestGitPushedGuardUsesConfiguredUpstreamNotOriginBranch and TestGitPushedGuardDetectsRemoteRewoundSinceLastFetch in internal/guards/git_test.go. NOTE: the Python admin_lib/guards.py still carries both bugs until admin-3rgp.30 deletes it.

title: Log bridge should work for multi-target sub-targets without requiring @action indirection
description:
## Problem

`[log_bridge]` only fires when an action is `kind = "interactive-shell"` — specifically inside `run_with_keybindings` in `admin_lib/keybindings.py`. Multi-target sub-targets that use `run = \"...\"` go through plain `run_cmd` and the bridge server is never started.

The only workaround is to split a sub-target into a separate `interactive-shell` action and reference it via `action = \"...\"`:

```toml
# Before (doesn't get log bridge):
[actions.dev.cf]
run = \"bun run dev:cf\"

# After (gets log bridge, but requires two extra stanzas):
[actions.dev.cf]
action = \"dev-cf\"

[actions.dev-cf]
kind = \"interactive-shell\"
run  = \"bun run dev:cf\"
```

That works, but it's boilerplate friction for something that should be transparent. The log bridge is useful for any long-running dev process that opens a browser — not only ones that happen to use `interactive-shell` as their top-level kind.

## Approaches to investigate

1. **Implicit interactive-shell for long-running sub-targets** — when `[log_bridge]` is configured and a multi-target sub-target uses `run`, automatically route it through `run_with_keybindings` instead of `run_cmd`. The `interactive-shell` vs plain-shell distinction inside sub-targets carries no meaningful difference to the user today.

2. **`pty = true` as a signal** — sub-targets already support `pty = true` to indicate an interactive process. Could treat `pty = true` as an implicit opt-in to `run_with_keybindings` (and thus the bridge) when `[log_bridge]` is configured.

3. **`interactive = true` on sub-targets** — the field is already parsed and stored in `meta["interactive"]` in `archetypes.py` but has no effect on sub-target dispatch. Could use it to select `run_with_keybindings` instead of `run_cmd`.

4. **Ambient bridge at the multi-target level** — start the log bridge once when a multi-target command is invoked, rather than per-action. Shutdown when the sub-target process exits. Most transparent ("just add `[log_bridge]` and it works everywhere") but needs care to avoid starting the bridge for short-lived sub-targets like `cf-reset`.

## Current workaround

Use `action = \"...\"` dispatch on sub-targets that need the bridge, pointing to standalone `interactive-shell` actions. This is functional but feels pedantic given the goal.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — inherited. The bridge is started in exactly one place, internal/keybindings/keybindings_unix.go:208-210, and the only thing that builds a logbridge.Config is internal/kinds/interactiveshell.go:36-64. A multi-target sub-target declaring `run = "..."` goes through the shell path and never starts a bridge, so the @action indirection workaround this bead documents is still the only way.

title: hugo detector misses Hugo projects in a subdirectory
description:
## Context
`detectors/hugo.py` matches a Hugo project only when `config.*` + `themes/` (or the build lock) exist at the repo root. The `hugo` archetype is now `${HUGO_SOURCE}`-aware and supports a Hugo project living in a subdirectory, but the detector can't find one — so a monorepo (e.g. Hugo under `site/`) requires adding the archetype to `admin.toml` by hand.

## Proposal
Extend `detectors/hugo.py` to also probe common subdirs (e.g. `site/`, `www/`, `web/`) one level down, and surface `HUGO_SOURCE` guidance when matched. Related to #342 (tauri detector depth hardcoded).

Saw this because: wedding's Hugo lives in `site/`; bootstrap detection would miss it even though the archetype now supports it via `${HUGO_SOURCE}`.

title: Move vite-dev web_dev injection to KIND_MODULES
description:
`render.py:68–71` still has a manual `if any(c.kind == "vite-dev")` block that pre-dates the KIND_MODULES general loop added in 48d2f91. Adding `"vite-dev": ["web_dev"]` to `KIND_MODULES` in `gen/fragments.py` and removing the manual block would make module injection fully consistent — every kind that needs extra modules would declare them in one place.

Saw this because: the KIND_MODULES loop was added directly below the vite-dev block; it now handles every other kind automatically but vite-dev is still wired manually above it.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — this describes the generator/bundler architecture (admin-gen, gen/, the bundled ./admin, generator_commit, templates/), which was already replaced by interpreter mode (ADR-0006) and is now replaced again by the Go binary. None of the named code has a successor: `admin compile` is dropped by admin-3rgp.30, and there is no code-generation step left to audit, bundle or re-bundle. gen/fragments.KIND_MODULES no longer exists; the Go kind catalog (internal/kinds/catalog.go) declares each kind once and factories.go registers one factory per entry, with an import-time check that the two can't drift.

title: Rename require_python_311 to require_python_min
description:
`gen/manifest.py:561` defines `require_python_311()` which now checks `>= 3.9` (updated in the Python 3.9 tomli backport). The name is actively misleading — a future contributor reading it will assume it enforces 3.11.

Its only caller is `admin-gen:41` (import) and `admin-gen:496` (call). Renaming to `require_python_min` and updating those two lines is a 3-line change.

The "name kept for back-compat" docstring comment is also wrong — there's nothing to be back-compat with since `admin-gen` is the sole caller.

title: Two pre-existing test failures not tracked as issues
description:
`./admin test` has two consistently failing tests that predate this repo's pytest migration and have no open issue:

- `tests/test_archetypes.py::test_manifest_override_propagates_group_and_priority`
- `tests/test_log_server.py::test_log_endpoint_appends_to_log_file` — `{'written': 3} != {'written': 2}`

Both fail on the clean tree (verified via git stash). They show up in every CI run and will mislead contributors reading test output.

Each probably warrants its own investigation, but filing together since neither has any tracking.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — this is pytest-suite hygiene for tests/ and admin_lib/, both deleted by admin-3rgp.30. The Go suite (117 *_test.go files) is a fresh suite with none of the machinery named here. Both failing tests are in the deleted Python suite (tests/test_archetypes.py, tests/test_log_server.py).

title: Move _log_bridge_allocate_port into ports.py as find_free_port(port_range)
description:
It's a general port utility that belongs with the rest of the port management code, not buried as a private function in `log_bridge.py`.

Saw this because: `admin_lib/ports.py` already owns all other port detection/allocation logic; the new function is an island in an unrelated module.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, WITH A CAVEAT WORTH DECIDING ON. The island survived: port allocation for the bridge is a private bindFreePort inside internal/logbridge/logbridge.go:245 (with DefaultPortRangeStart/End at :41-42 and the per-project override resolved at :69-72), while internal/ports owns every other port-related helper — PortFree, PortHolders, PreflightPort, WaitForPort (internal/ports/ports.go:107,142,283,340). The caveat: the Go version does not return a port number, it returns a bound net.Listener plus the port, which closes the check-then-bind race a plain find_free_port(range) would reopen. So if this moves, move it as `ports.BindFreePort(start, end) (net.Listener, int, error)` — don't reduce it to the find_free_port signature this bead originally proposed.

title: _log_bridge_allocate_port has a probe-then-bind race
description:
The function probes by binding then immediately releasing each port inside a `with` block. Between the probe closing and `ThreadingHTTPServer` binding for real, another process can snatch the port. Fix: bind to port 0 and read back `server_address[1]`, which is the same approach the test fixture already uses.

Saw this because: `admin_lib/log_bridge.py:38-50`; `tests/test_log_server.py:84` does it the right way with `port=0`.

title: [log_bridge].port_range validation doesn't check TCP bounds
description:
Values like `[0, 1]` or `[70000, 70010]` pass manifest validation and produce a confusing `OSError` at runtime instead of a clear `ManifestError`. Add a `1 <= start` and `end <= 65535` guard.

Saw this because: `gen/manifest.py:262-268` only checks `isinstance` and `start < end`; no port-range bounds check.

title: ensure_docker_template is redundant when [docker_run] is declared
description:
On every `./admin deploy` (non-dry-run), `ensure_docker_template()` scp's `deploy/unraid-template.xml` to `/boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user/my-<name>.xml`. The point of installing the template was to let users bootstrap the first container via the Unraid Docker GUI.

When `[docker_run]` is declared, first-deploy already creates the container directly via `_create_container_from_cfg` — the GUI template bootstrap is bypassed. The scp still runs and writes a file the user may never use.

Options:
- Skip `ensure_docker_template` when `_DOCKER_RUN_CONFIG` is present.
- Keep it but downgrade severity (warn-only on missing XML; no per-deploy scp once installed).
- Drop `ensure_docker_template` entirely once #<this-pr-template-gen-issue-number> lands and the XML is generated from the same source.

Probably depends on the unraid-template.xml generation issue — if templates become a derivative artifact, this becomes a non-question.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — both halves survived the port, so the redundancy does too. install-template is a first-class kind (internal/kinds/installtemplate.go, with installtemplate_test.go) that scp's the template to the Unraid host, and [docker_run] container creation is internal/dockerrun/provision.go. The question is unchanged: when [docker_run] is declared, first deploy creates the container directly and the GUI-template bootstrap is bypassed, yet the scp still runs every time. Still coupled to admin-g8aw — if the XML becomes derived, this decides itself.

title: ./admin diff: compare live container against declared [docker_run], not just last-deploy snapshot
description:
Currently `./admin diff` compares the live container's run config to `/tmp/<container>-lastdeploy.json` (a snapshot written at the end of each deploy). That catches drift between deploys but lets the declared `[docker_run]` table silently fall out of sync — e.g. someone tweaks a mount in the Unraid GUI, `./admin deploy` preserves it on the next push, and the toml never gets updated.

Add a third axis: live vs declared `[docker_run]`. `./admin diff` should report drift across all three states:
- declared (admin.toml `[docker_run]`) — desired config
- last-deploy snapshot (`/tmp/<container>-lastdeploy.json`) — what we last shipped
- live container (`docker inspect`) — what's running

Three-way diff helps distinguish:
- GUI tweak someone forgot to land back in toml: declared != live, but last-deploy == live (so the tweak happened pre-deploy and was preserved).
- Drift since last deploy (someone edited the container manually since): last-deploy != live.
- Toml change not yet deployed: declared != last-deploy, live matches one or the other.

UX: keep the current two-way default, add a flag (`./admin diff --declared`) or surface all three by default and use color/columns to disambiguate.
close_reason: Fixed by admin-3rgp.37's docker.deploy/docker.diff port (e7d00f8), rather than ported forward. admin-9bex: internal/dockerrun.BuildDeploySyncPlan is now the ONLY [deploy]-sync implementation, so there is no second path to silently drop post_sync or chown; verified for real with a local sync where post_sync fired and created its marker file, and --chown rendering is mutation-proven. admin-dbmj: diff now reports three axes — declared/live, last-deploy/live, and declared/last-deploy — verified with a simulated manual port change. admin-wxz0: every -e value is masked in both text and --format json output on all three axes, verified with a real secret-rotation scenario. admin-fr0e was deliberately left untouched and not made worse. NOTE: the Python admin_lib still carries these bugs until admin-3rgp.30 deletes it.

title: Generate deploy/unraid-template.xml from [docker_run] table
description:
Today the Unraid Docker template XML is hand-written at `deploy/unraid-template.xml` and `ensure_docker_template()` scp's it to the target. The XML duplicates what `[docker_run]` already declares (mounts, ports, env, devices, GPU). Two sources of truth drift; nothing enforces alignment.

Goal: `admin.toml` is the single source of truth. Either generate the XML at admin-gen time (deterministic, checked-in) or render it on demand during `ensure_docker_template()` and skip the file altogether.

Schema gaps to bridge before generation works:
- Unraid template `Display="always"|"advanced"` / `Required="true"|"false"` / `Mask="true"|"false"` have no `[docker_run]` equivalent. Either add optional fields per env / mount, or pick sane defaults (Required=true for binds, Mask=true for env names matching `*_KEY` / `*_PASSWORD` / `*_TOKEN`).
- `<WebUI>` and `<Support>` URLs aren't in `[docker_run]`. Could read `[urls].prod` for WebUI; `<Support>` could be derived from the git remote.
- `<Overview>` and `<Icon>` are template-specific — add as optional top-level fields on `[docker_run]` (e.g. `overview`, `icon_url`).

Validate by rendering both Recodarr and one other docker-unraid project's template, diffing against the hand-written XML, and reviewing remaining differences.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, AND THE PORT MADE IT EASIER. The duplication is unchanged: deploy/unraid-template.xml is hand-written and install-template scp's it (internal/kinds/installtemplate.go) while [docker_run] declares the same mounts, ports, env, devices and GPU. What is new is that [docker_run] now has a declarative field table — internal/dockerrun/fieldtable.go maps each key to its flag, shape, section and inspect key — which is exactly the source a generator would walk, instead of the 121-line if-chain this would have had to mirror before. The schema gaps the bead lists (Display/Required/Mask, WebUI, Support) are still gaps.

title: optional_mounts read paths from the machine you type on, then mount them on the server
description:
An optional mount names an environment variable instead of a path, so the path can differ per machine. On a deploy to a remote server, admin reads that variable on the machine running the command and hands the result to the docker daemon on the target — which needs a path that exists over there.

## What happens, with real values

```toml
[[docker_run.optional_mounts]]
env       = "MOUNT_MEDIA"
container = "/media"
```

Deploying from a laptop where `MOUNT_MEDIA=/Users/pierce/Media` to a server whose media lives at `/mnt/user/media`:

| What admin tells the server to mount | What the server needed |
|---|---|
| `-v /Users/pierce/Media:/media` | `-v /mnt/user/media:/media` |

The server has no `/Users/pierce/Media`, so docker creates an empty directory at that path and mounts nothing useful. The container starts and its media directory is empty.

The other half is worse, because it is silent. `admin_lib/docker.py:800-803`:

```python
host = env_vars.get(env, "").strip()
if not host:
    continue
```

If the variable is unset on the deploy machine, the mount is dropped with no message at all. The container comes up missing a volume and nothing anywhere says so.

## Why that is wrong

A path only means something on one machine. Reading it on machine A and using it on machine B is reading the wrong machine's answer — the value is not wrong in itself, it is being asked of the wrong computer.

## The lines that cause it

`admin_lib/docker.py:796-805` renders the mounts. It gets its values from `_build_run_args_from_cfg`'s `env_vars` argument (`:752`), and `remote_recreate_container` calls it at `:520` without passing one — so it defaults to `os.environ` of whatever machine is running admin. `bind_mounts` whose `host` contains a `${VAR}` reference has the same problem one block up at `:790`.

## Who it hurts and when

Any project deploying a container to a remote host with `optional_mounts` or a `${VAR}`-bearing `bind_mounts` entry, whenever the deploy is run from anywhere other than the target itself. It has not bitten yet because deploys have been running with `DEPLOY_LOCAL=true`, where the two machines are the same one — but the docker archetype fully supports genuine ssh deploys today (`admin_lib/remote.py:_is_local_host`, `admin_lib/docker.py:_docker_argv`), so it is one deploy-from-a-laptop away.

## The fix: read the values on the machine they describe

Decided 2026-08-11.

1. **New `[docker_run]` key: `remote_env_file`** — an absolute path on the *target*, e.g. `/boot/config/admin.env`. Before rendering argv for a non-local deploy, `remote_recreate_container` reads that file over ssh (`admin_lib/remote.py:ssh_cmd` with `cat`), parses it with the same rules as `_parse_env_file` (`admin_lib/docker.py:412` — KEY=value, `#` comments, quotes preserved verbatim), and passes the result as `_build_run_args_from_cfg`'s `env_vars`. The path is then read on the machine it exists on.
2. **No `remote_env_file` on a non-local deploy is an error, not a guess.** If the deploy is remote and the config has any `optional_mounts` entry or any `bind_mounts` host containing `${`, stop before creating the container: name the variable, say it would have been read on the deploy machine, and point at `remote_env_file`. Never fall back to local `os.environ` for a remote deploy.
3. **A variable missing from `remote_env_file` still skips the mount silently** — that is what "optional" means, and it is correct once the file being consulted is the target's own. Local deploys (`DEPLOY_LOCAL=true` / `_is_local_host`) keep reading `os.environ` exactly as today.

**Alternative rejected.** The issue proposed a per-mount `host_path` field holding the target's path directly. That cannot work here: a real path like `/mnt/user/media` must not be written into a committed file, so `host_path` would hold `${MOUNT_MEDIA}` and be read on the deploy machine again — the same bug with an extra field. Resolving over a plain `ssh host printenv MOUNT_MEDIA` was also rejected: a non-interactive ssh session does not read the target user's `.profile` or `.zshrc`, so the variable is usually empty and the silent-skip path swallows it.

## Acceptance check

- `tests/test_docker_run_args.py` / `tests/test_docker.py`: `_build_run_args_from_cfg` renders `-v` from a caller-supplied `env_vars` dict rather than `os.environ`; a remote deploy with `optional_mounts` and no `remote_env_file` raises with the variable named; a remote deploy with `remote_env_file` renders the target's value; a local deploy is unchanged; a variable absent from `remote_env_file` skips its mount.
- Document `remote_env_file` in the `[docker_run]` schema docstring at `admin_lib/docker.py:150-174`.
- Full suite green (`.venv/bin/pytest`).

Type: AFK

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #371] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-11T16:18:40Z:

Fixed in 0dd3fc4 + 83c74cf (merged to main). New [docker_run].remote_env_file key: on a non-local deploy admin reads it over ssh (_read_remote_env_file, sharing _parse_env_text with the existing local parser) and resolves optional_mounts and ${}-bearing bind_mounts host paths from the target's own values. A non-local deploy that needs such a path and declares no remote_env_file is refused before the container is touched, with the variable named. Local deploys are unchanged. 9 new tests plus one more described below; suite 880 after merge.

One correction made at landing, not by the worker. Point 1 of the plan routes every ${VAR} through the single env_vars dial, which meant a remote deploy with no env-dependent mount resolved everything against an empty dict — so an env value, a label, a port, or the health-check URL lost its substitution. _build_run_args_from_cfg warns and skips an unresolved ${VAR}, so it fails quietly: for {name = "API_KEY", value = "${API_KEY}"} the rendered command dropped the -e flag entirely and the container would have started without its key. Verified by test — with the empty dict the argv is 'docker run -d --name X myimage', with the fix it carries the flag. Values now resolve from os.environ as before; only paths come from the target. Regression test test_remote_deploy_without_mounts_still_resolves_env_values_locally, confirmed red before and green after.

Two notes from the worker worth keeping: the issue cited admin_lib/docker.py:150-174 as the [docker_run] schema docstring, but that range documents [docker_dev] and no [docker_run] schema docstring exists — remote_env_file is documented on remote_recreate_container instead. And no second machine exists here, so the remote path was driven at the function boundary with the ssh call intercepted, never by pointing at localhost, which _is_local_host would have classified as local. A real cross-machine deploy is still an unperformed confirmation.

title: [docker_run] env_file emitted as bare path breaks on remote ssh deploy
description:
In `_render_docker_run_argv` (admin_lib/docker.py), an `env_file = ".env"` value is emitted as `--env-file .env` and existence-checked against the local cwd. On a remote ssh deploy the docker daemon on the target resolves it relative to the ssh user's home, where it doesn't exist. Container creation will fail (or run with no env vars depending on docker version).

Currently latent because all Recodarr deploys use DEPLOY_LOCAL=true. Hits as soon as someone deploys from a non-target machine.

Fix options:
- scp the env_file to a known remote location before launching docker run and use the absolute remote path
- Inline the env_file as `-e KEY=VALUE` flags read from the local file (lossy: comments / shell expansion lost, but predictable)
- Refuse relative env_file paths in remote mode with a clear error

Counterpart to the dev path (line 504-507 in docker.py) which defers the existence check into a shell conditional run on the docker daemon's host.

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #370] @McBrideMusings at 2026-08-11T15:17:36Z:

Already fixed — closing as stale rather than picking one of the three options in the body.

The mechanism this issue describes is gone from the deploy path. remote_recreate_container parses the env file on the local machine (admin_lib/docker.py:518-520 via _parse_env_file at :412) and merges its contents into the argv as -e NAME=VALUE flags (:859-865). Nothing hands a bare --env-file path to the remote daemon, so there is no path for it to resolve against the ssh user's home.

A bare --env-file survives only at admin_lib/docker.py:294, inside _docker_dev_build_cmd — the docker-dev path, which talks to the local daemon and never crosses ssh, so the remote mismatch this issue is about cannot arise there.

Two stale citations for the record: _render_docker_run_argv does not exist (the function is now _build_run_args_from_cfg at :752), and the 'counterpart to the dev path (line 504-507)' is now at :291-294.

Sibling issue #371 covers the still-live case of the same class — optional_mounts resolving env vars on the deploy machine and mounting them on the target.

title: Wire VitePress docs preview into the admin runner
description:
## Context

The bootstrap session created `docs/.vitepress/config.mts`, `docs/index.md`, and section index pages, but didn't wire VitePress into `admin.toml`. A contributor cloning the repo today has no documented path to preview the docs locally — they'd have to reverse-engineer the npm setup from `package.json` (which doesn't exist yet) or the VitePress docs.

## Proposed work

1. Add a `[commands.docs]` block to `admin.toml` and a matching `[actions.docs]` (`kind = "shell"`, `run = "npx vitepress dev docs"`).
2. Decide on the bootstrap story for the npm side:
   - **Option A:** check in a minimal `package.json` with VitePress as a devDependency. Pros: one-step `npm i && ./admin docs`. Cons: introduces node tooling at the repo root.
   - **Option B:** add an `[actions.docs-install]` that runs `npm init -y && npm i -D vitepress` once, and document the two-step flow in CLAUDE.md / docs/development/.
3. Regenerate `./admin` so the new command appears in the TUI.
4. Update `docs/development/index.md` (and/or root `CLAUDE.md`) to document the preview workflow under "Common workflows".

## Acceptance

- `./admin docs` (or equivalent) starts the VitePress dev server.
- A new contributor can preview docs without consulting external VitePress documentation.

## Provenance

Surfaced by `/wrap-up` after the bootstrap session created the docs scaffold (commit 369752e) but left the preview path undocumented. Friction predicted: the next time the user wants to preview docs, they'll hit the same gap.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — narrowed to one wiring step. The tool now HAS the capability: kind="docs" is in the catalog (internal/kinds/catalog.go, implemented at internal/kinds/docs.go) and there is a docs archetype with a detector that recognises a docs:dev script in package.json or docs/package.json (internal/detect/detectors.go:344-372). What is missing is this repo's own wiring: admin.toml has no docs command — its only 'docs' line is :81, a Go spike runner. So option A vs option B in the bead is still the open question, but only for this repo. Doing it would also exercise the docs archetype against a real project.

title: Audit admin_lib/ and friends for third-party imports beyond icons.py
description:
## Context

[ADR-0001](../blob/main/docs/adr/0001-stdlib-only.md) documents a carve-out for try/except-guarded third-party imports and asserts:

> Today the only such module is `admin_lib/icons.py`, which uses `Pillow` and `cairosvg` for icon generation…

The code-review pass that surfaced `admin_lib/icons.py` was scoped to verifying the ADR's claim, **not** exhaustively sweeping the codebase. If more such modules exist anywhere in `admin_lib/`, `gen/`, `archetypes/`, or `detectors/`, the ADR's "today the only such module" sentence is wrong as written.

## Proposed work

1. Grep for try/except-guarded third-party imports across the tree:
   ```bash
   grep -rPn '^\s*try:\s*$' admin_lib/ gen/ archetypes/ detectors/ admin-gen | \
     while read m; do grep -A2 "$m" "${m%%:*}" | grep -E 'from |import '; done
   ```
   Filter out stdlib targets (`from .core import …`, etc.). Anything left is an unrecorded optional dep.
2. For each finding:
   - **Keep it:** extend ADR-0001's carve-out clause to name the module explicitly.
   - **Remove it:** drop the import and reduce the module's functionality if it was already optional.

## Acceptance

- ADR-0001's "today the only such module" sentence either lists *every* such module by name, or remains accurate because there is genuinely only one.
- No silent third-party dep lurking in the tree contradicts the stdlib-only stance.

## Provenance

Surfaced by `/wrap-up` code-review pass against `docs/adr/0001-stdlib-only.md:3` after the absolutist "no third-party imports anywhere" claim was caught and softened. Fix landed in commit 369752e but the sweep is outstanding.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — this is pytest-suite hygiene for tests/ and admin_lib/, both deleted by admin-3rgp.30. The Go suite (117 *_test.go files) is a fresh suite with none of the machinery named here. ADR-0001 (stdlib-only) is superseded by admin-3rgp.30, so its 'today the only such module is icons.py' sentence has nothing to be wrong about. The Go binary vendors its dependencies through go.mod.

title: Migrate tests from plain scripts to pytest
description:
## Problem

Tests currently run as plain `python3 tests/test_X.py` scripts with `if __name__ == "__main__":` blocks dispatching test functions manually. `tests/conftest.py` exists as a regular module holding a `make_command()` factory — it is **not** pytest config.

This pattern is not a deliberate decision — it's an accident of the project's history. It produces real friction:

- New test authors reach for pytest fixtures / `@parametrize` and have to rewrite their drafts to fit the manual-loop pattern.
- Every new test file must be added by hand to the `[actions.test]` list in `admin.toml` — there's no glob.
- Failure output is whatever the test happens to print; there's no standard summary, no `-k` selector, no `-x` fail-fast, no `--lf`.
- `conftest.py` is misleading — its name implies pytest config but it's just a module.

`pytest` doesn't violate the stdlib-only rule (ADR-0001) — that rule applies to the generator and to the bundled `admin_lib/` that ships into generated `./admin` scripts. Tests are dev-only and never get bundled.

## Proposed work

1. Add `pytest` as a dev dependency (`requirements-dev.txt` or `pyproject.toml`'s `[project.optional-dependencies]`, whichever fits the project's evolving setup).
2. Convert each `tests/test_*.py`:
   - Replace `def test_foo(): ... assert` blocks (they mostly already match pytest's discovery rules — verify and tidy).
   - Promote `tests/conftest.py`'s `make_command()` to a proper `@pytest.fixture`.
   - Where manual loops exist, port them to `@pytest.mark.parametrize`.
   - Drop the `if __name__ == "__main__":` dispatch tails.
3. Replace `[actions.test]`'s Python body with a single `pytest tests/` shell action.
4. Update `CLAUDE.md` and the docs to remove the "not pytest" framing.
5. Verify `./admin test` still passes via the new runner.

## Out of scope

- The bundled `admin_lib/` and generated `./admin` keep the stdlib-only rule (per ADR-0001). pytest is a dev-time dep only.

## Acceptance

- `./admin test` runs `pytest tests/` and produces standard pytest output.
- All existing test cases pass.
- No more manual test-script registration in `admin.toml`.
