Pytest migration landed: pytest.ini added with pythonpath setting, requirements-dev.txt with pytest dep, conftest.py stripped to a docstring (make_command was dead code), and all test_*.py files updated to drop manual sys.path manipulation. Auto-discovery works — no manual registration in admin.toml needed.

title: docker-dev kind has no user-facing documentation
description:
## Problem

The `docker-dev` action kind (five commits from `9973564` → `dee6db6`) ships a non-trivial config schema and has no documentation outside the source. The supported `[docker_dev]` fields:

- `image_tag` (required)
- `build_context` (default `.`)
- `target` — multi-stage build target
- `container_name`
- `gpu` — `true` | `"all"` | `["device=0", ...]` | string
- `env_file` — emitted as `--env-file` when the file exists at run time
- `pre_kill` — call `cmd_kill` first
- `ports[]` — `{ host, container }`
- `bind_mounts[]` — `{ host, container, mode?, mkdir? }` (relative `host` resolves against `host_root` or cwd)
- `anonymous_volumes[]` — `{ path }` or bare string; masks subpaths of a bind mount
- `optional_mounts[]` — `{ env, container, mode? }`; skipped silently when env var unset
- `env[]` — `{ name, value }` (also accepts no value → forward from host env)
- `devices[]` — `{ host, container? }`; emits `--device` (cgroup-registered, unlike `-v`)
- `host_root` — overrides where relative bind-mount paths resolve (socket-mounted-daemon scenarios)

The only working example is recodarr's `admin.toml` (extensively commented, but not discoverable from this repo).

## What needs to happen

1. README section or a dedicated `docs/kinds/docker-dev.md` that:
   - Documents each field with type + default + when to use it
   - Shows minimal example (just `image_tag` + `ports`)
   - Shows realistic example (gpu, env_file, bind_mounts, optional_mounts)
   - Shows the hot-reload dev pattern (target + bind_mounts of source + anonymous_volumes on node_modules)
   - Explains the `host_root` use case (Docker daemon on a different host than where admin runs — e.g. socket mounted into a dev container from the production daemon)
2. Cross-link from the existing `docker-reload-loop` docs (if any) since the two share `run_with_reload`.

## Provenance

While filling in recodarr's `[docker_dev]` table I kept jumping back to `_docker_dev_build_cmd()` in `admin_lib/docker.py` to remember field names — there's nothing else to read. Recodarr's toml has all the right comments, but a user adopting this kind in a new project has no signpost to it.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — the kind survived, the docs never existed. `docker-dev` is in the Go catalog (internal/kinds/catalog.go) implemented at internal/kinds/dockerdevcmd.go, and the [docker_dev] schema this bead enumerates is still documented nowhere outside the source. Same ask, new file to read it out of. Ties into admin-k6v5 (no kinds catalog at all) — doing that catalog well probably subsumes this.

title: Add test coverage for forge-engine workspace dev path
description:
The `forge-engine` archetype's new workspace path (sample folders containing `forge.workspace.toml` instead of `main.lua`) shipped without tests. `tests/test_archetypes.py` has no fixture exercising:

- workspace vs. game discovery in `_DISCOVER_PY` (the `_kind` branching and `_pick_sample` return shape)
- `_workspace_projects` glob expansion (including the empty-result paths and TOML parse failure)
- the parallel-launch exit-code aggregation in `_DEV_PY` (worst-rc propagation, KeyboardInterrupt cleanup)

Add a sample workspace fixture plus tests covering these three areas.

Saw this because: `grep -l forge tests/*.py` returned no hits while validating the workspace-support change.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, RE-POINTED. The forge-engine workspace path survived the port in two pieces: the archetype body is now Lua/Bash under archetypes/forge-engine/, and its parallel-launch supervision is Go — luahost.RunGroup (internal/luahost/rungroup.go:47), which ADR-0010 explicitly names as the one archetype body that did NOT become Lua (:27-28). RunGroup has its own test (rungroup_test.go), which covers the third area this bead lists (worst-rc propagation — :45-46 documents returning the highest exit code — and interrupt cleanup). The first two areas are still uncovered: workspace-vs-game discovery and workspace glob expansion, now in the Lua archetype. Re-aim at archetypes/forge-engine/ with a sample workspace fixture. Note the detector never fires at bootstrap either — admin-x6tn.

title: forge-engine workspace dev: SIGKILL escalation when child ignores SIGTERM
description:
The workspace branch of `_DEV_PY` in `archetypes/forge-engine.py` handles `KeyboardInterrupt` by calling `_p.terminate()` (SIGTERM) on each child and then `wait()`ing unbounded.

Two failure modes:
1. A child that ignores SIGTERM (game engine eating signals mid-shutdown) leaves `./admin dev` hung waiting forever.
2. A second Ctrl+C during the cleanup `wait()` raises `KeyboardInterrupt` again and aborts the remaining waits, orphaning the surviving children.

Fix: after `terminate()`, `wait()` each child with a bounded timeout (a few seconds), then escalate to `_p.kill()` for any still alive, then final wait. Catch `KeyboardInterrupt` inside the cleanup path too.

Saw this because: code review note on the workspace KeyboardInterrupt handler (forge-engine.py:127-132).

comments.author: github-import
comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #364] @McBrideMusings at 2026-05-12T17:29:57Z:

Fixed in dcf8532. Workspace dev KeyboardInterrupt cleanup now: SIGTERMs all children, waits up to 5s with a shared deadline, escalates to SIGKILL for any survivor, and swallows repeat Ctrl+C so the cleanup path can't be aborted into orphaning processes.

title: forge-engine workspace: per-glob warning when projects entry matches nothing
description:
In `archetypes/forge-engine.py` `_workspace_projects`, each entry in `forge.workspace.toml`'s `projects = [...]` list is expanded via `glob.glob` and silently dropped if it matches nothing. A misspelled literal (e.g. `projects = ["physis"]` instead of `"physics"`) produces an empty result for that entry, and only the aggregate "workspace has no launchable projects" message fires if every entry misses.

Emit a per-entry warning when a glob expands to zero matches so typos surface immediately instead of leaving the user wondering why a specific project didn't launch.

Saw this because: code review note on the glob loop in `_workspace_projects` (forge-engine.py:68) after the workspace-support change.

Fixed in dcf8532. `_workspace_projects` now warns per-entry when a `projects` glob matches nothing, and separately when it matches but no `main.lua` is found — typos surface immediately.

title: shell-passthrough interactive=true silently skips tmp/run.log
description:
When `interactive = true` is set on a `shell-passthrough` action, the renderer uses `subprocess.call(_cmdline, shell=True)` which inherits the terminal directly. This means output is never tee'd to `tmp/run.log`, violating the "all run output tee'd to tmp/run.log" convention documented in CLAUDE.md. No warning is shown to the user.

Options:
- Emit a one-time `warn("interactive mode: output is not logged to tmp/run.log")` before the subprocess call
- Or document the tradeoff clearly in the archetype schema docs

Saw this because: `gen/fragments.py`, `render_shell_passthrough` — the `interactive` branch uses bare `subprocess.call` with no `run_cmd` or tee path.

title: _with_global_defaults applied in dev_ios/build_ios only — dev_mac, deploy_*, dev_device, build_mac don't get global defaults
description:
When a user sets any `[apple]` key in `~/.admin/admin.toml` (e.g. `prebuild_cmd`, `mac_install_path_dev`), they'd expect it to apply across all apple commands. Currently `_with_global_defaults(cfg, "apple")` is only called in `dev_ios` and `build_ios`.

Functions that need the same call added:
- `dev_mac` (~line 1667)
- `deploy_mac` (~line 1795)
- `deploy_ios` (~line 1841)
- `dev_device` (~line 1898)
- `build_mac` (~line 1933)

Saw this because: the global defaults feature was added this session but only wired into the two iOS functions that were the immediate focus.

title: dev_ios: 'no simulator pinned' hint doesn't fire when IOS_DEVICE is set but unresolvable
description:
In `admin_lib/apple.py:1737`, after commit `3006659`:

```python
sim_id = None
device_name = os.environ.get("IOS_DEVICE") or cfg.get("ios_device") or _global_ios_device()
if device_name:
    sim_id = find_simulator(device_name)
    if not sim_id:
        warn(f"simulator '{device_name}' not found, falling back to auto-resolve")
if sim_id is None and not device_name:
    info("No simulator pinned — auto-resolving.")
    info("Pin one: set IOS_DEVICE env var, ios_device in [apple], or ios_device in ~/.admin/config.toml")
```

The help-text hint listing the three pin locations only prints when `device_name` is falsy. If a user sets `IOS_DEVICE=NotARealSim` (typo, retired simulator name, etc.), they get the `warn(...)` line but never the hint about where to fix the pin — exactly the moment the hint is most useful.

## Suggested fix

Change the guard so the hint also fires when the pin failed to resolve:

```python
if sim_id is None:
    if not device_name:
        info("No simulator pinned — auto-resolving.")
    info("Pin one: set IOS_DEVICE env var, ios_device in [apple], or ios_device in ~/.admin/admin.toml")
```

Also note: the existing hint text still says `~/.admin/config.toml` — that path was renamed to `~/.admin/admin.toml` in `3006659`. Fix the hint text at the same time.

## Provenance

Code-review agent flagged this as a sub-threshold UX gap (confidence 40) during `/wrap-up` of `3006659`.

title: Detect stale ~/.admin/config.toml after rename to ~/.admin/admin.toml
description:
Commit `3006659` introduced `_global_admin_config()` (admin_lib/apple.py:305) which reads `~/.admin/admin.toml`. An earlier prototype of this helper (lived briefly in-session as `_global_ios_device()`) read from `~/.admin/config.toml`.

If any user created a `~/.admin/config.toml` based on the prototype docs or a downstream commit message, that file is now silently ignored — no warning, no fallback chain to it.

## Suggested fix

Pick one of:

1. **Warn on load** — in `_global_admin_config()`, if `~/.admin/admin.toml` is absent and `~/.admin/config.toml` exists, print a one-time warn pointing at the rename.
2. **Migrate in install.sh** — detect a stale `~/.admin/config.toml` on install and either rename it (if no `admin.toml` exists) or warn the user.
3. **Read both** — accept either filename as a fallback, with `admin.toml` winning. Cheap and forgiving.

## Provenance

Surfaced during the `3006659` wrap-up. The mid-session path change happened when the helper was renamed from `_global_ios_device` (single-key) to `_global_admin_config` + `_with_global_defaults` (general). The filename changed alongside the rename and wasn't called out separately.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — nothing reads ~/.admin/admin.toml or ~/.admin/config.toml any more. Under the Go binary ~/.admin is only an archetype directory (internal/archetype/search.go:36,54-56); there is no global admin config file, so a stale prototype one cannot be silently ignored.

title: Test that remote_recreate_container uses the new image tag, not the inspected SHA
description:
Add a regression test for `admin_lib/docker.py:remote_recreate_container` that mocks `subprocess` and asserts:

- The live recreate `docker run` references the **tag** passed in (the `image` parameter), not the SHA returned by `_restore_image_from_inspect`.
- The `/tmp/<container>-restore.sh` file written to disk references the **SHA** from `docker inspect` (so recovery still pins to the prior good build).

## Context

Commit `3771171` fixed a bug where deploys silently relaunched the previous image SHA instead of the freshly-built tag. The cause: `restore_image` (the OLD container's image SHA) was being threaded into both the recovery script AND the live `docker run`. The fix split them.

This regression went unnoticed because the existing coverage at `tests/test_docker.py:292` (`test_restore_image_from_inspect`) only checks the SHA-extraction helper in isolation — nothing verifies how its return value flows through `remote_recreate_container`.

Issue #181 (closed) introduced the SHA-pinning intent for the restore script; today's regression silently extended that SHA to the live recreate, defeating every deploy.

## Provenance

Surfaced during the `3771171` fix session — `admin_lib/docker.py:443-466` (pre-fix) used `restore_image` for both `restore_script` and `remote_run`. No test caught it.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — this is pytest-suite hygiene for tests/ and admin_lib/, both deleted by admin-3rgp.30. The Go suite (117 *_test.go files) is a fresh suite with none of the machinery named here. admin_lib/docker.py is deleted. Remote container recreation is now internal/dockerrun/provision.go with internal/dockerrun/*_test.go.

title: Legacy apple_dev.dev_ios diverged from admin_lib/apple.dev_ios — missing launch_args plumbing
description:
Mirrors issue #352 (legacy `apple_dev.dev_macos` vs `dev_loop_macos`) — same divergence pattern, different function.

The active `dev_ios` in `admin_lib/apple.py` (commit b80af3a) now accepts an optional `launch_args` kwarg and threads it through `dev_loop_ios` → `install_and_launch_sim` so callers can forward args to `xcrun simctl launch`.

The parallel legacy `dev_ios` in `admin_lib/apple_dev.py:177-247` was not updated. Its simctl-launch path at line 247 still calls `install_and_launch_sim(device_id, app_path, dev_bundle_id)` with no launch_args. Not currently reached by any archetype (the active path goes through `admin_lib/apple.py`), but it lives in the tree and will silently drop launch_args if anything reactivates it.

Options:
- delete `apple_dev.py` if it's confirmed dead
- bring it to parity with `admin_lib/apple.py` (launch_args + everything else it lags on)

Saw this because: while threading `launch_args` through the apple archetype this session, `grep` turned up the second `dev_ios` and `install_and_launch_sim` call site. The default-`None` kwarg meant callers wouldn't break, but the divergence is exactly the same code-smell as #352.

title: install.sh should migrate stale ~/.admin/init-admin pre-commit hooks to admin-gen
description:
Older downstream projects have a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` that calls the renamed-and-removed `~/.admin/init-admin --audit`. Since that binary no longer exists, every commit touching `admin.toml` or `admin` fails silently with:

```
ERROR: ./admin is out of sync with admin.toml.
Regenerate with: ~/.admin/init-admin --regenerate . --force-dirty
```

…even though `admin-gen --audit` reports clean. The user has to hand-edit `.git/hooks/pre-commit` in every project to swap `init-admin` → `admin-gen`.

Two reasonable fixes:
1. **install.sh patches existing hooks** — sed-replace `init-admin` → `admin-gen` in any `.git/hooks/pre-commit` it finds across projects it knows about (or just on the current project if invoked from one).
2. **admin-gen detects + warns** — when running in a project whose pre-commit hook references the old name, print a one-time warning and offer to fix it.

Hit this in the stash-reels session 2026-05-10 during a routine commit; had to fix the hook by hand. Any project that hasn't been re-bootstrapped since the rename will hit the same wall.

title: run_cmd() logs raw ANSI codes while _log_write() strips them — inconsistent log file content
description:
## Problem

`run_cmd()` tees subprocess output to the log file raw (ANSI codes included), while the new `_log_write()` helper (added in c0d7038) strips ANSI before writing. Log files now have mixed content — Python-side status lines from `info()`/`ok()`/`warn()`/`err()` are clean plain text, but subprocess output may contain color escape codes that appear as garbage in a text editor or `cat`.

## Location

- `admin_lib/core.py:434` — `log_fh.write(line)` writes each subprocess line unmodified
- `admin_lib/core.py:45` — `_log_write` strips via `_ANSI_ESCAPE_RE.sub("", text)` before writing

## Fix

Apply the same `_ANSI_ESCAPE_RE` stripping to `log_fh.write(line)` in `run_cmd()`, or factor out a shared `_strip_ansi()` call used by both paths.

comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #355] @McBrideMusings at 2026-05-12T19:10:30Z:

Fixed in 8718dee. The non-PTY `run_cmd()` log-write path now applies `_ANSI_ESCAPE_RE.sub("", line)` (the same regex used by the PTY path and `_log_write`) so log files contain plain text across all three writers.

title: shell actions silently ignore extra CLI arguments
description:
When a command's action is `kind = "shell"`, any extra arguments passed on the command line are silently discarded. There is no \"unknown argument\" error.

**Observed:** After simplifying `etv-station`'s `dev` action from `multi-target` to `shell`, running `./admin dev station` (old muscle memory) quietly executes the shell action as if no argument was given. The old `multi-target` handler did error on unknown targets.

**Expected:** Either pass extra args through to the underlying shell command (useful for flags), or error if the action doesn't accept positional args.

comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #354] @McBrideMusings at 2026-05-11T14:21:13Z:

Resolved: added shell-passthrough action kind that shlex-quotes and appends positional args from ./admin <name> <ARGS> to the run string. Supports interactive = true for prompts.

title: Orphan log stream processes survive between admin dev runs
description:
`dev_loop_macos` spawns a `log stream --predicate ...` subprocess for the dev session. Cleanup happens in `stop_os_log` at end-of-iteration via `register_cleanup` and `atexit`. If admin is hard-killed (terminal closed, SIGKILL, kernel OOM, Ctrl+\), neither path fires and the `log stream` lives on as an orphan parented to launchd.

Observed during the macOS dev-loop fix session: `pgrep -af CCToolDev` returned a `log stream --predicate '...CCToolDev.app...'` PID whose admin parent had exited an hour earlier. They accumulate over time and consume system log streaming slots.

Suggested fix: at the top of `dev_loop_macos` (and the iOS equivalent), sweep any pre-existing `log stream` processes whose argv contains the predicate substring (e.g. the dev product name or subsystem) before launching a new one. Concretely something like:

```python
subprocess.run(["pkill", "-f", f"log stream.*{subsystem}"], capture_output=True)
```

run once before the main loop. This is also a more reliable cleanup than the SIGINT-handler path.

Provenance: `admin_lib/apple.py:_children` tracking only covers the current process tree, not orphans from prior runs.

title: Legacy apple_dev.dev_macos still has the kill-race pattern fixed in dev_loop_macos
description:
The older `apple_dev.dev_macos` function in `admin_lib/apple_dev.py` repeats the same SIGTERM-fire-and-forget then `open -n` race that was fixed today in `dev_loop_macos` (commit a48f2f6).

Specifically:
- `admin_lib/apple_dev.py:88-92` — sends `pkill -f dev_process_match` (and any `extra_kill_patterns`) without waiting for actual exit
- `admin_lib/apple_dev.py:135` — runs `open -n app_path` immediately after, racing with the still-dying instance
- `admin_lib/apple_dev.py:168` — same fire-and-forget pattern at end-of-iteration

Today's fix in `dev_loop_macos` poll-waits for the process to actually exit and escalates SIGTERM → SIGKILL after ~1.5s. The legacy function should either:

1. Get the same treatment, OR
2. Be deleted — `grep -rn "from .*apple_dev\|apple_dev\." admin_lib/ archetypes/` returns zero call sites in this repo, so it's effectively dead code.

Provenance: noticed during the dev-loop fix session — searched for callers of `dev_macos` to decide whether to fix it too, found none in-tree, decided to leave it for a follow-up rather than touch untested code with no callers.

[migrated from GitHub #352] @McBrideMusings at 2026-05-11T14:21:08Z:

Resolved: apple_dev.py deleted. The legacy dev_macos function with the kill-race pattern is gone; admin_lib/apple.dev_loop_macos is the sole implementation.

title: Add static-analysis check (pyflakes/ruff) to catch undefined names in admin-gen
description:
## Problem

admin-gen ships without static analysis, so undefined-name bugs reach users.

Concrete instance: commit 08c63a8 added `_ensure_gitattributes` which calls `subprocess.run(...)` at admin-gen:425, but the `import subprocess` was missing from the import block. The function only runs when `project_dir` is inside a git repo, so a manual smoke run wouldn't have triggered the path. The first user to invoke `admin regen` inside a git repo got a `NameError: name 'subprocess' is not defined` traceback (fixed in 4f11442).

Pyflakes or ruff would have caught this in milliseconds.

- `install.sh` as a pre-install gate (fail fast before deploying to ~/.admin/)

- A CI workflow (if/when one exists)

title: Guard against unset PLUGIN_NAME in unraid-plugin actions
description:
When `PLUGIN_NAME` is unset, `os.environ.get('PLUGIN_NAME')` returns `None` and the generated commands silently operate on wrong paths:

- `deploy` rsyncs to `/boot/config/plugins/None/`
- `register` runs `installplg /boot/config/plugins/None/None.plg`
- `uninstall` runs `removeplg None`

No error is raised — the operations just silently fail or corrupt the wrong path.

The `require_host` helper in `remote.py` already handles the same pattern for `UNRAID_HOST`. `PLUGIN_NAME` needs the same treatment: check at the top of each action and exit with a clear message if unset.

title: Mount host Cargo registry cache in Docker cross-compile to avoid full re-download on every build
description:
## Problem

Each Linux cross-compile (`docker run --rm ...`) starts with an empty Cargo home inside the container and redownloads all dependencies from scratch — 120+ crates on every build. The `--rm` flag destroys the container filesystem on exit, so nothing is cached between runs.

The compiled artifact cache (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`) is already persisted via a host-mounted volume (`-v {server_dir}:/src`), but the source tarball registry (`~/.cargo/registry`) is not.

## Fix

Add a registry cache mount to the `docker run` call in `admin_lib/rust.py`:

```python
f"-v {os.path.expanduser('~')}/.cargo/registry:/usr/local/cargo/registry "
```

This shares the host Mac's already-populated `~/.cargo/registry` into the container. Cargo only downloads crates it hasn't seen before, making incremental Linux builds much faster.

## Context

The cross-compile is used to build the Linux server binaries bundled into the iOS/macOS client apps (`cctool-server/bundled-binaries/`). Since the dev machine is macOS, Docker is the only way to produce ELF binaries. Native macOS builds already benefit from the host registry cache automatically — this brings Linux builds to parity.

Saw this because: the build output showed a full crate-registry download on every pass (120+ `Downloaded X vY.Z` lines).

title: Auto-pull modules for symbols referenced in kind=python action bodies
description:
**Type:** Risk / Structural

## Context

Issue #TBD (the bundle-shrinking work) introduced two ways an action can pull in additional admin_lib modules transitively:

1. **By kind:** `gen/fragments.KIND_MODULES` declares e.g. `"kill-port" → ["ports", "ports_nuke"]`. Set up by archetype actions that use the dedicated kind.
2. **By module list:** the manifest's `modules = [...]` is the explicit declaration.

Neither catches the case where a `kind = "python"` action body references a function that lives in a module the manifest didn't declare.

## The bug this allows

Demonstrated this session in web-file-manager:

```toml
modules = ["ports", "web_dev"]

[actions.kill]
kind = "python"
run  = "kill_port_interactive(int(os.environ.get('BACKEND_PORT', '3011')))"
```

`kill_port_interactive` was moved from `ports.py` into `ports_nuke.py` upstream. The manifest above doesn't list `ports_nuke`, the kind isn't `kill-port` (so KIND_MODULES doesn't trigger), and the bundler successfully produces a bundle that compiles but fails at runtime with `NameError: kill_port_interactive` when the user runs `./admin kill`.

Same shape as #TBD `run_vite_rust_dev` — a manifest references a name that isn't bundled, and we only find out at first invocation.

## Fix path

After resolving the action set in `gen/archetypes.resolve`, scan each `kind = "python"` action's `run` body for top-level admin_lib symbols. For each match, look up which admin_lib module owns it and add that module to the bundle's module list.

Implementation sketch:
- Build a once-per-generator `SYMBOL_OWNERS` map (`name → module`) by AST-walking each `admin_lib/*.py` once at gen startup. Cache the result.
- For each python-kind action, AST-parse `run`, collect referenced names, intersect with `SYMBOL_OWNERS.keys()`, union the owner modules into the bundle.
- The reachability strip pass already preserves these symbols once they're bundled, so no other change is needed.

## Workaround

Manually add the required module to the manifest's `modules = [...]`. That's what web-file-manager does today after this session.

## Provenance

Saw this because: regenerating web-file-manager after the upstream `ports.py` → `ports`/`ports_nuke` split produced a bundle missing `kill_port_interactive`. Realized the same trap will catch any future module split or function move.

title: Add direct unit tests for compact_whitespace
description:
**Type:** Test gap
**File:** `tests/test_bundler.py` (would be expanded), function under test: `gen/bundler.compact_whitespace`

## Context

`tests/test_bundler.py` has 8 test cases covering `strip_unreachable` (hard-keep, cmd_* entry, string-literal dispatch, module-level call edges, decorator preservation, transitive walk, unreferenced constants, no-changes baseline). It does not directly exercise `compact_whitespace`.

## Why this matters

`compact_whitespace` does three things, each with real failure modes:

1. **Empty module section detection** — uses a regex to find `# === admin_lib.<name> ===` banners and AST-parses the body to decide whether to drop. Could mis-parse a section, mis-detect a banner, or accidentally drop a section that has only constants (no defs).
2. **Blank-line coalesce** — collapses runs of 3+ blank lines to 2. Could strip too aggressively if leading-whitespace handling is wrong (lines that are spaces-only vs empty).
3. **Divider-comment strip** — drops lines matching `# -{20,}`. Could false-positive on a meaningful comment that happens to start with `# -` (e.g. `# -1 means fill-remaining` — currently safe because the rule requires the rest to be all `-`, but worth pinning behavior).

Today these are validated only end-to-end via the regenerate-and-compile flow. Adding direct tests would let us regression-pin the edge cases.

## Provenance

Saw this because: code-simplifier agent's wrap-up report flagged "Missing direct test for `compact_whitespace`, but its behavior is benign (whitespace only)" — benign behaviors are still worth pinning when they affect every downstream bundle.

title: Cap strip_unreachable iteration loop in gen/render.py
description:
**Type:** Risk
**File:** `gen/render.py:render` (the `while True:` block around the strip-unreachable call)

## Context

`render()` runs `strip_unreachable` in a `while True: ...; if n_dropped == 0: break` loop to reach a fixed point. This is necessary because some references hold symbols alive transiently — e.g. forward-reference type annotations like `def f() -> "Bar":` keep `Bar` alive until `f` itself is dropped, after which the string disappears too.

In practice the loop converges in 2-3 iterations.

## Risk

The loop has no upper bound. If a future change introduces:
- A cyclic dependency in the call graph that flip-flops between two states across iterations
- A pathological forward-ref pattern that never converges
- A bug in `strip_unreachable` that drops different symbols on each call

…the bundler would loop forever during regeneration.

## Fix

Cap iterations at ~10 (well above the realistic 2-3) and emit a warning if hit. If the cap is reached, that's a bug to investigate — but at least the bundler returns instead of hanging.

## Provenance

Saw this because: I added the loop in this session without a safety net. `gen/render.py` line ~210, the `while True: full, n_dropped, _dropped = strip_unreachable(full); ...` block.

title: Simplify remote_recreate_container (admin_lib/docker.py, 102 lines)
description:
**Function:** `remote_recreate_container`
**File:** `admin_lib/docker.py`
**Current size:** 102 lines (9-line docstring)
**Bundle impact:** Bundled in every `docker-unraid` deploy.

## Context

Main deploy path for the docker-unraid archetype. Transports a local image to the remote host and recreates the named container against it, preserving the existing run config (read via `docker inspect`).

## Why it's big

Sequential pipeline with several distinct phases:
1. Verify container exists on remote
2. `docker inspect` → snapshot dict
3. Save+load image (or push if a registry is configured)
4. Stop + remove old container
5. Build new `docker run` from the snapshot (calls `_build_run_args_from_inspect`)
6. Run + verify

Each phase has its own error path with `info`/`err`/`return rc` boilerplate.

## Simplification angles

- **Extract phases** into 3-5 small helpers (`_inspect_or_die`, `_transport_image`, `_replay_run_config`, etc.) so the top-level reads as a sequence of named steps. Each helper handles its own error printing.
- **Unified rc-handling:** today every phase has `if rc != 0: err(...); return rc`. A small `step()` wrapper that runs a callable and exits on nonzero would drop a lot of repetition.
- **The dry-run path** ties into every phase. Could that gate be lifted to a single early branch that produces the docker run line without doing any of the destructive work?
- **The push-vs-load decision** could move into a helper (`_get_image_to_remote`).

## Constraints

- Behavior must be byte-identical for the success path (deploys are run against this).
- The dry-run output is consumed by users to understand what would happen — don't change its format without notice.

title: Simplify _build_run_args_from_inspect (admin_lib/docker.py, 121 lines)
description:
**Function:** `_build_run_args_from_inspect`
**File:** `admin_lib/docker.py`
**Current size:** 121 lines (largest function in admin_lib)
**Bundle impact:** Present in every bundle that uses `docker-unraid` archetype (deploy/diff commands).

## Context

After the bundle-shrinking pass (#TBD/PRs that took web-file-manager from 3284 → 1455 lines), this is now the single largest function bundled in downstream `./admin` scripts. It reconstructs a `docker run` command line from the live container's `docker inspect` output so we can preserve the Unraid GUI's run config across image recreations.

## Why it's big

It enumerates every kind of run-arg field that might be set: Binds, PortBindings, Env, Labels, RestartPolicy, NetworkMode, CapAdd/Drop, User, Hostname, Mac, ExtraHosts, Devices, etc. Each field has its own `if val:` branch with formatting logic.

- **Field-table approach:** replace the long if/elif chain with a list of `(inspect_path, format_fn)` tuples. Iterate once, skip empties.
- **Trivial-value detection:** there's already a `_is_trivial` helper — look for opportunities to short-circuit empty/default values earlier.
- **Move quoting into one helper** instead of inline `shlex.quote` per branch.
- **Group related field-sets** (e.g. all PortBindings handling) into named helpers if any are reusable for `remote_container_diff`.

## Constraints

- Output must remain byte-identical for the same input (deploy idempotency depends on this).
- Drift detection in `remote_container_diff` compares against the snapshot this fn produces, so any change here may require updating the snapshot format.
- Keep test coverage in `tests/test_docker.py` green.

title: Env var scanner misses bare os.environ[KEY] accesses in archetype action strings
description:
The env var scanner in `gen/fragments.py` (`_PY_ENV_RE` regex, around line 504) only matches `os.environ.get('VAR')` patterns. Bare `os.environ['VAR']` or `os.environ["VAR"]` accesses are invisible — the var never gets a `register_env_var()` call, so `./admin env` won't report it and runtime crashes with a raw `KeyError` instead of a clean "UNSET required" message.

Fixed the immediate symptom in docker-unraid (645ffab) by changing bare accesses to `.get()`, but the scanner itself should also match `os.environ[` to catch future archetypes that use the bare form.

**Saw this because:** `UNRAID_HOST` was used in 3 places via `os.environ['UNRAID_HOST']` in `archetypes/docker-unraid.py` but never appeared in `./admin env` output. The workaround was to rewrite the accesses as `.get()`, but the structural gap remains.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — there is no env-var scanner and no Python action bodies to scan. kind="python" is gone (internal/kinds/catalog.go:14-20), so os.environ appears nowhere, and gen/fragments.py is deleted with the generator. There is also no `admin env` verb for a missed variable to be absent from. The equivalent surface in Go is manifest.IterEnvRefs (internal/manifest/envrefs.go:30), which scans ${VAR} placeholders in manifest strings — a different mechanism with no bare-access blind spot, because there is no second way to read an environment variable.

title: Bundler: from . import module as alias patterns silently produce NameError in generated scripts
description:
The bundler replaces all relative imports with `pass`, with a comment claiming this is always safe because the imported name is already in the flat namespace. This holds for `from .foo import name` (where `name` is inlined as a module-level definition), but **not** for `from . import module as alias`.

In the bundled flat namespace, the module object itself doesn't exist — only the module's *contents* are inlined. So `from . import docker as _docker` becomes `pass`, and any subsequent use of `_docker` raises `NameError` at runtime with no bundler-time warning.

**Seen in the wild:** `admin_lib/ports.py:259` — `from . import docker as _docker` followed by `getattr(_docker, "_reload_active", False)` caused a `NameError` in downstream generated scripts. Fixed by switching to `from .docker import _reload_active`.

**Root cause:** `gen/bundler.py:46–53` — the `_repl` function and its comment claim `pass` is "a safe no-op... in every case" but this is incorrect for module-alias imports.

**Fix:** The bundler should detect `from . import X` and `from . import X as Y` patterns and either raise a `BundlerError` at generation time, or (if the module is always bundled) rewrite them as `Y = <module_level_sentinel>` — though the former is safer since module objects can't be reconstructed from a flat namespace.

Note: this is distinct from #297 (name shadowing between inlined modules). That issue is about collisions; this is about the bundler incorrectly claiming safety for a pattern it cannot handle.

title: Dev builds force one bundle ID onto every target, so an app extension collides with its parent app
description:
`admin dev ios` builds a Debug copy that can sit beside the Release copy by giving it a different bundle ID. It applies that ID to the whole Xcode project, so a widget extension inside the app gets the app's ID too, and the simulator refuses to install an app whose extension claims to be the app.

## What happens, with real values

In a project whose app is `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios` and whose widget target is set to `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios$(SCRATCHPAD_BUNDLE_ID_SUFFIX).widgets`, run `admin dev ios`:

| Target | Bundle ID it gets | Bundle ID it should get |
|---|---|---|
| app | `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios.dev` | `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios.dev` |
| widget extension | `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios.dev` | `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios.dev.widgets` |

The build succeeds. The install fails:

```
An error was encountered processing the command (domain=IXErrorDomain, code=2):
Simulator device failed to install the application.
Mismatched bundle IDs.
Underlying error (domain=IXErrorDomain, code=2):
	Failed to set app extension placeholders for com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios.dev
```

## Why that is wrong

Two separate pieces of software inside one app are claiming to be the same piece of software. iOS uses the bundle ID as the identity of an installed thing, so an app and its own extension having one identity is a contradiction — the installer is right to refuse it.

## The line that causes it

`admin_lib/apple.py:2607`, in `_compose_dev_settings`:

```python
override = f"PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER={dev_bundle_id}"
```

That string is handed to `xcodebuild` through `xcodebuild_filtered`'s `extra_settings`, and a setting passed that way applies to every target in the project — `xcodebuild_filtered`'s own docstring at `apple_lib/apple.py:273` says so ("applies globally (incl. SwiftPM bundles)").

## Who it hurts and when

Any apple-archetype project with an app-extension target — a widget, a share extension, a notification service. It fires on every `admin dev ios` and `admin dev device` run in such a project, and the project is unrunnable through admin until it's fixed. Projects with a single app target are unaffected, which is why this survived this long.

## The fix: admin stops naming any target's bundle ID

Decided 2026-08-11. `_compose_dev_settings` no longer emits `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` at all. Instead it emits a suffix that each target's own `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` setting in the pbxproj appends to itself:

```
ADMIN_DEV_BUNDLE_SUFFIX=.dev
```

The app target's pbxproj setting becomes `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios$(ADMIN_DEV_BUNDLE_SUFFIX)`; the widget's becomes `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios$(ADMIN_DEV_BUNDLE_SUFFIX).widgets`. Each target derives its own identity, so there is no value admin could push that would make two targets collide. Release builds pass no suffix, the variable expands to nothing, and prod IDs are unchanged — so this needs no separate prod path.

**Alternatives rejected.** Patching each `.appex`'s `Info.plist` after the build and re-signing (the shape `dev_macos_postprocess` already uses for the macOS rename) was rejected: it leaves admin still forcing one ID onto everything and then repairing the damage, so the next setting that shouldn't be global fails the same way. Teaching admin to enumerate extension targets and run a separate `xcodebuild` per target was rejected: `xcodebuild` cannot scope a setting to one target inside a scheme build, so it means giving up the single scheme build that currently embeds and signs the extension.

## What to change

1. `_compose_dev_settings` (`admin_lib/apple.py:2592`) emits `ADMIN_DEV_BUNDLE_SUFFIX=<suffix>` instead of `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER=<dev_bundle_id>`.
2. Derive the suffix by subtracting the prod bundle ID from the dev one. The dev ID is already `<prod>.dev` by default (`_resolve_ios_dev_bundle`, `admin_lib/apple.py:2047`), giving `.dev`. If a manifest sets `ios_dev_bundle` / `mac_dev_bundle` explicitly to something that is *not* the prod ID plus a suffix, that is now unexpressible — fail with an error naming both values and saying to either drop the explicit key or make it prod-plus-suffix. Do not silently fall back to the old global override; that reintroduces the bug.
3. The existing warning at `admin_lib/apple.py:2598` about a manifest putting `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` in `dev_build_settings` becomes a hard error — under the new scheme that string is exactly the thing that breaks extensions, and a warning is not enough to stop it.
4. Document the required pbxproj setup in the apple archetype docs: each target's `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` must reference `$(ADMIN_DEV_BUNDLE_SUFFIX)`. Note that a project which has not been updated will build dev on top of prod (same ID, no side-by-side install) rather than failing loudly.

## Acceptance check

- Tests in `tests/test_apple.py` asserting `_compose_dev_settings` emits `ADMIN_DEV_BUNDLE_SUFFIX=.dev` for a default config, emits no `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` under any config, errors on an explicit dev bundle that isn't prod-plus-suffix, and errors when `dev_build_settings` contains `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER`.
- Full suite green (`.venv/bin/pytest`).

## Still needs a person, after the code lands

Confirming a real widget-bearing project installs is a manual step in another repo: update `apple-notepad`'s pbxproj so both targets reference `$(ADMIN_DEV_BUNDLE_SUFFIX)`, run `admin dev ios`, and check the widget's built `Info.plist` carries `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios.dev.widgets` while the app carries `com.piercemakes.scratchpad.ios.dev`. This repo has no Xcode project with an extension target to drive.

Type: AFK

title: Document inline target name collision with VALID_ACTION_KEYS (run, kind, desc, etc.)
description:
The inline target form \`[actions.X.NAME]\` filters subtables by \`k not in VALID_ACTION_KEYS\` (\`gen/archetypes.py:280\`-ish). So target names like \`run\`, \`kind\`, \`desc\`, \`targets\` get parsed as the action's reserved keys, NOT as targets.

Hit while wiring a multi-target action where one target was naturally named \`run\` (e.g. \`./admin dev run\` to mean \"run both processes\"). The TOML \`[actions.dev.run]\` got treated as a malformed action \`run\` key and silently produced an empty action.

Workaround: use the flat \`[actions.X.targets]\` form (\`name = \"shell-string\"\`), but that loses per-target descriptions for the picker menu.

Related to #314 (\"Flat targets can't use group/priority — no migration hint\"), but the underlying issue is broader: target names colliding with VALID_ACTION_KEYS produce confusing/silent failures.

Suggest:
- At parse time, detect inline subtable keys that collide with VALID_ACTION_KEYS and either reject loudly (\"target name 'run' collides with reserved action key\") or auto-promote to a target if the value is a dict that looks like a target spec.
- Document the constraint in the manifest reference.

The flat form supports any name including \`run\`; the inline form rejects (silently right now) some names. Consistent behavior + good error message would have saved the workaround dance.

title: install.sh without --force silently no-ops on existing install
description:
Wasted ~30 minutes today during a debug session because \`bash install.sh\` (no flags) didn't actually copy files when \`~/.admin/\` already existed — it printed \`updating generator_commit\` and \`Done\` but the source-tree change I'd made wasn't deployed. Had to run \`bash install.sh --force\` to actually copy.

Reproduction:
1. \`~/.admin/\` exists and was installed at SHA A.
2. Make a code change in \`~/Projects/admin-project-tool/\` (now SHA B+dirty).
3. \`bash install.sh\` (no flags).
4. Output suggests success.
5. \`grep <my-change> ~/.admin/gen/foo.py\` → not present. Code didn't deploy.

Two reasonable fixes:
- **Default behavior**: copy unless \`~/.admin/\` is at the same git SHA as the source repo. \`--force\` becomes a no-op for the same case.
- **Fail-loud**: keep current default but print \`'~/.admin/' already at SHA X (source at SHA Y); pass --force to overwrite\` clearly to stderr. Don't print \`Done\` if nothing copied.

The second is probably less surprising for existing users. Either way, the \`updating generator_commit: A → B\` log line was actively misleading because the SHA wasn't actually being updated in the deployed code.

title: run_with_reload forwards SIGTERM (not SIGINT) when admin process receives SIGINT as a signal
description:
The fix in \`29ecb56\` correctly sends \`SIGINT\` to the child when \`KeyboardInterrupt\` is raised via the \`\x03\` stdin byte (the normal Ctrl-C path in raw tty mode).

However, if the admin process receives \`SIGINT\` as an actual *signal* (e.g. \`kill -INT <pid>\` from another terminal), Python's default \`SIGINT\` handler raises \`SystemExit\`, not \`KeyboardInterrupt\`. In that case \`sys.exc_info()[0]\` is \`SystemExit\` in the \`finally\` block, so the child still receives \`SIGTERM\`.

For projects like recodarr where SIGTERM means "reload, leave worker alive," this means a programmatic \`SIGINT\` to the admin process leaves the worker running with no supervisor — the same orphan scenario the fix was meant to prevent.

**Fix options:**
- Also check for \`SystemExit\` in addition to \`KeyboardInterrupt\`
- Register an explicit \`SIGINT\` handler in \`run_with_reload\` that sets a flag and re-raises \`KeyboardInterrupt\`
- Use a local \`_user_exit\` flag set on \`KeyboardInterrupt\` **and** in a SIGINT handler, checked in the \`finally\`

title: Add regression test for run_with_reload SIGINT-vs-SIGTERM forwarding on exit
description:
The fix in \`29ecb56\` changes \`run_with_reload\` to send \`SIGINT\` (not \`SIGTERM\`) to the child process when the admin exits due to \`KeyboardInterrupt\` (Ctrl-C). This is a single-line behavior change that's easy to regress.

A targeted test should:
1. Spawn a dummy child process that records which signal it received
2. Trigger \`KeyboardInterrupt\` in the \`run_with_reload\` loop (simulate \`\x03\` on stdin or raise directly)
3. Assert the child received \`SIGINT\`, not \`SIGTERM\`
4. Also verify that a reload (SIGUSR1) still sends \`SIGTERM\` to the child

Without this test, a future refactor of the \`finally\` block could silently revert to always-SIGTERM and break any project that distinguishes the two signals.

title: _PBXPROJ_CACHE never invalidates on file mtime
description:
The pbxproj parser cache (`_PBXPROJ_CACHE` in `admin_lib/apple.py`) is a module-level dict keyed by project_path with no eviction. For one-shot admin invocations this is fine — the process is short-lived and a single parse per project_path is exactly the goal. But:

- If anything embeds `admin_lib` in a long-running daemon or REPL (the test suite already imports it), edits to `project.pbxproj` between calls won't be picked up.
- Cache poisoning: a transient `plutil` failure populates the cache with `{}`, and subsequent calls within the same process serve stale empty data even after the file becomes parseable.

**Fix:** key the cache on `(project_path, mtime)` instead of just `project_path`. `os.stat(pbxproj_path).st_mtime_ns` is cheap. Naturally invalidates on file change, and lets the cache outlive a transient failure.

Lower urgency since admin invocations are typically one-shot, but worth doing before anyone builds tooling that calls the resolvers in a loop.

Reference: `admin_lib/apple.py:_read_pbxproj` (added in 48c7848).
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — inherited. The pbxproj parse is 'cached per path for the process's lifetime' (docs/architecture/lua-host-api.md:209, implementation in internal/luahost/apple_pbxproj_darwin.go), keyed on path with no mtime component and no eviction, and it returns {} on any failure — so the cache-poisoning half of this bead (a transient plutil failure caching an empty result for the rest of the process) is reproduced exactly. Same fix: key on (path, mtime).

title: Apple archetype implicitly depends on rust module — declare it (or auto-pull when [server] is present)
description:
`archetypes/apple.py` declares `"modules": ["core", "icons", "apple", "log_format", "log_columns"]`. `rust` is not in that list, but command bodies (`_BUILD_PY`, `_DEV_PY`, `_DEPLOY_PY`, `_TEST_PY`, and now `_CLEAN_PY` in 48c7848) call into 7+ functions from `admin_lib.rust` (`build_server`, `dev_server`, `deploy_server_docker`, `deploy_bazzite_server`, `test_server`, `clean_server`, `clean_bundled_binaries`).

This works in practice because every downstream manifest with `[server]` also declares `modules = [..., "rust", ...]`. But it's a layering smell:
- A new downstream user who copies just `archetypes = ["apple"]` and adds `[server]` without thinking about modules will hit a NameError at clean/build/deploy time.
- The dependency isn't visible from the archetype declaration itself.

**Two ways to fix:**
1. **Declare explicitly:** add `"rust"` to the apple archetype's modules list, with the understanding that rust functions are no-ops when `_SERVER_CONFIG` is empty.
2. **Auto-pull conditionally:** in `gen/manifest.py` or `gen/render.py`, when an archetype's command body references `_SERVER_CONFIG` and the manifest declares `[server]`, automatically include the `rust` module in the bundle.

Option 1 is simpler. Option 2 is more general (would benefit any archetype that conditionally pulls in optional functionality).

Pre-existing layering smell unchanged by this session, just made more visible by the new `clean_bundled_binaries` lambda.

title: Tighten _STRIP_RELATIVE_IMPORT_RE to exclude leading newlines from match
description:
The fix in e28d109 (post-strip leading `\n` from `indent`) is a workaround. The underlying issue is that the regex itself allows the preceding blank line's `\n` into the match:

```python
_STRIP_RELATIVE_IMPORT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*from\s+\.[\w.]*\s+import\s*(?:\([^)]*\)|[^\n]*)\n",
    re.MULTILINE,
)
```

`^\s*` in MULTILINE mode greedily consumes whitespace including `\n`, so for a top-level `from .X import Y` preceded by a blank line, `match_text` starts with `\n` and the captured "indent" needed a post-hoc strip to be meaningful.

**Fix:** restrict the leading whitespace to non-newline characters:

```python
_STRIP_RELATIVE_IMPORT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^[\t ]*from\s+\.[\w.]*\s+import\s*(?:\([^)]*\)|[^\n]*)\n",
    re.MULTILINE,
)
```

Then `_repl` can drop the `indent.lstrip("\n")` workaround — `indent` will only ever be tabs or spaces, and the truthy check correctly distinguishes top-level from indented.

Lower-risk than the lstrip workaround if anyone ever extends `_repl` (e.g. to detect if the import is inside a function body) and assumes `indent` is real whitespace.

Reference: `gen/bundler.py:_STRIP_RELATIVE_IMPORT_RE` and `_repl`.

title: _detect_project_path should return None instead of sys.exit(1) so resolvers can chain
description:
`_detect_project_path(cfg)` calls `sys.exit(1)` when no `cfg["project_path"]` is set and no `.xcodeproj`/`.xcworkspace` is in cwd. With the new resolver chain (added in 48c7848), several resolvers (`_resolve_subsystem`, `_resolve_mac_install_path_prod`, etc.) call into `_xcode_target_settings → _detect_project_path` even when the manifest could fully satisfy the lookup.

**Symptom:** running admin from a non-project cwd, or in projects that use the apple archetype without an actual Xcode project (server-only, hypothetical), hard-exits where it could fall through to the manifest fallback.

**Fix:** return `None` from `_detect_project_path` instead of exiting. Make `_read_pbxproj({}, ...)` and `_xcode_target_settings(cfg, None, ...)` no-op to `{}`. Existing callers (`build_*`, `deploy_*`) that genuinely need a project path can do the explicit check + `err`/`exit` themselves at the entry point.

Reference: `admin_lib/apple.py:1180-1182` (current exit), `1191-1226` (chain through), `1244-1248` (resolver call site).

Downstream lookups degrade to {} and fall back to manifest-supplied values (:209-211) instead of the process dying under them.

title: _xcode_setting: fall back to xcodebuild -showBuildSettings when pbxproj returns None
description:
`_xcode_setting(cfg, scheme, key)` (added in 48c7848) reads only the embedded `buildSettings` dict in `project.pbxproj`. Projects that put `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` (or any other key the resolvers care about) in an `.xcconfig` file referenced via `XCBuildConfiguration.baseConfigurationReference` get `None` back, then fall through to the manifest. That's correct fail-safe behavior, but it means xcconfig-driven projects lose the auto-detection win and have to set `mac_bundle` / `ios_bundle` explicitly.

**Fix:** secondary fallback to `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings -json -scheme X -configuration Debug -project Y` when pbxproj lookup returns None and no manifest override is set. Slow (5–15s per scheme), so cache aggressively (per-process, keyed by scheme + configuration; can re-use the existing `_PBXPROJ_CACHE` shape).

**When this matters:** any downstream Apple project where bundle ID, product name, etc. live in xcconfig — common for projects with shared dev/prod config split. The cctool project doesn't trigger this (settings are inline in pbxproj), so the gap was hidden by the test target.

Reference: `admin_lib/apple.py:_xcode_target_settings`, `_xcode_setting`, and the `_resolve_*` family.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — inherited, and now documented as a known limitation rather than fixed. apple.xcode_target_settings 'only sees settings written into the pbxproj itself; .xcconfig values and $(VAR) substitutions come back as literals' (docs/architecture/lua-host-api.md:210), and apple.xcode_setting returns nil for a missing key or an unresolved $(...) (:211). There is no -showBuildSettings fallback anywhere: TargetBuildDir (internal/luahost/apple_xcode_darwin.go:64-94) is the only -showBuildSettings caller and it reads exactly one key, TARGET_BUILD_DIR. So an xcconfig-driven project still has to set mac_bundle / ios_bundle by hand. The caching advice in the bead still applies — see admin-xcse for the cache's own defect.

title: Remove hardcoded "main.js" marker from nuke_dev_processes parent-supervisor heuristic
description:
`admin_lib/ports.py:nuke_dev_processes` step 1 (port-bound listeners) kills the listener AND its parent if the parent command line contains any of `("bun", "node", "npm", "python", "main.js")`:

```python
if ppid and any(k in pcmd for k in ("bun", "node", "npm", "python", "main.js")):
    pids.add(ppid)
```

The `"main.js"` marker leaks recodarr-specific filename detection into the generic helper. If another project's supervisor is named `daemon.js` or `index.js`, this list won't catch it; if a project has a `main.js` deep in `node_modules` somewhere, the check could over-match.

**Options:**
- Drop `"main.js"` (the runtime markers `bun`/`node`/`npm` already cover the parent in practice)
- Move the marker list to per-project config (e.g. `[dev_kill].supervisor_markers = ["main.js"]`)

title: Default [clean_dev].pre_kill to true
description:
The `clean-dev` kind (`gen/fragments.py:render_clean_dev`) only calls `cmd_kill(args)` first if `pre_kill` is truthy in `[clean_dev]`. Currently absent → false → dev server keeps running while `rmtree` walks the work directory.

The whole point of `clean-dev` is to clean reliably. Default should be **opt-out**, not opt-in:

```python
# fragments.py: render_clean_dev
if _cfg.get("pre_kill", True) and "cmd_kill" in globals():  # default true
    cmd_kill(args)
```

Then projects can set `pre_kill = false` only if they explicitly don't want it (rare).

title: Audit warning when mac_process and ios_process are not both set
description:
`mac_process` and `ios_process` are nearly always identical (same `productName` on a multiplatform target). When only one is set, the other path silently uses the scheme name as the fallback — which mismatches DerivedData and produces "Could not find built app" only at deploy time.

Add an `--audit` warning: if either `mac_process` or `ios_process` is set in [apple] but the other is missing, print a hint to set both (or remove both, if scheme-name happens to match `productName`).

Lower priority if #3 (auto-detect from pbxproj) lands, since auto-detection makes both fields fully optional.

title: Document workspace-vs-project discovery order in apple archetype
description:
`_detect_project_path` (admin_lib/apple.py) globs `*.xcworkspace` before `*.xcodeproj` and returns the first match. Projects with both will silently get the workspace, which may not be what the user intended.

Document the precedence in `archetypes/apple/` (or wherever apple archetype docs live) so users know:
- Workspace wins over project when both exist in the cwd.
- They can pin behavior with explicit `project_path` in [apple].

Optional: also flip the default to prefer `.xcodeproj` if the team's convention is project-first, OR emit a warning when both exist.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). DOCUMENTED. The precedence is stated in docs/architecture/lua-host-api.md:208: find_project_path returns an explicit path unchanged if given, else the FIRST *.xcworkspace or *.xcodeproj found in cwd — workspace before project. Pinning it explicitly via the manifest is the documented override, which is what this asked for.

title: Auto-detect product name from pbxproj for mac_process / ios_process
description:
`mac_process` and `ios_process` are required hand-set in admin.toml to make derived-data globs find the built `.app`. They are almost always identical to the `productName` attribute on the target that matches the scheme (mac_scheme / ios_scheme).

Parse `<project>.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` (regex or pbxproj parser) for the matching target's `productName` and use it as a default. Fall back to the scheme name only if pbxproj lookup fails.

Eliminates a manual config step every new apple archetype consumer otherwise has to remember (and which fails silently with "Could not find built app" — see apple-coding-tool deploy_ios incident).

title: Regression test: build_multiplatform must use absolute paths in Docker bind mounts
description:
When `server_dir` is a relative path like `"cctool-server"`, Docker interprets `-v cctool-server:/src` as a *named volume*, not a bind mount, so the container sees an empty `/src` and cargo fails with:

> error: could not find `Cargo.toml` in `/src` or any parent directory

Fixed in 293e256 by wrapping with `os.path.abspath()`. Add a unit test that captures this: render the docker command (or expose the path) and assert the bind-mount path is absolute regardless of how `server_dir` is passed in. Also covers the strip-pass mount on `out_dir`.

title: kill-port: support multiple ports in a single invocation
description:
Currently `kill-port` kills one port at a time. Projects with a frontend dev server and an API server on separate ports would benefit from:

```
./admin kill            # kills all default ports (space-separated list in run)
./admin kill 3000 8080  # kill specific ports
```

Would require:
- `run` to accept a space-separated list of port numbers (e.g. `run = "3000 8080"`)
- `render_kill_port` to iterate and call `kill_port_interactive` for each port
- CLI args to extend (not replace) the default list, or override entirely

title: run_vite_dev: backend_cmd injected into shell unquoted — design gap from #174
description:
\`#174\` fixed \`frontend_dir\` and \`backend_dir\` with \`shlex.quote()\`, but explicitly left \`backend_cmd\` unquoted because it is an intentional shell string (may contain pipes, redirects, etc.):

\`\`\`python
f"cd {shlex.quote(backend_dir)} && {env} {backend_cmd}"
\`\`\`

This is a known gap. If a project ever passes a \`backend_cmd\` value that originates from user input or an env var containing shell metacharacters, it would be vulnerable.

The broader design issue is tracked in #126 (\`run_cmd(shell=True)\` vs argv list). Until that's resolved, callers of \`run_vite_dev\` must ensure \`backend_cmd\` is a trusted, hand-written string — worth documenting on the function signature explicitly.

Short-term fix: add a docstring note to \`backend_cmd\` parameter warning that it is executed verbatim through a shell and must not be constructed from untrusted input.

So the gap #174 left open is exactly as it was. The short-term ask — document on the parameter that it is executed verbatim through a shell and must not be built from untrusted input — now belongs on the BackendCmd field's doc comment at vitedev.go:164.

- Timeout path: call with a port nothing is listening on, assert it returns \`False\` and (optionally) that the warning was emitted

Could use the same exec+regex harness as \`tests/test_logtail.py\`, or wait for #95 (make admin_lib importable directly).

title: deploy --diff alias is now undocumented after desc update
description:
The \`deploy\` command desc was updated from:

> Build, push, and recreate container on Unraid (preserves run config); pass --diff to show drift

to:

> Build, push, and recreate container on Unraid (preserves run config)

The \`--diff\` flag still works (kept for backwards compatibility) but is no longer mentioned anywhere in the TUI or \`--help\` output. A user who knew the old flag won't find documentation for it.

Options:
1. Add a brief note to the \`deploy\` desc: "use \`diff\` command or pass \`--diff\` for drift"
2. Remove \`--diff\` handling from \`deploy\` entirely (it now has a dedicated \`diff\` command)

Option 2 is cleaner — the alias adds complexity for little benefit since \`./admin diff\` is now discoverable. Wait one release cycle before removing in case any scripts use \`./admin deploy --diff\`.

title: remote_container_diff: dict-valued translations (Tmpfs, Sysctls) may produce false positives from non-deterministic ordering
description:
\`remote_container_diff\` calls \`_build_run_args_from_inspect\` twice (for current and last-deploy inspects) and diffs the resulting arg lists. The diff uses \`_pair_args\` + \`sorted()\` on the pairs, which makes flag-value tuples order-independent.

However, \`Tmpfs\` and \`Sysctls\` are dicts. If the same dict is serialized by Docker in different key orders across two inspect calls (e.g. after a container restart), the generated \`--tmpfs\` and \`--sysctl\` args will appear in different positions in the flat arg list — which \`_pair_args\` + \`sorted()\` may or may not normalize correctly depending on the exact flag structure.

Worth adding a test to \`test_docker.py\` or \`test_docker_diff.py\` that constructs two inspects with the same Tmpfs/Sysctls in different dict orders and asserts \`remote_container_diff\` reports no drift.

title: Tmpfs translation: guard against None opts values within the dict
description:
The new `Tmpfs` translation in `_build_run_args_from_inspect` handles the empty-string opts case (`{"/path": ""}` → `--tmpfs /path`) but does not guard against `None` opts values. Some Docker versions or inspection paths may return `{"/path": null}`, which would produce `--tmpfs /path:None` — a broken arg.

Fix: treat `None` opts the same as empty string:
\`\`\`python
for mount_path, opts in (host_cfg.get("Tmpfs") or {}).items():
    spec = f"{mount_path}:{opts}" if opts else mount_path
    args += ["--tmpfs", spec]
\`\`\`

The condition `if opts` already handles `None` (falsy), so this may already be correct — but it's worth adding a test case with `{"/tmp": None}` to confirm the current guard covers it.

title: remote_recreate_container: deploy continues when restore script write fails
description:
If the SSH `cat >` write for the restore script fails (`write_proc.returncode != 0`), the current code prints a warning and continues with the deploy. This is arguably worse than stopping: the user sees "Could not write restore script" but the deploy proceeds, so if the container start fails they have no recovery path.

Options:
1. **Abort** if the restore script write fails (safest — no deploy without a safety net)
2. **Prompt** — ask the user whether to proceed without a restore script
3. **Current behavior** — warn and continue (risk: user thinks they have recovery when they don't)

Related: #127 (general partial-failure hardening).

title: remote_recreate_container: old image SHA may be GC'd between docker load and inspect
description:
The restore script fix (#181) captures `inspect["Image"]` (the old SHA) after `docker load` has transferred the new image. This is correct because the container is still running the old image at that point.

However, once the old tag is overwritten by `docker load`, the old image becomes untagged. If Docker's garbage collector runs between `docker load` and the inspect call (or between stop/rm and the restore script being used), the old SHA could be invalidated — making the restore script reference a non-existent image.

In practice this is rare on Unraid (no automatic GC by default), but worth noting. A `docker image ls --digests` before the transfer could record the old SHA earlier, before the tag is overwritten, giving a more reliable reference window.

title: _HOST_CFG_EXPECTED should group entries by reason with inline comments
description:
The set currently has ~30 keys under a single top-level comment ('Runtime infrastructure / always-populated defaults we intentionally skip'). That comment doesn't distinguish between:

- Fields that are always-zero infrastructure defaults (e.g. `ContainerIDFile`, `AutoRemove`)
- cgroup/CPU resource limits intentionally skipped (e.g. `CpuPeriod`, `NanoCpus`, `PidsLimit`)
- Path-related fields (e.g. `MaskedPaths`, `ReadonlyPaths`)
- Fields skipped but not yet translated, now that we have candidates (e.g. `Tmpfs`, `Sysctls` — see #188)

Grouping with inline comments (similar to `_CONFIG_EXPECTED`) would make it obvious which category a future unknown field should land in and reduce the risk of accidentally suppressing warnings for genuinely important fields.

title: Translate Tmpfs, Sysctls, SecurityOpt, GroupAdd, Ulimits in _build_run_args_from_inspect
description:
These fields were added to `_HOST_CFG_EXPECTED` to suppress false-positive warnings, but they are silently dropped — the container's actual config isn't replayed by `remote_recreate_container`.

Each has a direct `docker run` equivalent:
- `Tmpfs` → `--tmpfs` (in-memory mounts, e.g. `/tmp`)
- `Sysctls` → `--sysctl` (kernel params, e.g. `net.core.somaxconn`)
- `SecurityOpt` → `--security-opt` (e.g. `no-new-privileges:true`, seccomp profiles)
- `GroupAdd` → `--group-add` (extra groups, e.g. video for GPU access)
- `Ulimits` → `--ulimit` (resource limits)

Translating these would make `remote_recreate_container` faithfully reproduce containers that rely on them, and move them from `_HOST_CFG_EXPECTED` (skipped) to `_HOST_CFG_CONSUMED` (translated).

Related: the existing test issue #185 should cover these translations once implemented.

title: resolve_env doesn't support nested ${VAR:-${OTHER:-default}} fallback chains
description:
The regex `[^}]*` in `_ENV_VAR_RE` stops at the first closing brace, making multi-level env var fallbacks impossible. For example, `${PROD_URL:-${UNRAID_APP_URL:-http://localhost}}` would:

- Leave `${UNRAID_APP_URL:-http://localhost}` unexpanded when `PROD_URL` is unset (single-pass, no recursion)
- Append a spurious `}` to the result when `PROD_URL` is set (outer brace is consumed by the match, trailing `}` leaks)

This came up when trying to provide a one-cycle migration fallback for the `UNRAID_APP_URL` → `PROD_URL` rename in the docker-unraid archetype.

title: remote_container_diff masks SSH failure as 'no snapshot found'
description:
In \`remote_container_diff\`, the lastdeploy snapshot is fetched with:

\`\`\`python
snap_proc = subprocess.run(
    ["ssh", host, f"cat {shlex.quote(snapshot_path)} 2>/dev/null"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
if not snap_proc.stdout.strip():
    err(f"No deploy snapshot found at {host}:{snapshot_path} — run a deploy first")
    return 1
\`\`\`

If SSH itself fails (host unreachable, auth error), \`snap_proc.stdout\` is empty and the error message says "No deploy snapshot found" — which is misleading. The real problem is a connectivity failure.

Fix: check \`snap_proc.returncode\` first. SSH auth/connection failures produce non-zero exit codes. Only fall through to "no snapshot" if SSH succeeded (rc 0) but stdout is empty:

\`\`\`python
if snap_proc.returncode != 0:
    err(f"SSH to {host} failed (rc {snap_proc.returncode})")
    return 1
if not snap_proc.stdout.strip():
    err(f"No deploy snapshot found at {host}:{snapshot_path} — run a deploy first")
    return 1
\`\`\`

title: _HOST_CFG_EXPECTED missing Tmpfs, Sysctls, SecurityOpt — will produce false-positive warnings
description:

- \`Sysctls\` — kernel parameter overrides (e.g. \`net.core.somaxconn\`)
- \`SecurityOpt\` — security options (e.g. \`no-new-privileges:true\`, \`seccomp\` profiles)

- \`Runtime\` — container runtime (e.g. \`nvidia\` for GPU containers) — always set, even to \`"runc"\`
- \`PidsLimit\` — process limit
- \`Ulimits\` — resource limits

These should either be added to \`_HOST_CFG_EXPECTED\` (with a comment noting they're skipped) or handled with a translation (e.g. \`Tmpfs\` could emit \`--tmpfs\` args).

title: Restore script uses new image tag — true rollback requires old image SHA
description:
\`remote_recreate_container\` writes a restore script (\`/tmp/<container>-restore.sh\`) before stop/rm. The script contains \`docker run ... <image>\` where \`<image>\` is the new image tag being deployed — because \`docker load\` of the new image has already overwritten the old tag before the restore script is written.

This means the restore script is useful for "retry with the same run args" but not for "roll back to the previous image." The old image data is still on the remote (untagged), reachable by SHA.

To support true rollback:
1. Capture the old image SHA from \`inspect.get("Image")\` (the sha256 string) before loading the new image.
2. Write the restore script using the SHA instead of the tag: \`docker run ... sha256:abc123...\`

The SHA remains valid as long as Docker hasn't garbage-collected the untagged layer. For most use cases this is reliable enough.

title: install.sh shell_rc(): add fish and nushell support
description:
Both fish and nushell are increasingly common, especially among developers who might use this tool. Currently \`shell_rc()\` routes them to \`~/.profile\` (the catch-all default), which neither shell sources.

Correct targets:
- **fish**: \`~/.config/fish/config.fish\` — PATH is set with \`fish_add_path ~/.admin\`, not the bash export syntax
- **nushell**: \`~/.config/nushell/env.nu\` — PATH is set with \`$env.PATH = ($env.PATH | prepend ...)\`

The PATH_LINE string is also shell-syntax-specific (\`export PATH=...\`), so adding fish/nushell support requires either generating shell-appropriate syntax or printing a manual instruction instead of writing to the rc file automatically.

Minimum viable: detect fish/nushell, skip rc-file write, print a manual instruction telling the user what to add.

title: install.sh --force reinstalls unconditionally; consider a narrower --force-dirty flag
description:
The original issue (#164) requested a way to opt out of the dirty-SHA reinstall when the developer knows their changes don't affect installed files. The implemented \`--force\` flag does a full unconditional reinstall, which is broader than needed.

A narrower \`--force-dirty\` flag would strip the \`+dirty\` suffix when comparing SHAs, letting an unchanged-but-dirty tree be treated as up to date. Use case: editing docs, tests, or \`admin.toml\` examples without wanting to trigger a full \`do_install\` on every \`./install.sh\` run.

The two behaviors are different:
- \`--force\`: always reinstall regardless of SHA (useful when working on \`admin_lib/\` directly)
- \`--force-dirty\` (proposed): skip reinstall if base SHA matches, even if tree is dirty (useful when working on non-installed files)

Not urgent — \`--force\` covers most cases. Worth revisiting if the dirty-install-every-commit cycle becomes painful.

title: manifest parse() silently ignores unknown top-level keys
description:
`gen/manifest.py`'s `parse()` uses `data.get()` for every field it knows about and ignores everything else. A typo like `excude_modules` or `exlude_modules` will be silently swallowed — the manifest appears valid but the intended key has no effect.

This makes `exclude_modules` (and any other new key) especially fragile: a one-character typo produces no error and no warning, just unexpected behavior at runtime.

Fix: collect all recognized keys, then warn (or raise) if `data` contains any keys outside that set. Low-effort given parse() already touches every key explicitly. Related to #58.

title: manifest dump() silently drops exclude_modules on round-trip
description:
`gen/manifest.py`'s `dump()` function is a hand-rolled TOML emitter that only knows about the fields it was originally written for. The newly added `exclude_modules` field is not emitted, so a `--regenerate` round-trip will silently drop it from admin.toml and re-include the excluded modules on the next build.

Repro:
1. Add `exclude_modules = ["log_columns"]` to admin.toml
2. Run `init-admin --regenerate`
3. Observe admin.toml now lacks `exclude_modules`; the generated admin bundles log_columns again

Fix: add `exclude_modules` to `dump()`'s output, guarded by `if manifest.exclude_modules:`.

Related to #58 (manifest dump() silently drops unknown keys on round-trip).

title: Generic column Timestamp shows current time, not the source log timestamp
description:
`_reformat_generic_line` in `log_columns.py` normalizes the Timestamp column to `datetime.now()`:

```python
field_map = {
    "Timestamp": datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S.%f"),
    ...
}
```

The original timestamp extracted from the raw line by `strip_log_timestamp` is discarded. For real-time processes this is fine, but for buffered, replayed, or delayed logs the displayed timestamp is the ingestion time rather than the event time. This matches `LogFormatter`'s behavior but is worth revisiting for column mode where the Timestamp column is explicitly visible.

Possible fix: use the extracted source timestamp when present, fall back to `datetime.now()` only when the line had no parseable timestamp.

title: _find_level_color does redundant search before loop
description:
`_find_level_color` in `admin_lib/log_columns.py` does:

```python
def _find_level_color(text: str) -> str | None:
    if _LEVEL_RE.search(text):           # first pass
        for pat, color in _LEVEL_COLORS:
            if pat.search(text):          # second pass
                return color
    return None
```

The outer `_LEVEL_RE.search()` check is redundant — the inner loop already handles the no-match case by falling through to `return None`. The fix is to remove the outer guard and let the loop do the work:

```python
def _find_level_color(text: str) -> str | None:
    for pat, color in _LEVEL_COLORS:
        if pat.search(text):
            return color
    return None
```

Minor efficiency and clarity cleanup — two regex passes become one.
