title: sequence kind: support per-step fixed args
description:
Allow sequence steps to carry fixed args alongside the command name, for cases where you always want a specific subcommand variant:

\`\`\`toml
[commands.dev]
kind  = "sequence"
desc  = "Dev plugin and reload"
steps = [
  {cmd = "build", args = ["plugin"]},
  "reload",
]
\`\`\`

Mixed list — plain strings use no args, tables use the specified args. Useful when a sequence should always target a specific variant of a multi-target command without prompting the user.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — inherited. A command's `steps` is a plain []string and each entry is passed to RunActionRouted by name (internal/kinds/dispatch.go:246-250); there is no {cmd=, args=} table form. Related: admin-1qte, where the port silently settled the args-forwarding question these two share.

title: http kind: optionally print response body for debugging
description:
Currently `kind = "http"` discards the response body on success. For debugging webhook integrations it would be useful to see what the server returned.

Could be a manifest flag:

\`\`\`toml
[commands.reload]
kind    = "http"
run     = "${STASH_URL}/graphql"
body    = '{"query": "mutation { reloadPlugins }"}'
verbose = true   # print response body
\`\`\`

Or always print in verbose mode (`./admin reload --verbose`). Response body should be capped/truncated to avoid flooding the terminal.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — inherited. internal/kinds/http.go closes the response body at :72 without reading it, so the response is discarded on success exactly as before.

title: http kind: support configurable request headers
description:
Currently `kind = "http"` always sends `Content-Type: application/json` when a body is set. Some webhooks need different content types (form-encoded data, custom auth headers, etc.).

Proposed manifest syntax:

\`\`\`toml
[commands.notify]
kind    = "http"
run     = "${WEBHOOK_URL}"
method  = "POST"
body    = "status=deployed"
headers = {"Content-Type" = "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "X-Token" = "${WEBHOOK_TOKEN}"}
\`\`\`

`headers` would be a TOML inline table. Env var expansion should apply to header values. The `Content-Type: application/json` default only kicks in when no `headers` key is present.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — inherited. internal/kinds/http.go:63 sets `req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")` when a body is present and there is no `headers` key in the action schema. The proposed TOML inline-table syntax is unchanged in shape; env expansion for header values would go through manifest.ResolveEnv, the same call the body already uses at http.go:48.

title: Show stale generator warning in --help output, not just TUI
description:
The stale generator warning (shown when `~/.admin/VERSION` differs from the bundled SHA) only appears in the interactive TUI. Non-TTY users running `./admin --help` or `./admin` in CI won't see it.

Should print the same dim notice at the top of `_print_help()` output when `_stale_generator` is True.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — this describes the generator/bundler architecture (admin-gen, gen/, the bundled ./admin, generator_commit, templates/), which was already replaced by interpreter mode (ADR-0006) and is now replaced again by the Go binary. None of the named code has a successor: `admin compile` is dropped by admin-3rgp.30, and there is no code-generation step left to audit, bundle or re-bundle. There is no generator, so no stale-generator warning to surface.

title: Decide sequence args-forwarding behavior
description:
Currently `kind = "sequence"` passes `[]` to each step — args given to the sequence are silently dropped.

Three possible designs:
1. **Drop args (current)** — sequences are fixed workflows, args are meaningless
2. **Forward to all steps** — `./admin dev plugin` passes `["plugin"]` to each step in the sequence
3. **Forward to first step only** — reasonable for sequences that start with a dispatch step

Need to decide before more sequences are built in downstream projects, since changing this is a breaking behavior change. Document the chosen behavior in README.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). DECIDED BY THE PORT, STILL UNDOCUMENTED. The Go dispatcher picked option 2: internal/kinds/dispatch.go:246-250 forwards the SAME args slice to every step of a command. So `admin dev plugin` passes ["plugin"] to each step, not []. That resolves the breaking-change risk this bead was filed to head off — the behaviour is now shipped — and reduces the bead to its second half: write it down. docs/architecture/design.md is the place, and it is stale generally (see admin-1vnl), so this can ride along with that rewrite.

title: Simplify stash-reels admin.toml using http + sequence kinds
description:
Now that `kind = "http"` and `kind = "sequence"` exist, stash-reels' ~260-line admin.toml can be significantly trimmed.

The three copy-pasted `_reload_plugins` / `_load_dotenv` / `_stash_url` helper blocks across `dev` and `deploy` collapse into a single `reload` http command:

\`\`\`toml
[commands.reload]
kind   = "http"
desc   = "Reload Stash plugins"
run    = "${STASH_URL:-http://localhost:9999}/graphql"
method = "POST"
body   = '{"query": "mutation { reloadPlugins }"}'
\`\`\`

And the deploy/dev commands become sequences referencing the appropriate sub-steps. Combined with the nested command syntax (see #146), the entire file should shrink to ~40 lines.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — a downstream cleanup, unaffected in substance. kind=http exists (internal/kinds/http.go) and step sequencing is now [commands.X].steps rather than kind="sequence", so the collapse this describes is still available with slightly different syntax. Two dependencies to note: the nested-command syntax it assumes is admin-xt6s (still unbuilt), and every step of a command receives the same args (admin-1qte), which may change how the dev/deploy sequences are written.

title: Nested command syntax: [commands.build.plugin] dot notation
description:
Dot notation in TOML section headers to define subcommands directly, auto-generating a picker parent.

Instead of one monolithic `[commands.build]` block with `pick_target()` and if/elif dispatch, you'd write:

\`\`\`toml
[commands.build.plugin]
kind = "shell"
desc = "Build plugin"
run  = "npm run build"

[commands.build.ios]
kind = "python"
desc = "Build iOS"
run  = "..."
\`\`\`

The generator detects that `build` has children and emits a parent command that calls `pick_target({...})` and dispatches. This would dramatically clean up projects like stash-reels where every top-level command (build/dev/deploy) splits on the same plugin/ios axis.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL — inherited. There is no dot-notation subcommand syntax: a [commands.X] entry is pure routing (desc + steps, enforced by checkPureRouting at internal/kinds/dispatch.go:240) and target-splitting is done by kind="multi-target" under [actions]. The picker this bead wants auto-generated already exists as multi-target's own (internal/kinds/multitarget.go:195-212) — so the ask reduces to a manifest-frontend sugar that expands [commands.build.plugin] into a multi-target action, not new runtime machinery. Worth weighing against ADR-0003 before building.

title: dirty-tree guard blocks regenerate during normal dev iteration
description:
`--force-dirty` is required whenever admin-project-tool is installed from an uncommitted working tree, which happens constantly during development. This means every edit-install-regenerate cycle requires the flag.

Consider a local dev mode (e.g. a `.admin-dev` sentinel file or an env var) that skips the guard automatically when working on the tool itself.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — this describes the generator/bundler architecture (admin-gen, gen/, the bundled ./admin, generator_commit, templates/), which was already replaced by interpreter mode (ADR-0006) and is now replaced again by the Go binary. None of the named code has a successor: `admin compile` is dropped by admin-3rgp.30, and there is no code-generation step left to audit, bundle or re-bundle. There is no regenerate step and no dirty-tree guard on one.

title: install module: pip detector fails if venv doesn't exist yet
description: The `requirements.txt` detector runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` directly, which fails if no virtualenv is active. `uv sync` (the `pyproject.toml` detector) creates a venv automatically. The pip path should either check for an active venv first, use `uv pip install` instead, or be documented as requiring manual venv setup. Also worth auditing whether `cargo fetch` vs `go mod download` is the right pairing — both are correct but the asymmetry is worth a comment.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — admin_lib/install.py and its per-manifest detectors (requirements.txt / pyproject.toml / Cargo.toml / go.mod) were not ported. The dependency-freshness check that did survive is the deps-fresh guard (internal/guards/deps_fresh.go), which is node/bun-workspace-specific and installs nothing.

title: install module: no escape hatch for custom skip dirs
description: The `_SKIP_DIRS` set in `admin_lib/install.py` is hardcoded. Projects with non-standard cache or build directories (e.g. `.turbo`, `.nx`, `_build` for Elixir) will be walked and may surface false-positive manifests. Add support for a `[install] skip_dirs = [...]` config field in `admin.toml` so projects can extend the skip list without touching the module.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — admin_lib/install.py and its _SKIP_DIRS set were not ported. There is no `install` kind in the Go catalog (internal/kinds/catalog.go) and no [install] config table, so there is no hardcoded skip list to make extensible.

title: Generated ./admin is 2000 lines — shrink it or mark as generated
description:
Every archetype change regenerates `./admin` in every downstream project with a ~2000-line diff that buries the signal. The file is a bundled, self-contained Python script by design (no runtime imports from ~/.admin), but that design choice makes commits loud and diff noisy.

Options:
- Add `admin linguist-generated=true` to downstream `.gitattributes` so GitHub hides it from PR diffs by default (low effort, doesn't change local git experience).
- Support an optional "trampoline" mode: a 30-line `./admin` that execs `~/.admin/admin-run PROJECT_DIR`, for users who explicitly opt in via `admin.toml` and accept the runtime dependency on `~/.admin`.
- Keep the bundled file as-is but move it to `.admin/admin` and add a tiny `./admin` shim that just `exec`s it — same UX, smaller top-level noise.

Not urgent; fixing it properly touches every consumer project.

title: Warn when docker inspect returns fields _build_run_args_from_inspect doesn't consume
description:
`admin_lib/docker.py::_build_run_args_from_inspect` consumes a hand-curated subset of `docker inspect` JSON. If a future Docker release renames or adds a field (e.g. `HostConfig.GPUs`, sysctls, ulimits, health check overrides not captured anywhere in our extractor), the recreate will silently drop that config.

Add a debug-level log listing any populated keys under `HostConfig` / `Config` / `NetworkSettings` that we did not translate, so drift shows up the first time someone deploys a container using those features.

title: Add `./admin deploy --diff` to surface run-config drift
description:
`remote_recreate_container` silently preserves whatever happens to be on the live container — including accidental Unraid GUI tweaks between deploys. A `--diff` mode that compares the current inspect output against the previous deploy's captured config (stash it in `/tmp/` or `.admin-lastdeploy.json` on the remote) would let you spot unintended changes before they become load-bearing.

Related: admin-project-tool/admin_lib/docker.py::_build_run_args_from_inspect.

title: Harden remote_recreate_container against partial-failure state
description:
If docker stop/rm succeeds but the subsequent docker run fails (bad args, corrupted image, wrong network), the old container is already gone and the deploy leaves the remote in a broken state — no container, no easy recovery without hand-running a docker run from GUI template config.

Options:
- Snapshot inspect, try run, and only stop/rm after new container is confirmed healthy (requires temporary rename and port-juggling for same-name semantics).
- Cache the reconstructed docker run command to a tmp file on the remote so rollback is a single `bash /tmp/wfm-prev.sh`.
- Add a `--dry-run` flag that prints the docker run it would execute so you can eyeball it first.

Surfaces in admin-project-tool/admin_lib/docker.py::remote_recreate_container.

comments.text:
[migrated from GitHub #127] @McBrideMusings at 2026-04-27T02:33:39Z:

title: run_cmd(shell=True) is unnecessary when the archetype already has args as a list
description:
The forge-engine archetype's `dev` command (and by extension any archetype doing `subprocess` via shell strings) currently does:

\`\`\`python
cmd = shlex.quote(binary) + \" \" + shlex.quote(project_dir)
run_cmd(cmd)
\`\`\`

This works but passes through a shell unnecessarily. `run_cmd` in admin_lib/core.py accepts `shell=True` by default; exposing a `shell=False` path (or a sibling `run_argv(argv: list[str])` helper) would let archetypes pass argv lists and avoid the quoting dance entirely.

This is a broader refactor: many archetypes would benefit (anywhere a command builds up with user-influenced substrings). Worth doing once and propagating.

Scope:
- admin_lib/core.py: `run_cmd` to accept either a `str` (shell mode) or a `list[str]` (argv mode); formatter/logging invariants preserved.
- Update call sites in existing archetypes that build commands from dynamic parts.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, RE-POINTED. The Python run_cmd(shell=True) is gone, but the shape survived: luahost.Host.RunCmd takes a command STRING and runs it through a shell, and archetypes build those strings by concatenation with a shellQuote helper (e.g. internal/kinds/vitedev.go:188, :242). There is no argv-list entry point. So the same quoting dance is still required at every call site that interpolates a dynamic value, and the same class of bug is still available. Re-scope to: add an argv variant to the host API and move the archetype call sites that build from dynamic parts onto it.

title: forge-engine detector doesn't trigger at bootstrap
description:
Bootstrapping forge-engine on 2026-04-21 fell through to the `simple` fallback archetype even though:

- `detectors/forge-engine.py` was installed at `~/.admin/detectors/forge-engine.py`
- Both match conditions were true (`engine/build.zig` exists + `sample-games/` directory exists)
- `admin.toml` had to be hand-edited to `archetypes = ["forge-engine"]` then `--regenerate` run.

Possible causes:
- Detector iteration order runs `simple` or another fallback first and short-circuits.
- `is_dir()` check on `sample-games/` was evaluated before the directory existed in the test run (unlikely; dir was created first).
- Detector loading requires a non-pycache refresh that `install.sh` didn't do cleanly.

Repro:
1. Start a fresh repo with `engine/build.zig` and `sample-games/` siblings.
2. Run `~/.admin/init-admin .`.
3. Observe "detector matched: fallback" in stdout.

Expected: "detector matched: forge-engine".
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, AND THE CAUSE IS NOW LOCATED — it is neither of the three guesses in the bead. The forge-engine detector is deliberately absent from the run order: internal/detect/detect.go:37-43 says so outright ('forge-engine has a detector (detectForgeEngine, registered in Registry) and a matching archetype directory, but is deliberately absent from Order: admin_lib.detectors.DETECTOR_ORDER never lists it either, so it never runs'). detectForgeEngine (detectors.go:387-392) checks exactly the two conditions the bead says were true — engine/build.zig and sample-games/ — and would have matched; it is simply never called. raylib-game is in the same position (detectors.go:395). SECOND, LARGER FINDING: nothing in the repo imports internal/detect at all (grep for the import path finds only a doc spike), and there is no `admin new` verb — 'new' appears only in cmd/manifest.go:23's reservedToolVerbs list. So the detectors are ported but entirely unwired: there is no bootstrap path in Go for any detector to run from. Fixing this bead means adding forge-engine to Order AND giving the port a bootstrap verb.

title: dev_macos_postprocess doesn't validate input is an .app bundle
description:
`admin_lib/apple.dev_macos_postprocess(built_app_path, dev_product_name, dev_display_name)` (added in 0ee8f92) renames whatever path it's given. If a caller passes a non-bundle path (typo, wrong glob, `find_app()` returned None-becomes-empty-string), the function will:

1. Rename the path (silently succeeds for any existing dir/file).
2. plutil fails on missing `Contents/Info.plist` → warn.
3. codesign may succeed or fail on garbage input → warn or silent.
4. Return a path the caller thinks is a valid `.app`.

A two-line sanity check at the top would catch the typo class:

\`\`\`python
if not built_app_path.endswith(".app") or not os.path.isdir(built_app_path):
    raise ValueError(f"dev_macos_postprocess: not an .app bundle: {built_app_path!r}")
if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(built_app_path, "Contents", "Info.plist")):
    raise ValueError(f"dev_macos_postprocess: missing Info.plist in {built_app_path!r}")
\`\`\`

Arguable whether to raise or `err()` + return None; match whatever the rest of `admin_lib/apple.py` does with precondition failures (currently mixed).

title: iOS home-screen display name differentiation: playbook for the .xcconfig workaround
description:
The module docstring in `admin_lib/apple.py` (added in 0ee8f92) documents the known gap: distinct iOS dev/prod home-screen display names cannot be achieved via global xcodebuild flags because `INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDisplayName` cascades to SwiftPM resource bundles and breaks the build (see #44).

The workaround is project-level: a per-target `.xcconfig` variant, or a dual-Info.plist setup, or a user-defined build setting referenced by Info.plist. None of that lives in admin-project-tool.

If the gap bites in a future project, capture the concrete working setup as a playbook in `docs/` (or an answer in CLAUDE.md when one exists). For now, the docstring flag is enough.

title: Collapse repeated subprocess.run(capture_output=True) pattern in apple.py
description:
`admin_lib/apple.py` has ~a dozen call sites that do `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` and then either ignore the output, decode stderr manually, or check the return code. The 0ee8f92 `dev_macos_postprocess` added two more.

A small `_quiet_run(cmd) -> (returncode, stderr_str)` helper would collapse all of them into a consistent shape:

\`\`\`python
def _quiet_run(cmd):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True)
    return r.returncode, r.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
\`\`\`

Micro-cleanup, no behavior change. Worth doing when someone next touches apple.py for a larger reason.

title: Migrate downstream Apple projects to apple.dev_macos_postprocess
description:
Now that `admin_lib/apple.dev_macos_postprocess()` exists (added in 0ee8f92), downstream Apple projects can delete their open-coded rename / plutil / codesign blocks and call the helper.

Known project carrying the open-coded pattern:
- `apple-coding-tool/admin_inline.py:341-359` — the canonical reference this helper was lifted from.

Other candidates: grep `~/Projects/apple-*` for `plutil -replace CFBundleDisplayName` and `codesign --force --sign -`.

Migration per project:
1. Re-bundle the project against current admin-project-tool HEAD so `apple.dev_macos_postprocess` is in scope.
2. Replace the rename+plutil+codesign block with `renamed = dev_macos_postprocess(built, MAC_DEV_PRODUCT_NAME, "<display name>")`.
3. Verify `./admin dev mac` still produces the same `.app`.

Related: #42 (scaffolding for future projects), #43 (re-bundle sweep).
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, RE-POINTED. dev_macos_postprocess survived the port as a Lua binding — apple.dev_macos_postprocess(built_app_path, dev_product_name, dev_display_name[, sign_identity]) (docs/architecture/lua-host-api.md:194) — so downstream projects can still delete their open-coded rename/plutil/codesign blocks and call it. Two changes to the migration: there is no re-bundle step any more (step 1 of the bead's recipe drops), and the caller is now a Lua archetype body or a manifest action, not inline Python. Also note the tool itself does not call it — the mac dev-rename postprocessing is a documented unported gap (internal/kinds/apple_darwin.go:14-21) — so a project wanting it must invoke it explicitly.

title: No drift detection on downstream ./admin generator_commit
description:
Generated `./admin` scripts embed a `generator_commit=<sha>` field in the `# @bundled` header. We have no tooling that surfaces "this project's generated `./admin` is N commits behind admin-project-tool HEAD."

The #101 audit (closed) made this obvious: 17 of 19 downstream scripts are at various older generator commits, and the only way to know is manual grep.

Possible directions:
- `~/.admin/init-admin --audit <repo>` (exists) could also flag stale `generator_commit` against `~/.admin/VERSION`.
- A `~/.admin/init-admin --audit-all ~/Projects` sweep that lists stale repos with their delta.

Related to #43 (re-bundle sweep).
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). None of the named code has a successor: `admin compile` is dropped by admin-3rgp.30, and there is no code-generation step left to audit, bundle or re-bundle. generator_commit does not exist. A single installed binary replaces N generated scripts, so there is no per-project staleness to detect.

description:
`tail_local` gained a `poll_interval=0.25` kwarg in d717e0b (closes #108) to let tests inject a tight interval. Not exposed anywhere user-facing — users can't tune it without editing the generated script.

Probably fine — it's a test knob. If per-project tuning ever matters, consider threading it through from `admin.toml`'s `[logs.<target>]` (e.g. `poll_interval = 0.1`) and through `register_logs_command` / `cmd_logs` to `tail_local`.

title: register_logs_command closure pattern makes cmd_logs awkward to test
description:
`cmd_logs` is created inside `register_logs_command(spec)`'s closure in `admin_lib/logtail.py` and registered via the `@command` decorator. Testing it requires a special loader (`_load_logtail_for_cmd`, added in d717e0b to close #102) that captures decorator registrations via a fake `command` stub and then pulls `cmd_logs` out by name.

Cleaner: top-level `cmd_logs(spec, args)` with a thin `register_logs_command(spec)` shim that wires it into the registry. Testable directly without a decorator harness.

Defer until the next change to the logs command flow.

title: SSH stderr thread join timeout of 1s may truncate error output
description:
`tail_remote` in `admin_lib/logtail.py` joins the stderr daemon thread with `timeout=1` after the SSH process exits. If SSH is slow to flush/close stderr on an orderly shutdown, we may drop the tail of the error message — exactly the context we need for the structured error report added to close #99.

Possible directions:
- Extend the join timeout on orderly exits (e.g. 5s if `proc.returncode == 0` or SSH closed gracefully).
- Instead of a timeout, block until the stderr pipe closes.

Low priority; file it here so it isn't lost.

title: Make logtail rotation tests deterministic by injecting poll interval
description:
Summary
`test_logtail.py` currently relies on timing assumptions such as 0.5 second sleeps and a 0.25 second poll interval. On loaded CI, the rotation test could miss its window if the tailer polls late.

Problem
Time-based tests are vulnerable to scheduler noise and CI load, which makes failures intermittent and hard to trust.

Requested change
Make `tail_local` accept an injectable poll interval so tests can run deterministically with tighter control.

Why this matters
- Reduces flakiness in CI
- Makes the rotation test deterministic
- Separates production polling defaults from test timing

Acceptance criteria
- `tail_local` can use an injected poll interval in tests
- Rotation coverage no longer depends on coarse sleeps
- Existing runtime behavior remains unchanged by default

title: Avoid binary-log peek when caller will immediately seek to EOF
description:
Summary
The binary-log detection path always reads 512 bytes to check for NULs, even when the caller will immediately seek to EOF.

Problem
The cost is negligible, but it is still unnecessary I/O in a path that may run often against large rotating logs.

Priority
Low priority.

Requested change
Skip the binary peek when the subsequent control flow will seek to EOF and never use the initial bytes.

Acceptance criteria
- The optimization is only applied where it preserves behavior
- The tailing logic still correctly handles binary logs
- Any complexity added is justified by the simplification or clarity of the control flow

title: Consider chunked SSH stderr reads instead of readline in daemon thread
description:
Summary
The SSH stderr daemon thread currently uses `readline()`. If SSH emits a long prefix without a trailing newline before exiting, stderr can appear late.

Problem
Line-buffered reads delay partial stderr visibility. That can hide useful failure context until process teardown.

Priority
Low priority.

Requested change
Evaluate switching the stderr reader from `readline()` to chunked raw reads so partial output becomes visible sooner.

Acceptance criteria
- Behavior is reviewed with at least one failure case in mind
- If changed, stderr is surfaced promptly even without newline-terminated output
- If not changed, document why the current tradeoff is acceptable

title: Document origin-string format as a compatibility contract

title: wtree should support explicit --yes for non-interactive use
description:
Summary
`wtree` currently relies on non-TTY stdin returning empty and treating that as an implicit yes. That makes non-interactive behavior surprising and fragile.

Problem
The current behavior bit us in this session: automation got a silent affirmative because stdin was non-interactive. That is hard to discover and creates a hidden contract around empty input.

Requested change
Add an explicit `--yes` flag for non-interactive use and require callers to opt in to automatic confirmation.

Why this matters
- More robust than inferring intent from non-TTY stdin
- Less surprising for scripts and CI
- Makes the non-interactive contract explicit and documentable

Acceptance criteria
- `wtree --yes` skips the prompt in non-interactive contexts
- Non-interactive use without `--yes` does not silently proceed
- Help text documents the flag and intended scripting behavior
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). HALF DONE — the flag landed, the contract did not. `admin worktree --yes/-y` exists (cmd/worktree.go:48-49, :54) and `admin branch` has the same flag (branch.go:54). But the surprising half is unchanged: cmd/prompt.go falls back to a line read when stdin is not a TTY (:40) and treats an EMPTY line as yes (:45 — `case "", "y", "yes": return true`). So automation still gets a silent affirmative from EOF, which is the exact behaviour this bead was filed about. Remaining acceptance criterion: non-interactive use without --yes must not proceed. One-line fix at cmd/prompt.go:44-47 — drop "" from the accepting case, or return false outright when stdin is not a terminal.

title: Add unit test for cmd_logs non-TTY early-exit path
description:
Summary
There is currently no unit test covering the `cmd_logs` non-TTY early-exit path. The new `_require_interactive` branches were only exercised manually.

Problem
If `pick_target` semantics change later, the current behavior could regress without automated coverage.

Requested change
Add a unit test that exercises the non-interactive branch and asserts the command exits early with the expected status and messaging.

Why this matters
- Protects the new `_require_interactive` behavior
- Prevents accidental changes to CLI scripting semantics
- Moves manual-only validation into CI

Acceptance criteria
- Test covers non-TTY invocation of `cmd_logs`
- Test asserts the early exit behavior
- Test fails if `pick_target` changes break the intended contract

title: ./admin logs in non-TTY silently exits when target/env is ambiguous

In non-TTY (scripted) contexts `pick_target` returns None and we exit silently with code 0. Should print a clear error like 'logs: target required in non-interactive context (have: app, worker)' and exit non-zero.

title: v2: polish — info('running:') shows resolved, not literal, command
description:
Cosmetic bug in render_shell fragment. Today:

    info("running: hugo ${DEPLOY_HOST}")
    rc = run_cmd("hugo ${DEPLOY_HOST}")

The info line prints the literal placeholder before resolve_env fires inside run_cmd, which is confusing when the var is unset (you see 'running: ...${DEPLOY_HOST}...' immediately before the 'required env var DEPLOY_HOST is not set' error).

Fix: emit `info(f"running: {resolve_env(<cmd>)}")` OR move the info log inside run_cmd itself. Second option is cleaner — kills the duplicate 'running:' chatter in every command function.

Low priority but worth fixing before shipping more archetypes (otherwise the pattern propagates).

Only PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER is SwiftPM-safe as a global override. Add a warning comment near any apple.py helpers that accept extra_settings, or a docstring note in the new dev_macos_postprocess helper (#40).

title: Migrate apple-coding-tool to dispatch_target
description:
apple-coding-tool's hand-written admin uses the older `pick_target` + manual if/elif dispatch pattern. Migrating it to `dispatch_target` would:

- Serve as a proof-of-concept for the new pattern on a real complex project (4 targets: macOS, iOS, server, bazzite)
- Validate that `dispatch_target` handles all the edge cases in practice
- Reduce boilerplate in the admin file
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). STILL REAL, RE-POINTED. dispatch_target and the pick_target + if/elif pattern are both Python that no longer exists; the modern equivalent is kind="multi-target" (internal/kinds/multitarget.go), which does the target picking, per-target guards and per-target frame handling generically. The proof-of-concept value this bead is really about stands: migrate apple-coding-tool's hand-written admin onto the Go multi-target kind across its four targets, and see which edge cases it does not cover.

title: Add --dry-run to multi-target generation
description:
Add a `--dry-run` flag to `init-admin` that prints the composed multi-target admin to stdout without writing the file. Useful for debugging template assembly and reviewing output before committing.

Single-target generation could also benefit from this, but multi-target is where the fragment composition makes it most valuable.

title: Multi-scheme xcodeproj detection
description:
Currently a single `.xcodeproj` with both macOS and iOS schemes only detects one platform (based on `SDKROOT`/`IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` in the pbxproj). Projects like apple-coding-tool have one xcodeproj with separate macOS and iOS schemes.

Parse scheme lists from `xcodebuild -list -project <path> -json` to detect multiple platform targets from a single xcodeproj. This would let init-admin generate both `macos` and `ios` targets automatically instead of just one.
close_reason: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). MOOT — this is init-admin generation work, and init-admin is deleted. The `xcodebuild -list -json` scheme parsing this proposes has no consumer: the Apple pbxproj reader is used for build settings, not scheme enumeration (docs/architecture/lua-host-api.md:209-211), and the detectors are not wired to anything (admin-x6tn).

title: kinds.CommandNames duplicates manifest.CommandNames
description:
Two functions build the same command-name set — Custom union Overrides — with nothing checking that they agree:

- internal/manifest/manifest.go:461, (*Manifest).CommandNames() map[string]bool
- internal/kinds/dispatch.go:85, CommandNames(m *manifest.Manifest) []string — the same set, de-duplicated and sorted, used by cmd/root.go:143 to name a project's commands when a typed word matches nothing.

A command source added to one (a new archetype tier, say) leaves the other silently narrower. Concretely: `admin check` would report a valid [keys.<row-kind>] binding as naming a missing command, or the CLI's "did you mean" list would omit a command that exists.

kinds.CommandNames should be sortedKeys(m.CommandNames()) rather than its own walk.

History: this was originally filed against cmd/check.go's local commandNames() helper, which was a THIRD copy. The admin-l6kb.2 pass (landed as 5308c1f) deleted that one and moved it onto Manifest, taking three copies down to two. This ticket is the remaining pair.

title: install.sh prints a link path it did not use
description:
Run from the primary checkout, install.sh printed:

  admin-project-tool: linked to /Users/pierce/.worktrees/admin-project-tool/hosted-pty-drain/admin_lib — Python edits are already live

while the symlink it actually wrote points at the primary checkout:

  ~/.admin/admin_lib -> /Users/pierce/Projects/admin-project-tool/admin_lib

The printed path was a stale worktree that was about to be torn down. Believing the message means concluding the install is about to dangle and `admin` is about to break system-wide, which invites a "fix" that breaks the install that was in fact correct. Reproduced 2026-09-01 04:37 UTC (12:37am ET) after a worker had previously run install.sh from inside its own worktree.

The message should name the path it linked, not a remembered or previously-configured one.
acceptance_criteria: install.sh's link line names the path in the symlink it just wrote. Running it from the primary checkout after a worktree install prints the primary checkout path.

title: A nudged row says so in the Work tab
description:
A nudge that leaves no trace is unverifiable. A worker that was nudged and a worker that
unblocked itself look identical in the Work tab — including to the person checking whether
the orchestrator works at all.

The Work tab shows that the orchestrator sent a nudge to a row, and when.

HITL: the wording and the placement are a judgment call against a row that is already
dense, and the same rendering has open regressions (`admin-4s8d`, the badge counting target
rows; `admin-3rlr`, the submenu on a running multi-target command). Decide where this goes
in relation to those rather than layering onto a row that is about to change.

## Out of scope

A nudge history longer than the most recent one.
acceptance_criteria:
- A row whose entry was nudged is visibly distinguishable from one that was not.
- The display names when the nudge was sent, not only that one was.
- A row that has never been nudged renders exactly as it does today.
- The change is verified by screenshot against the running dashboard, not by test alone.

title: Decide whether livework keeps a retry op now that nothing calls it
description:
## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Decide whether the live-work registry keeps a retry operation now that nothing in the interface offers one.

## Current behavior

Retry was removed from the Work tab: the key binding, the footer hint, the worker-detail action and the handler are all gone. The reason is that restarting a live thing under the same identity is not something every producer can honour or every kind of work can survive — an agent session half-way through editing a worktree is not safely restartable, and neither is a dev loop holding a port.

The registry still carries the machinery. `Ops.Retry` is a field on every entry, `Registry.Retry` is exported with its own state checks, and two producers still populate it.

## Desired behavior

One of two, decided rather than defaulted:

- **Remove it.** No caller means no contract to maintain, and a populated field nothing invokes is a trap for the next reader, who will reasonably assume something calls it.
- **Keep it as a programmatic-only affordance,** with the doc comment saying explicitly that it has no interface surface and why — so it reads as a deliberate API rather than an oversight.

The decision hinges on whether anything outside the dashboard is expected to drive the registry. If nothing is, the first option is right.

Whichever is chosen, the producers that populate it are updated to match, and no code is left constructing a value nothing can reach.

## Key interfaces

- The registry entry's operation set, and the exported retry method.
- The two producers that supply a retry implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The decision is recorded in the registry's own doc comment.
- [ ] If removed: no field, no exported method, no producer supplies one, and nothing references it.
- [ ] If kept: the doc comment states it has no interface surface and names why it exists.
- [ ] The retry-related tests match whichever way it went.
- [ ] No producer constructs a retry implementation that nothing can invoke.

## Out of scope

- Re-adding a retry affordance to the interface. That was removed deliberately.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
acceptance_criteria: The decision is recorded in the registry's doc comment. If removed: no field, no exported method, no producer supplies one, nothing references it. If kept: the comment states it has no interface surface and why. Retry tests match. No producer constructs an implementation nothing can invoke.

Measured on iptv-mac: 16 with everything collapsed, 21 with 'dev' open — the number moves while the set of available commands has not. internal/tui/work.go:580 — 'if r.kind == rowCommand || r.kind == rowCommandTarget || r.kind == rowWorker {'.

title: Delete the admin-tui-desktop prototype once its tickets land
description:
## Parent

admin-3rgp

## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Delete `docs/spikes/admin-tui-desktop/` once every ticket that cites it has landed.

## Current behavior

The prototype is committed reference material: a runnable Bubble Tea program plus 23 dumped frames that the Work-tab tickets cite by path. It is the fixed target an implementing agent compares against, and the thing a reviewer can read without launching anything.

That is only true while the shipped code has not caught up. Once it has, the frames stop being a target and start being a second, stale account of a screen that already exists — and a stale picture gets argued with more readily than stale markup.

## Desired behavior

The whole directory is removed: the build, the frames, and the `prototype` sub-target in `admin.toml` that opens it. Nothing in the repo references it afterwards.

This issue is blocked by every ticket that cites the prototype, so it only becomes ready once the work it described is done. That dependency is the point — it makes the cleanup arrive on its own instead of needing to be noticed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/spikes/admin-tui-desktop/` no longer exists.
- [ ] The `prototype` sub-target naming it is removed from `admin.toml`, and `admin check` still resolves.
- [ ] A repo-wide grep for `admin-tui-desktop` returns nothing outside closed issue history.
- [ ] No remaining ticket body cites a frame under that path.

## Out of scope

- Deleting any other spike.
- Removing the `prototype` command itself — only this sub-target.

## Blocked by

Every ticket citing the prototype.
acceptance_criteria: docs/spikes/admin-tui-desktop/ no longer exists. The prototype sub-target naming it is removed from admin.toml and admin check still resolves. A repo-wide grep for admin-tui-desktop returns nothing outside closed issue history. No remaining ticket body cites a frame under that path.

title: Six files are not gofmt-clean and admin.toml has no fmt or vet command to catch it
description: gofmt -l reports: cmd/root.go, internal/dockerrun/deployfiles_test.go, internal/dockerrun/dockerrun_test.go, internal/dockerrun/fieldtable.go, internal/luahost/apple_icons_darwin_test.go, internal/luahost/apple_pbxproj_darwin_test.go. cmd/root.go's is a struct-field alignment gofmt wants collapsed (Use: "admin"), present since before 547b28d. The manifest declares build, deploy, prototype, tampermonkey, tampermonkey-status and test — no fmt and no vet — so nothing in the normal loop reports this and the drift accumulates. Fix: gofmt -w the six files, then add [commands.fmt] and [commands.vet] on the canonical group-2 slots (fmt priority 30, vet priority 20) so the next drift is caught.

title: Workflow queries only resolve against beads; a GitHub-tracked project has no resolver
description:
internal/kinds/workflowquery.go's ResolveQuery resolves over.query ("ready", "label:<name>")
against the beads tracker only. A project whose declared tracker is github has no query
resolver, so a query-sourced workflow cannot run there.

Noted in-code by admin-3rgp.26's worker (in workflowquery.go's doc comment) rather than
folded in under that ticket — correctly, since a GitHub resolver is network-backed and a
different shape of work.

This matters more now than it did: admin-3rgp.21 and .22 made `tracker` a DECLARED key, so
a project saying tracker = "github" is making an explicit statement the tool should honour
end to end. Today it silently has no workflow queries.

Decide: implement a gh-backed resolver, or make a query-sourced workflow on a non-beads
tracker fail loudly at `admin check` time rather than at dispatch — the same principle
admin-3rgp.50 established for unknown kinds.

title: rasterx, a new transitive dependency, has been unmaintained since 2022
description:

one deserves a decision you did not explicitly make.

- golang.org/x/image v0.36.0 — the Go team's own module. Fine.
- github.com/fyne-io/oksvg v0.2.0 — actively maintained fork, last release Sept 2025. Fine.
- github.com/srwiley/rasterx v0.0.0-20220730225603 — oksvg's own dependency, and it has
  NOT been touched since 2022.

All three clear the bar the epic set and the orchestrator verified independently: pure Go,
no cgo, CGO_ENABLED=0 builds clean, internal/luahost cross-compiles to linux and windows.

title: Herdr dispatch hard-errors when herdr is present but the split fails
description:

title: Should rust and launchd be kinds at all? (admin_lib/rust.py, admin_lib/launchd.py)
description:
Split out of admin-3rgp.15, which halted on this rather than guessing. Its finding, verified:

- catalog.go has no 'rust' or 'launchd' entry, and Python never had one either — kinds.py
  declares neither.
- interp.py's _CONFIG_GLOBALS carries a DEAD '_LAUNCHD_CONFIG' mapping that no factory reads.
- admin_lib/rust.py has zero call sites anywhere in the repo outside its own file.

So these are library modules with no kind contract — no manifest shape, no dispatch
behaviour, nothing observable to port against. Every other kind in .15 had a Python
contract to match, which is what its acceptance criteria checked.

NEEDS A DECISION before it can be implemented. Porting them means DESIGNING a new kind's
manifest schema and dispatch shape from nothing — architecture work of the same weight as
admin-3rgp.12's Apple kinds, not a straight port.

1. Design them as real kinds — decide the manifest shape for each, then port.
2. Port them as plain helper packages with no kind, callable from Lua bodies via the host
   API, matching what Python actually did (module code, never dispatched).
3. Drop them. rust.py has no callers and _LAUNCHD_CONFIG is already dead code; ADR-0010's
   deletion of the Python may make this moot. admin-3rgp.30 would remove both.

Option 3 deserves a real look before anyone builds anything: dead code with no callers is
cheaper to delete than to port.

description: docs/spikes/admin-tui-desktop TestTabSwitchesTabs fails intermittently with 'repo screen did not render' — measured 1 failure in 4 runs on the same commit (44c3bf0), and it passed in full-suite runs earlier the same session. It is a frame-settle deadline test, so the deadline is the suspect rather than the code under test. notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED 2026-08-31 by a swarm worker that HALTED rather than fix it in the
wrong package. No code change was made.

MEASUREMENT CORRECTION: this is not "1 run in 4". Under real concurrent load (load average
6.69-8.87, three sibling worktrees building and testing at once) the worker ran
TestTabSwitchesTabs in 20 separate fresh processes and got 20/20 FAIL, each at
key_test.go:75 "repo screen did not render", each taking 2.6-2.9s. The orchestrator's
earlier 1-in-4 figure came from an idle machine. It is load-dependent, not random.

deadline instead of a quiescence check on outstanding commands. The spike's Settle is
900ms (docs/spikes/admin-tui-desktop/variants.go:174); under contention the render exceeds
it. This is exactly what the epic's own amendment predicted: "Settle is a deadline, not a
quiescence check."

fires — is in internal/tui/frame.go, which is production code shared with cmd/root.go, not
in the spike. A sibling worker owned internal/tui that round. Every fix reachable from
inside the spike alone (retry-until-content, or widening Settle) is a symptom-guard, which
the brief forbade.

but the defective drain lives in production code and would survive that deletion.

title: Go detector project_name merge ignores an explicit clear
description:
internal/detect/detect.go:130 — Match.ProjectName merge diverges from Python.

admin_lib/detectors.py:80-81 overwrites project_name whenever a later matched detector's dict contains the key at all, even when the value is falsy. The Go guards with `if m.ProjectName != ""`, so a later detector explicitly clearing project_name leaves the earlier value standing.

The fix is a presence flag distinguishing "not set" from "set to empty", the same pattern internal/manifest already uses for its Has* fields on Command. A previous attempt (commit d546f84, reverted by 606edc4) implemented exactly that with a discriminating test and it was correct — reuse it.

SCOPE NARROWED. This ticket originally carried a second finding about detectApple's glob matching dot-prefixed basenames. THAT FINDING WAS WRONG and is now dropped. The parity harness disproves it: given a `.foo.xcworkspace` fixture, Python returns [apple] and the "fixed" Go returned [simple]. The original Go behaviour already matched Python. Do not reintroduce a dotfile filter.

Verifying this needs a working parity harness — see admin-3rgp.34. The harness currently self-skips when <repo>/.venv/bin/python is absent, which is why the reverted attempt reported PASS from a worktree that had no .venv. Either land .34 first or create the venv in the worktree before trusting a green run.
acceptance_criteria: A later detector setting project_name to an empty value clears it, matching admin_lib/detectors.py:80-81, covered by a test that fails against the current implementation. TestParityWithPythonDetectors actually runs (not skips) and passes.
notes:
Attempted and reverted (commits 4d9a437, reverted by 606edc4). Two things came out of it.

Fix 1 (project_name presence) is CORRECT and has a real discriminating test — a HasProjectName flag on Match, matching admin_lib/detectors.py:80-81. Reuse it.

Fix 2 (dotfile glob) is WRONG. The parity harness from admin-3rgp.5 disproves the premise: with a dot-prefixed .foo.xcworkspace fixture, Python returns [apple] and the "fixed" Go returns [simple]. The ORIGINAL Go behaviour matched Python. Drop this half of the ticket.

Why the worker reported PASS on a change that fails: internal/detect/detect_test.go:396 skips the whole Python parity check when <repo>/.venv/bin/python is absent, and no .venv existed in the worker's worktree. The harness self-skipped, so TestParityWithPythonDetectors never ran there. It ran in the primary checkout at land time and failed immediately.

That skip is a hole worth closing on its own — a parity harness that silently passes when it cannot run is worse than one that fails.

title: Open question: nudging a pty-hosted worker
description:
Open question, recorded rather than answered.

`shim.PromptAgent` addresses a herdr agent by name. A pty-hosted entry (`livework.Entry`
with `PTYID` set and `PaneID` empty) has no agent name — its pseudo-terminal is owned by
the dashboard process itself — so the sweep skips it. As hosted-pty dispatch grows, a
larger share of workers becomes unsupervisable.

Two candidate answers:

- The dashboard writes the nudge text straight to the pty master it already owns. No herdr
  round trip, but it is a keystroke injection rather than a message to the agent, and it
  depends on how `admin-3rgp.61` ends up draining that master.
- Pty-hosted workers are declared out of scope for supervision, and anything meant to be
  supervised is dispatched to a herdr pane.

Depends on where `admin-3rgp.61` lands. Decide after it does.

title: Open question: a worker hung while StateRunning is invisible
description:
Open question, recorded rather than answered. This is the accepted cost of the stuck
definition chosen in `admin-16ju.1`.

A worker spinning silently — an infinite loop, a network call that never returns, a model
turn that died mid-stream — stays `StateRunning` forever and never reaches `StateWaiting`,
so the sweep cannot see it. Everything the orchestrator supervises today is a worker that
politely announced it was blocked.

The candidate answer is output-silence detection: a `LastOutputAt` stamp alongside the
bounded ring buffer proposed in `admin-3rgp.61`, flagging an entry with no new output for
some interval. Two problems with it, both real:

- `.61` is unmerged WIP, and the ring buffer only exists for pty-hosted entries. A herdr
  pane's output never passes through this process, so half the registry stays invisible.
- A four-minute model turn and a dead process produce identical silence. Any threshold long
  enough to avoid interrupting real work is long enough to leave a hang sitting.

Deliberately not decided now. Resolve it or close it as won't-do; do not let it be
discovered later as a surprise.

title: Scope the orchestrator
description:
Interview and scope the orchestrator, then cut its real slate.

The Swarm registry gives a queryable state per worker. What reads that and acts on it without a
human is undesigned, and cannot be specified until four questions have answers:

1. **What counts as stuck?** Idle time, a pattern in the output, an explicit signal from the
   agent, or something else.
2. **What does a nudge send, and where?** A keystroke into the pane, a message to the agent, a
   restart.
3. **May it land work without a human?** And does that differ between a repo you own and one you
   contribute to.
4. **Where does it run?** Inside the TUI process, or as a daemon that outlives it.

Until those are answered, no acceptance criteria for "keeps them moving" can be written, which is
why this epic holds one bead instead of a slate.

Deliverable: the answers, and the tickets that follow from them.
design:
Interview answers (2026-08-31). All four questions resolved.

1. WHAT COUNTS AS STUCK — an entry that has been StateWaiting (herdr's
"blocked": the agent settled on a question or approval prompt) longer than a
threshold. Requires a new StateChangedAt field on livework.Entry, stamped in
Registry.SetState. Reads registry state only, so it works identically for
pane- and pty-hosted entries and does not gate on admin-3rgp.61.
Rejected: output-silence detection (gates on .61's ring buffer, sees only pty
entries, cannot tell a 4-minute model turn from a dead process); an explicit
agent-sent signal (the truly hung agent is the one that cannot send it).
Accepted cost: a worker spinning silently while StateRunning is invisible.

2. WHAT A NUDGE SENDS — one canned continuation message to the agent via a new
shim.PromptAgent(name, text) = `herdr agent prompt <name> <text>` with no
--wait, beside the existing PromptAndWait. Reaches the agent's real input
channel rather than typing keystrokes into a pane.
Rejected: reading the question first and answering it (needs .61 plus a herdr
pane-capture verb that does not exist, and puts a model call in the TUI
process); escalate-only (an alarm clock, not an orchestrator).
Restart is deliberately not a nudge — Registry.Retry is human-triggered and
restarting a worker that asked a question loses its work.
Accepted cost: it answers a question it never read.

3. MAY IT LAND — no, and ownership never enters this codebase. See
docs/adr/0017-the-orchestrator-never-lands-work.md. Taken as "for now" —
explicitly reversible.

4. WHERE IT RUNS — in the TUI process, on the existing 1s workTickCmd
(internal/tui/work.go:756). The bead's original "one process or two" framing
is stale: livework.Default is in-memory and process-scoped, so a daemon would
need a second registry rebuilt from herdr queries, and every pty-hosted entry
would be structurally invisible to it.
Accepted cost: close the dashboard and supervision stops.
acceptance_criteria:
- All four questions above have recorded answers.
- An ADR records any decision among them that is hard to reverse.
- A slate of implementable tickets exists in this epic.
notes: Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). NOT AFFECTED BY THE GO REWRITE — left as filed. This is the orchestrator interview (what counts as stuck, what a nudge sends, may it land work unattended, where it runs). title: Orchestrator logic
description:
The half of the Swarm feature that reads the live-work registry and acts on it without a
human: notice a worker that has stopped moving, and get it moving again.

Scoped by admin-16ju.1, whose design field records the four answers and the reasoning for
each. In short: a worker is stuck when it has been StateWaiting past a threshold; the
action is one canned continuation message to its agent; the orchestrator never lands work
(ADR-0017); and it runs inside the TUI process on the Work tab's existing tick.

Two costs of those answers are recorded as open questions rather than forced —
admin-16ju.7 (a worker hung while StateRunning is invisible) and admin-16ju.8 (a
pty-hosted worker has no agent name to prompt).
notes:
Go-rewrite triage (admin-3rgp landed). NOT AFFECTED BY THE GO REWRITE as filed. One input
did change, and admin-16ju.1 resolved it: the Swarm registry and the dashboard now live in
the same binary (internal/tui, internal/livework), so "inside the TUI process or a daemon
that outlives it" was never a choice between two existing processes. livework.Default is
in-memory and process-scoped, so a daemon would need a second registry rebuilt from herdr
queries and every pty-hosted entry would be invisible to it. Answered: inside the TUI
process.
